syllabus_content:
# Database Systems and Design
**[Semester/Quarter]**

## Course Description

This course provides a comprehensive introduction to database systems, covering both theoretical foundations and practical implementation skills essential for modern software development. Students will explore relational database design principles, SQL programming, database normalization, transaction management, and performance optimization techniques. The curriculum emphasizes hands-on experience with industry-standard database management systems including MySQL and PostgreSQL, while also introducing NoSQL databases like MongoDB for modern web applications. Through real-world projects, students will design and implement database solutions for business scenarios, learning to balance performance, security, and scalability requirements. The course integrates current industry practices including database security, backup strategies, and cloud database deployment. Students will work both individually and in teams to develop database-driven applications, preparing them for software engineering roles, data analyst positions, or advanced coursework in data science and distributed systems. By the end of the quarter, students will have built a portfolio demonstrating proficiency in database design, query optimization, and full-stack application development with database integration.

## Learning Objectives

Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

• Design normalized relational database schemas to solve complex business data management problems using entity-relationship modeling and normalization principles
• Implement advanced SQL queries and stored procedures through hands-on practice with MySQL and PostgreSQL database management systems
• Analyze database performance bottlenecks by examining query execution plans, indexing strategies, and transaction isolation levels
• Develop full-stack web applications using modern frameworks like Node.js or Django that integrate seamlessly with both relational and NoSQL databases

## Target Audience

Undergraduate computer science majors in their sophomore or junior year who have completed foundational programming courses and are pursuing careers in software engineering, web development, data analysis, or database administration. Ideal for students planning to work in technology companies, financial services, healthcare IT, or those considering graduate studies in data science or information systems.

## Weekly Schedule

### Week 1: Hash Tables and Database Fundamentals
**Topics:** Hash function design, collision resolution strategies, database system overview
- **Monday:** Hash Tables: Implementation and Collision Resolution Strategies
- **Wednesday:** Binary Number System Flashcard Memory Challenge (40 min activity)
- **Friday:** Database system architecture and storage fundamentals
- 
### Week 2: Relational Model and ER Design
**Topics:** Entity-relationship modeling, relational algebra, normalization principles
- **Monday:** Introduction to relational model and ER diagrams
- **Wednesday:** Entity-relationship design workshop
- **Friday:** Normalization theory (1NF, 2NF, 3NF, BCNF)
- - **Assessment:** Introduction to Programming Concepts and Python Basics Quiz (100 points) - Due Friday

### Week 3: SQL Fundamentals and Binary Search Trees
**Topics:** Basic SQL queries, data manipulation, tree structures for indexing
- **Monday:** Binary Search Trees: Implementation and Analysis
- **Wednesday:** SQL SELECT statements and basic operations
- **Friday:** Advanced SQL: JOINs and subqueries
- 
### Week 4: Advanced SQL and Query Optimization
**Topics:** Complex queries, stored procedures, query performance analysis
- **Monday:** Stored procedures and functions
- **Wednesday:** Analyzing Database Query Performance: Execution Plan Investigation (75 min activity)
- **Friday:** Query optimization techniques and indexing strategies
- 
### Week 5: Graph Algorithms and Database Indexing
**Topics:** Graph traversal algorithms, B-trees, index structures
- **Monday:** Graph Algorithms: Traversal and Shortest Path Solutions
- **Wednesday:** B-tree and B+ tree indexing structures
- **Friday:** Hash indexing and bitmap indexes
- - **Assessment:** Data Structures and Algorithm Analysis Practical Exam (100 points) - Friday

### Week 6: Transaction Management
**Topics:** ACID properties, concurrency control, recovery systems
- **Monday:** Transaction concepts and ACID properties
- **Wednesday:** Concurrency control and locking mechanisms
- **Friday:** Recovery and logging systems
- 
### Week 7: NoSQL Databases and Graph Systems
**Topics:** Document databases, MongoDB, graph databases, Neo4j
- **Monday:** Graph Algorithms: Shortest Path Problems
- **Wednesday:** NoSQL database models and MongoDB introduction
- **Friday:** Graph databases and Neo4j
- - **Assessment:** Distributed Systems Architecture Design Discussion (100 points) - Due Friday

### Week 8: Database Security and Performance
**Topics:** Security threats, access control, performance tuning
- **Monday:** Security Vulnerability Analysis in Real-World Web Application Code (120 min activity)
- **Wednesday:** Database security and access control
- **Friday:** Performance monitoring and tuning strategies
- 
### Week 9: Advanced Topics and Cloud Databases
**Topics:** Distributed databases, cloud deployment, backup strategies
- **Monday:** Algorithm Efficiency Analysis: Comparing Search Implementations (135 min activity)
- **Wednesday:** Distributed database concepts and CAP theorem
- **Friday:** Cloud database services (AWS RDS, Azure SQL, Google Cloud SQL)
- 
### Week 10: Final Projects and Review
**Topics:** Project presentations, course review, advanced applications
- **Monday:** Final project presentations
- **Wednesday:** Advanced database topics and industry trends
- **Friday:** Course review and exam preparation
- - **Assessment:** Distributed Hash Table Implementation and Performance Analysis Lab Report (100 points) - Due Wednesday

## Assessment Plan

| Assessment Type | Points | Percentage | Description |
|----------------|---------|------------|-------------|
| Quizzes | 100 | 15% | Programming concepts and database fundamentals |
| Practical Exam | 100 | 15% | Data structures, algorithms, and SQL implementation |
| Discussion Participation | 100 | 15% | Distributed systems architecture design |
| Lab Reports | 100 | 15% | Distributed hash table implementation project |
| Weekly Lab Assignments | 200 | 30% | Hands-on database implementation exercises |
| Final Project | 100 | 10% | Complete database-driven application |
| **Total** | **700** | **100%** | |

# COURSE SYLLABUS

**CS 598: Advanced Machine Learning Systems DesignComputer Science DepartmentGraduate Level | 4 Credits | [Semester/Quarter]**

---

## COURSE INFORMATION

**Meeting Time:** Monday/Wednesday/Friday 10:00-10:50 AM  
**Lab Sessions:** Wednesday 2:00-4:50 PM (Engineering Lab 205)  

**Prerequisites:** Completion of undergraduate algorithms and data structures course, proficiency in Python programming, foundational machine learning course (equivalent to CS 229), basic statistics and linear algebra, experience with version control systems (Git), and familiarity with Linux/Unix command line.  

**Recommended Background:** Prior coursework in distributed systems, databases, or software engineering, and hands-on experience with ML libraries such as scikit-learn, TensorFlow, or PyTorch.

---

## COURSE DESCRIPTION

This graduate-level course focuses on the design, implementation, and deployment of large-scale machine learning systems in production environments. Students will explore the complete ML pipeline from data ingestion and feature engineering to model training, validation, and deployment at scale. The course covers critical aspects of ML systems including distributed training, model versioning, continuous integration/deployment for ML (MLOps), monitoring and maintenance of production models, and handling real-world challenges such as data drift, model degradation, and scalability constraints. 

Through hands-on projects using industry-standard tools and frameworks, students will gain practical experience building robust, scalable ML systems that can handle enterprise-level workloads. Topics include microservices architecture for ML, containerization and orchestration, A/B testing for model validation, and ethical considerations in automated decision-making systems. This course bridges the gap between academic ML knowledge and industry practices, preparing students for roles as ML engineers, data scientists, or research engineers in technology companies.

## LEARNING OBJECTIVES

By the end of this course, students will be able to:

• **Design and implement** distributed machine learning pipelines to handle large-scale data processing and model training across multiple computing nodes  
• **Evaluate and deploy** ML models in production environments through containerization, API development, and cloud-based orchestration platforms  
• **Monitor and maintain** production ML systems by implementing automated testing, performance tracking, and model retraining workflows  
• **Optimize** ML system performance using distributed computing frameworks like Apache Spark, Kubernetes, and cloud-native ML platforms such as AWS SageMaker or Google AI Platform

---

## WEEKLY SCHEDULE

### **Week 1: Foundation - Algorithm Complexity Analysis and System ArchitectureModule:** Algorithm Complexity Analysis and Big O Notation  
*Mathematical notation describing algorithm growth rates, time complexity measurement, and space complexity analysis for ML pipeline optimization*

**Key Concepts:**
- Big O Notation for ML system scalability analysis
- Time Complexity in distributed training scenarios  
- Space Complexity in large-scale data processing

**Activities:**
- Advanced Algorithm Complexity Classification Memory Challenge (50 min) - memorize complexity notations for 25 ML algorithms
- 
**Deliverables:** Environment setup verification

---

### **Week 2: Data Structures for ML Systems - Hash Tables and Distributed StorageModule:** Hash Tables and Collision Resolution Strategies  
*Implementation of hash-based data structures critical for feature storage, caching, and distributed data management in ML systems*

**Key Concepts:**
- Hash Functions for distributed feature storage
- Load Factor optimization in ML data pipelines  
- Collision Resolution in high-throughput ML systems

**Activities:**
- Analyzing Memory Management Vulnerabilities in C++ Code (210 min) - examine memory-critical ML system components
- 
**Assessment:** Data Structures and Algorithm Analysis Quiz (100 points)

---

### **Week 3: Graph-Based ML Systems - Model Dependency and Workflow ManagementModule:** Graph Algorithms: Traversal and Shortest Path  
*Application of graph algorithms to ML pipeline orchestration, model dependency management, and optimal resource allocation*

**Key Concepts:**
- Breadth-First Search for ML pipeline dependency resolution
- Depth-First Search for model versioning and lineage tracking
- Dijkstra's Algorithm for optimal resource allocation across ML clusters

**Activities:**
- Distributed System Failure Analysis: CAP Theorem Trade-offs (150 min) - analyze ML system architectures
- 
**Project Milestone:** System architecture design document due

---

### **Week 4: Tree Structures in ML - Model Selection and Feature EngineeringModule:** Binary Search Trees: Implementation and Analysis  
*Hierarchical data structures for efficient model organization, hyperparameter optimization, and feature selection in ML systems*

**Key Concepts:**
- Binary Search Property for efficient model registry organization
- Tree Traversal Algorithms for systematic hyperparameter search
- Recursive Tree Operations for automated model selection pipelines

**Activities:**
- Comparative Analysis of Sorting Algorithm Performance (160 min) - optimize data preprocessing pipelines
- 
**Assessment:** Begin Distributed Database System Project (ongoing)

---

### **Week 5: Advanced Hashing - Feature Engineering and Model ServingModule:** Hash Tables: Implementation and Collision Resolution Strategies  
*Advanced hashing techniques for real-time feature computation, model serving optimization, and distributed caching in production ML systems*

**Key Concepts:**
- Hash Function design for ML feature engineering
- Load Factor management in production serving systems
- Separate Chaining for handling high-volume prediction requests

**Activities:**
- Algorithm Efficiency Analysis: Comparing Sorting Algorithms (115 min) - optimize real-time data processing
- 
**Assessment:** Portfolio development begins - Personal ML System Implementation

---

### **Week 6: Graph Networks - Advanced ML Pipeline OrchestrationModule:** Graph Algorithms: Shortest Path Problems  
*Complex graph algorithms for advanced ML system optimization, including multi-objective optimization and resource-constrained scheduling*

**Key Concepts:**
- Dijkstra's Algorithm for cost-optimal ML pipeline execution
- Bellman-Ford Algorithm for handling negative feedback in reinforcement learning systems
- Floyd-Warshall Algorithm for all-pairs optimization in distributed ML networks

**Activities:**
- Memory Palace: Complex Algorithm Time Complexities (90 min) - master advanced ML algorithm performance characteristics
- 
**Project Checkpoint:** Distributed system implementation progress review

---

### **Week 7: Performance Analysis - Production ML System OptimizationModule:** Algorithm Analysis and Big O Notation  
*Comprehensive performance analysis techniques for production ML systems, including capacity planning and scalability assessment*

**Key Concepts:**
- Big O Notation for production system capacity planning
- Time Complexity analysis for real-time ML inference
- Space Complexity optimization for memory-constrained deployments

**Activities:**
- Algorithm Efficiency Analysis: Sorting Algorithm Performance (110 min) - optimize batch processing systems
- 
**Assessment:** System optimization report due

---

### **Week 8: Advanced Data Management - ML Data Pipeline ArchitectureModule:** Hash Tables and Hash Functions: Implementation and Collision Resolution  
*Enterprise-grade data management systems for ML, including data versioning, lineage tracking, and consistency guarantees*

**Key Concepts:**
- Hash Function optimization for data deduplication and versioning
- Collision Resolution in high-throughput data ingestion systems
- Load Factor management for dynamic scaling of ML data pipelines

**Activities:**
- Advanced Data Structure Implementation Recall Challenge (90 min) - master complex ML system components
- 
**Assessment:** Distributed Database System Project Due (100 points)

---

### **Week 9: Final Integration - Complete ML System ArchitectureModule:** Graph Algorithms and System Integration  
*Integration of all components into a comprehensive, production-ready ML system with monitoring, alerting, and automated maintenance*

**Activities:**
- Programming Language Syntax Elements Memory Cards (70 min) - review deployment scripting fundamentals
- 
**Assessment:** System Architecture Design Presentation (100 points)

---

### **Week 10: Presentations and Portfolio CompletionFinal Project PresentationsPortfolio Submission and Peer ReviewAssessment:** Beginner Programming Portfolio: Personal Website with Interactive Features (100 points) - adapted as Advanced ML Systems Portfolio

---

## ASSESSMENT PLAN

| Assessment Type | Points | Percentage | Description |
|----------------|--------|------------|-------------|
| **Weekly Quizzes & Activities** | 200 | 20% | In-class activities and knowledge checks |
| **Data Structures Quiz** | 100 | 10% | Mid-term knowledge assessment |
| **Distributed Database Project** | 100 | 10% | Major implementation project |
| **System Architecture Presentation** | 100 | 10% | Design and presentation of ML system |
| **ML Systems Portfolio** | 100 | 10% | Comprehensive portfolio of implementations |
| **Lab Assignments** | 200 | 20% | Weekly hands-on implementations |
| **Final Project** | 200 | 20% | Complete production ML system |
| **TOTAL** | **1000** | **100%** | |

## REQUIRED MATERIALS

### **Textbooks**
- *Designing Machine Learning Systems* by Chip Huyen (Primary)
- *Building Machine Learning Pipelines* by Hannes Hapke & Catherine Nelson
- *Machine Learning Engineering* by Andriy Burkov

### **Software & Platforms**
- **Programming:** Python 3.8+, Docker, Kubernetes
- **ML Frameworks:** TensorFlow, PyTorch, Scikit-learn
- **Cloud Platforms:** AWS (SageMaker, EC2, S3), Google Cloud Platform
- **Tools:** Git, Apache Spark, Apache Airflow, MLflow
- **Development:** Linux/Unix environment, VS Code or PyCharm

### **Hardware Requirements**
- Computer capable of running virtual machines
- Minimum 16GB RAM recommended
- Cloud computing credits will be provided

---

## COURSE POLICIES

### **Attendance Policy**
Attendance is mandatory for all lectures and lab sessions. More than two unexcused absences may result in course failure. Lab sessions are critical for hands-on learning and cannot be made up easily.

### **Late Work Policy**
- **Assignments:** 10% penalty per day late, maximum 3 days
- **Projects:** 15% penalty per day late, no extensions beyond 2 days
- **Presentations:** Cannot be made up without documented emergency

### **Academic Integrity**
All work must be original. Collaboration is encouraged on lab exercises but discouraged on individual assignments. Proper citation is required for any external code or resources. Plagiarism will result in course failure.

### **Collaboration Guidelines**
- **Encouraged:** Discussing concepts, debugging help, study groups
- **Prohibited:** Sharing code solutions, copying implementations
- **Required:** Individual understanding and explanation of all submitted work

### **Technology Policy**
Laptops are required for in-class activities. Mobile phones should be silenced. Recording of lectures requires permission.

### **Accommodation Statement**
Students with documented disabilities should contact the Office of Disability Services to arrange reasonable accommodations. Please discuss any needed accommodations with the instructor within the first two weeks of class.

### **Communication**
- **Primary:** Course website and email announcements
- - **Emergency Contact:** Department office at (xxx) xxx-xxxx

syllabus_content:
# CS 7850: Advanced Machine Learning Systems and Scalability
**Department of Computer Science | Fall 2024 | 3 Credit Hours**

---

## Course Description

This graduate-level course explores the design, implementation, and deployment of machine learning systems at scale. Students will examine the complete ML pipeline from data ingestion to model serving, focusing on distributed computing frameworks, model optimization techniques, and production deployment strategies. The course covers advanced topics including federated learning, edge computing for ML, automated machine learning (AutoML), and MLOps practices. Students will work with industry-standard tools such as Apache Spark, TensorFlow Extended (TFX), Kubernetes, and cloud-based ML platforms. Through hands-on projects, students will design and implement scalable ML architectures that can handle real-world data volumes and traffic patterns. The course emphasizes both theoretical foundations and practical skills needed for ML engineering roles in industry. Topics include distributed training algorithms, model compression and quantization, A/B testing for ML systems, monitoring and observability, and ethical considerations in large-scale ML deployment. By the end of the course, students will have experience building end-to-end ML systems that can scale to millions of users while maintaining reliability, performance, and fairness standards required in production environments.

## Learning Objectives

Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

• Design distributed machine learning architectures to handle petabyte-scale datasets using Apache Spark and cloud computing platforms  
• Implement model optimization techniques through pruning, quantization, and knowledge distillation to reduce computational requirements by 80% or more  
• Develop automated ML pipelines by integrating continuous integration/continuous deployment (CI/CD) practices with model versioning and automated testing frameworks  
• Deploy production-ready ML systems using containerization technologies like Docker and Kubernetes with comprehensive monitoring and logging capabilities  

## Target Audience

Graduate students in Computer Science, Data Science, or related fields with strong programming backgrounds who are pursuing careers as ML engineers, research scientists, or technical leads in AI-driven companies. Ideal candidates are those seeking to transition from academic or small-scale ML projects to enterprise-level system design and implementation.

## Prerequisites

• Completion of undergraduate courses in data structures and algorithms, statistics, and linear algebra  
• Prior coursework in machine learning fundamentals (equivalent to CS 4/229 Machine Learning) with hands-on experience in Python, TensorFlow or PyTorch  
• Familiarity with software engineering principles, version control systems (Git), and basic understanding of distributed systems concepts  
• Students should have completed at least one significant ML project involving model training and evaluation  

---

### Software & Platforms
- Python 3.8+, TensorFlow 2.x, PyTorch 1.x
- Apache Spark, Docker, Kubernetes
- AWS/GCP/Azure account (student credits provided)
- GitHub account for version control
- Jupyter Notebook/Lab environment

## Weekly Schedule

### Week 1 (Aug 22-26): Course Introduction & ML Systems Overview
**Topics:** Course logistics, ML system architecture fundamentals, distributed computing primer  
**Activity:** Advanced Algorithms Flashcard Mastery Challenge: Complexity Classification and Properties (75 min)  
**Reading:** Ameisen Ch. 1-2  

### Week 2 (Aug 29 - Sep 2): Data Infrastructure and Storage Systems
**Topics:** Data lakes, data warehouses, streaming data architectures  
**Module:** Hash Tables and Hash Functions: Design, Implementation, and Analysis  
**Activity:** Analyzing Cache Performance: Memory Hierarchy Trade-offs (105 min)  
**Assignment:** Programming Paradigms Discussion (Due Sep 8)  

### Week 3 (Sep 5-9): Distributed Data Processing with Apache Spark
**Topics:** Spark architecture, RDDs, DataFrames, MLlib fundamentals  
**Module:** Binary Search Trees: Implementation and Analysis  
**Activity:** Binary Number System Flashcard Challenge (40 min)  
**Reading:** Kleppmann Ch. 10-11  

### Week 4 (Sep 12-16): Model Training at Scale
**Topics:** Distributed training, parameter servers, gradient aggregation  
**Module:** Graph Algorithms: Traversal and Shortest Path Solutions  
**Activity:** Deconstructing Algorithm Efficiency: Comparative Analysis (130 min)  

### Week 5 (Sep 19-23): Model Optimization and Compression
**Topics:** Pruning, quantization, knowledge distillation, model compression techniques  
**Module:** Hash Tables and Collision Resolution Strategies  
**Activity:** Algorithm Efficiency Analysis: Big O Notation Performance Breakdown (90 min)  
**Assessment:** Advanced Algorithms Design and Analysis Comprehensive Exam (Sep 23)  

### Week 6 (Sep 26-30): MLOps and Continuous Integration
**Topics:** CI/CD for ML, model versioning, automated testing  
**Module:** Binary Search Trees: Implementation and Analysis (Advanced)  
**Activity:** Operating System Process State Transition Memorization (75 min)  

### Week 7 (Oct 3-7): Container Orchestration and Kubernetes
**Topics:** Docker fundamentals, Kubernetes for ML workloads, scaling strategies  
**Module:** Hash Tables and Hash Functions: Implementation and Analysis  
**Activity:** Programming Language Syntax Flashcard Challenge (30 min)  

### Week 8 (Oct 10-14): Model Serving and API Design  
**Mid-term Break (Oct 10-11)Topics:** REST APIs, model serving patterns, load balancing  
**Module:** Graph Algorithms: Traversal and Shortest Path  
**Activity:** Analyzing Network Protocol Vulnerabilities (120 min)  

### Week 9 (Oct 17-21): Monitoring and Observability
**Topics:** Logging, metrics, alerting, performance monitoring for ML systems  
**Module:** Hash Tables and Collision Resolution Strategies (Advanced)  
**Activity:** Analyzing Memory Management Performance (90 min)  
**Project:** Personal Task Manager Application (Due Oct 21)  

### Week 10 (Oct 24-28): A/B Testing and Experimentation
**Topics:** Experimental design, statistical significance, feature flags  
**Activity:** Advanced Algorithm Time Complexity Classification Sprint (75 minutes)  
**Reading:** Ameisen Ch. 8-9  

### Week 11 (Oct 31 - Nov 4): Federated Learning and Edge Computing
**Topics:** Federated learning architectures, edge deployment, mobile ML  
**Module:** Hash Tables and Hash Functions: Design and Implementation  
**Activity:** Binary Number System Flashcard Recognition Challenge (25 min)  

### Week 12 (Nov 7-11): AutoML and Hyperparameter Optimization
**Topics:** Automated model selection, hyperparameter tuning, neural architecture search  
**Module:** Hash Tables and Collision Resolution Strategies (Final)  
**Activity:** Advanced Algorithms Complexity Classification Memory Challenge (75 min)  
**Assessment:** Distributed System Design and Implementation Lab Report (Due Nov 11)

### Week 14 (Nov 21-25): Industry Case Studies

# Database Systems and Applications
**Course Code:** CS 340 | **Credits:** 4 | **Quarter:** Fall 2024

---

## Course Description

This course provides a comprehensive introduction to database systems, focusing on relational database design, implementation, and management. Students will explore fundamental concepts including data modeling, normalization, SQL programming, transaction processing, and database administration. The course covers both theoretical foundations and practical applications, with hands-on experience using industry-standard database management systems such as MySQL, PostgreSQL, and Oracle. 

Students will learn to design efficient database schemas, write complex queries, optimize database performance, and understand security considerations. The curriculum includes real-world case studies from various industries, preparing students for database-related roles in software development, data analysis, and system administration. By the end of the course, students will have built a complete database-driven web application and gained experience with modern database technologies including NoSQL databases and cloud-based database services. 

This course is essential for students pursuing careers in software engineering, data science, web development, or any field requiring data management skills. The knowledge gained will directly support advanced coursework in data mining, machine learning, and distributed systems.

---

## Learning Objectives

Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

• Design normalized relational database schemas to solve real-world data storage problems using entity-relationship modeling and functional dependencies  
• Implement complex database queries and transactions through advanced SQL programming including joins, subqueries, stored procedures, and triggers  
• Optimize database performance by analyzing query execution plans, creating appropriate indexes, and implementing efficient data access patterns  
• Develop database-driven applications using modern web frameworks such as Django or Spring Boot with ORM technologies and RESTful API design

---

## Target Audience & Prerequisites

**Target Audience:** Second or third-year Computer Science undergraduates who have completed foundational programming courses and are interested in software development, data management, or web applications. Ideal for students planning careers as software engineers, database administrators, data analysts, or full-stack developers who need strong database skills for enterprise applications.

**Prerequisites:** 
- CS 162 (Data Structures and Algorithms)
- CS 170 (Introduction to Programming II with object-oriented concepts)  
- CS 225 (Discrete Mathematics)

Students should have proficiency in at least one programming language (preferably Java, Python, or C++), basic understanding of file systems and data structures, and familiarity with command-line interfaces.

---

## Weekly Schedule

### Week 1: Database Fundamentals and ER Modeling
**Module:** Introduction to Database Systems and Entity-Relationship Modeling  
**Topics:** Database concepts, DBMS architecture, entity-relationship diagrams, conceptual design  
**Activities:** 
- Programming Terminology Memory Card Match (40 min) - Database terminology focus
**Readings:** Chapter 1-2 (Silberschatz)  

### Week 2: Relational Model and Schema Design
**Module:** Relational Database Theory and Schema Implementation  
**Topics:** Relational algebra, functional dependencies, normalization (1NF, 2NF, 3NF, BCNF)  
**Activities:** 
- Binary Number System Flashcard Drill with Visual Patterns (45 min) - Applied to database indexing concepts
**Readings:** Chapter 3-4 (Silberschatz)  

### Week 3: SQL Fundamentals and Query Construction

**Topics:** SELECT statements, joins, subqueries, aggregate functions, grouping  
**Activities:** 
- Python Basic Syntax Identification Flash Card Challenge (45 min) - Adapted for SQL syntax
**Assessment:** Python Variables and Data Types Lab Report (100 points) - Database connection and basic queries
**Readings:** Chapter 5-6 (Silberschatz)  

### Week 4: Advanced SQL and Transaction Processing
**Module:** Advanced Query Techniques and ACID Properties  
**Topics:** Stored procedures, triggers, views, transaction management, concurrency control  
**Activities:** 
- Algorithm Efficiency Analysis: Comparing Search Implementation Performance (95 min) - Applied to query optimization
**Readings:** Chapter 7-8 (Silberschatz)  

### Week 5: Database Performance and Optimization
**Module:** Query Optimization and Index Design  
**Topics:** Query execution plans, indexing strategies, performance tuning, database statistics  
**Activities:** 
- Analyzing Database Query Performance Bottlenecks Through Execution Plan Decomposition (95 min)
**Assessment:** Advanced Algorithm Analysis and Design Quiz (100 points) - Query optimization focus
**Readings:** Chapter 9-10 (Silberschatz)  

### Week 6: Database Security and Administration
**Module:** Security, Backup, and Recovery  
**Topics:** User authentication, authorization, backup strategies, disaster recovery, data privacy  
**Activities:** 
- TCP/IP Stack Layer Function Memorization Challenge (55 min) - Applied to database networking
**Readings:** Chapter 11-12 (Silberschatz)  

### Week 7: Application Development and ORM
**Module:** Database-Driven Web Applications  
**Topics:** Object-relational mapping, Django ORM, RESTful APIs, web application architecture  
**Activities:** 
- Programming Language Syntax Flashcard Challenge (55 min) - Python/Django focus
**Assessment:** Database Design Trade-offs: Relational vs NoSQL Architecture Discussion (100 points)
**Readings:** Django documentation (selected chapters)  

### Week 8: NoSQL and Modern Database Technologies
**Module:** Non-Relational Database Systems  
**Topics:** Document databases (MongoDB), key-value stores, graph databases, cloud database services  
**Activities:** 
- Distributed System Failure Analysis: Dissecting the 2017 AWS S3 Outage (150 min)
**Readings:** Chapter 15-16 (Silberschatz)  

### Week 9: Data Warehousing and Analytics
**Module:** Big Data and Analytics Platforms  
**Topics:** Data warehousing concepts, OLAP vs OLTP, ETL processes, business intelligence  
**Activities:** 
- Algorithm Complexity Classification Memory Challenge (75 min) - Applied to data processing algorithms
**Readings:** Chapter 17-18 (Silberschatz)  

### Week 10: Final Project Presentations and Course Review

**Topics:** Distributed databases, emerging technologies, course review, final project presentations

# CS 3220: Database Systems and Design
**Spring 2024 | 3 Credit Hours**

---

## Course Description

This course provides a comprehensive introduction to database systems, covering both theoretical foundations and practical implementation skills essential for modern software development. Students will explore relational database design principles, SQL programming, transaction management, and database optimization techniques. The curriculum emphasizes hands-on experience with industry-standard database management systems including MySQL, PostgreSQL, and MongoDB. Through real-world projects, students will design and implement database solutions for various application domains, learning to balance performance, scalability, and data integrity requirements. The course covers emerging topics such as NoSQL databases, cloud database services, and big data fundamentals, preparing students for contemporary data management challenges. Students will develop proficiency in database modeling using Entity-Relationship diagrams, normalization techniques, and query optimization strategies. Additionally, the course addresses critical topics including database security, backup and recovery procedures, and ethical considerations in data management. Upon completion, students will possess the technical skills and theoretical understanding necessary for database-related roles in software engineering, data analysis, and system administration, while also being prepared for advanced coursework in data science and distributed systems.

---

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this course, students will be able to:

• **Design normalized relational database schemas** to solve complex business requirements using Entity-Relationship modeling and functional dependency analysis

• **Implement advanced SQL queries and stored procedures** through hands-on projects using MySQL and PostgreSQL database management systems

• **Evaluate database performance and reliability** by analyzing query execution plans, implementing indexing strategies, and designing backup recovery procedures

• **Develop full-stack database applications** using modern web frameworks such as Django or Node.js with both SQL and NoSQL database backends

---

## Target Audience & Prerequisites

**Target Audience:** Junior-level Computer Science majors who have completed core programming courses and are interested in software engineering, data management, or web development careers. Ideal for students planning to work as software developers, database administrators, or data analysts, as well as those preparing for advanced coursework in data science, machine learning, or distributed systems.

**Prerequisites:** 
- CS 2420 Data Structures and Algorithms (C- or better)
- CS 2100 Discrete Mathematics 
- CS 1410 Object-Oriented Programming

Students must demonstrate proficiency in at least one programming language (preferably Python or Java) and have basic understanding of software development principles, file systems, and command-line interfaces.

---

## Weekly Schedule

### Week 1 (Jan 15-19): Course Introduction & Database Fundamentals
**Topics:** Course overview, database concepts, DBMS architecture
**Activity:** *Database Query Performance Analysis: Comparing Index Strategies* (95 min)
**Due:** Software installation verification

### Week 2 (Jan 22-26): Data Modeling and ER Diagrams
**Topics:** Entity-relationship modeling, conceptual design
**Activity:** *Critical Analysis of Database Normalization Trade-offs in E-commerce System Design* (90 min)
**Due:** ER Diagram Practice Problems

### Week 3 (Jan 29-Feb 2): Relational Model and Normalization
**Topics:** Relational algebra, functional dependencies, normal forms
**Activity:** *Analyzing Database Query Performance: Identifying Bottlenecks in JOIN Operations* (120 min)

### Week 4 (Feb 5-9): SQL Fundamentals
**Topics:** Basic SQL queries, joins, subqueries
**Assessment:Advanced Algorithm Design and Complexity Analysis Quiz** (100 points)

### Week 5 (Feb 12-16): Advanced SQL Programming
**Topics:** Stored procedures, triggers, views

### Week 6 (Feb 19-23): Database Performance and Indexing
**Topics:** Index structures, query optimization
**Activity:** *Binary Number System Flashcard Memorization Challenge* (35 min)

### Week 7 (Feb 26-Mar 1): Hash Tables and Database Implementation
**Module:** *Hash Tables and Hash Functions: Implementation and Analysis*
**Key Concepts:**
- Hash Function: A deterministic function that maps keys of arbitrary size to fixed-size values
- Load Factor: The ratio of occupied slots to total slots in a hash table
- Collision Resolution: Techniques for handling multiple keys that hash to the same slot
**Activity:** *Advanced Data Structure Terminology and Classification Flashcard Challenge* (90 min)

### Week 8 (Mar 4-8): Midterm Exam Week
**Assessment:Advanced Data Structures and Algorithm Design Comprehensive Exam** (100 points)

### **Spring Break (Mar 11-15)**

### Week 9 (Mar 18-22): Binary Search Trees and Database Indexing
**Module:** *Binary Search Trees: Implementation and Analysis*
**Key Concepts:**
- BST Property: For every node, all values in left subtree are smaller and right subtree larger
- In-order Traversal: Recursive algorithm visiting nodes in sorted order
- Deletion Cases: Three scenarios for removing nodes with different approaches
**Activity:** *Python Data Types Memory Card Challenge* (45 min)

### Week 10 (Mar 25-29): Transaction Management
**Topics:** ACID properties, concurrency control, locking

### Week 11 (Apr 1-5): Database Recovery and Reliability
**Topics:** Backup strategies, recovery techniques, disaster planning
**Activity:** *Comparative Analysis of Cache Replacement Algorithms Through Memory Trace Simulation* (110 min)

### Week 12 (Apr 8-12): NoSQL Databases
**Topics:** MongoDB, document stores, key-value databases
**Assessment:Introduction to Programming Concepts Presentation** (100 points)

### Week 13 (Apr 15-19): Graph Algorithms for Database Applications
**Module:** *Graph Algorithms: Traversal and Shortest Path Solutions*
**Key Concepts:**
- Graph representation: adjacency lists vs matrices and their trade-offs
- Breadth-First Search (BFS): level-by-level traversal using queues
- Depth-First Search (DFS): exploration using stacks/recursion
**Activity:** *Distributed System Failure Analysis: Diagnosing Performance Bottlenecks in Microservices Architecture* (3 hours)

### Week 14 (Apr 22-26): Cloud Databases and Big Data
**Topics:** Database-as-a-Service, scalability, distributed systems
**Project Work:** Final project development

### Week 15 (Apr 29-May 3): Database Security and Ethics
**Topics:** Security threats, access control, privacy considerations
**Due:Personal Task Management System with REST API** (100 points)

### Finals Week (May 6-10)
**Assessment:Full-Stack Web Application Development Portfolio** (100 points)

---

## Assessment Plan

|-----------------|--------|--------|-------------|
| **Midterm Exam** | 100 | 20% | Advanced Data Structures and Algorithm Design Comprehensive Exam |
| **Final Portfolio** | 100 | 25% | Full-Stack Web Application Development Portfolio |
| **Major Project** | 100 | 20% | Personal Task Management System with REST API |
| **Quiz** | 100 | 10% | Advanced Algorithm Design and Complexity Analysis Quiz |
| **Presentation** | 100 | 10% | Introduction to Programming Concepts Presentation |
| **Lab Activities & Participation** | 100 | 10% | Weekly lab exercises and in-class activities |
| **Homework & Assignments** | 100 | 5% | Regular practice problems and readings |
| **Total** | **700** | **100%** | |

---

## COURSE INFORMATION

**Course Title:** Database Systems Design and Implementation  
**Course Code:** CS 325  
**Credits:** 4 Quarter Hours  
**Prerequisites:** CS 162 (Data Structures and Algorithms), CS 163 (Discrete Mathematics), and CS 201 (Object-Oriented Programming) with grades of C+ or better  

**Class Schedule:Teaching Assistant:** Michael Rodriguez ()  
**TA Office Hours:** Wednesdays 3:00-5:00 PM,   

---

## COURSE DESCRIPTION

This course provides comprehensive coverage of database system concepts, design principles, and implementation techniques essential for modern software development. Students will explore relational database theory, normalization, SQL programming, and transaction management while gaining hands-on experience with popular database management systems including MySQL and PostgreSQL. The curriculum emphasizes both theoretical foundations and practical applications, covering database design methodologies, query optimization, indexing strategies, and concurrent access control. Students will work on real-world projects involving database schema design, complex query development, and performance tuning. The course also introduces emerging topics such as NoSQL databases, distributed systems, and cloud-based database services. Upon completion, students will possess the skills necessary to design, implement, and maintain robust database systems for enterprise applications, web services, and data-driven applications.

---

## LEARNING OBJECTIVES

Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

• **Design normalized relational database schemas** to eliminate data redundancy and ensure data integrity for complex business applications  
• **Construct advanced SQL queries** through joins, subqueries, views, and stored procedures to extract meaningful information from multi-table databases  
• **Analyze query performance** by examining execution plans and implementing appropriate indexing strategies to optimize database operations  
• **Implement transaction management and concurrency control** using ACID properties and locking mechanisms in MySQL and PostgreSQL environments  

---

## TARGET AUDIENCE

This course is designed for junior and senior undergraduate Computer Science majors who have completed core programming courses and are preparing for software development careers, data engineering roles, or graduate studies requiring strong database fundamentals.

---

## REQUIRED MATERIALS

**Textbooks:**
- *Database System Concepts* (7th Edition) by Silberschatz, Korth, and Sudarshan
- *Learning SQL* (3rd Edition) by Alan Beaulieu

**Software:**
- MySQL Community Server 8.0+
- PostgreSQL 14+
- MySQL Workbench
- pgAdmin 4
- Access to university cloud computing resources

**Hardware Requirements:**
- Laptop with minimum 8GB RAM
- 50GB available storage space
- Reliable internet connection for cloud database access

---

### **Week 1: Foundation and Algorithm AnalysisTopics:** Course introduction, database fundamentals, algorithm complexity review  
**Module:** Algorithm Analysis and Big O Notation  
**Activities:**
- Algorithm Time Complexity Classification Memory Challenge (50 min)
- Programming Language Symbol Matching Challenge (40 min)
**Readings:** Textbook Chapter 1-2  

### **Week 2: Data Structures Review and Database ArchitectureTopics:** Review of fundamental data structures, database system architecture  
**Module:** Hash Tables and Collision Resolution Strategies  
**Activities:**
- Computer Hardware Component Identification (45 min)
- Programming Language Syntax Memory Match (50 min)
**Readings:** Textbook Chapter 3  
**Assessment:** Fundamentals of Programming Logic and Basic Algorithms Exam (Week 2)

### **Week 3: Relational Model and Tree StructuresTopics:** Relational algebra, relational calculus, tree-based indexing  
**Module:** Binary Search Trees: Implementation and Analysis  
**Activities:**
- Binary Number System Digit Card Recall Challenge (45 min)
**Readings:** Textbook Chapters 4-5  

### **Week 4: Advanced Data Structures and SQL FundamentalsTopics:** Advanced indexing structures, basic SQL operations  
**Module:** Hash Tables and Hash Functions: Implementation and Analysis  
**Activities:**
- Advanced Algorithm Complexity Classification Memory Challenge (50 min)
**Readings:** Textbook Chapter 6  

### **Week 5: Graph Theory in Database DesignTopics:** Entity-relationship modeling, schema design principles  
**Module:** Graph Algorithms: Traversal and Shortest Path  
**Activities:**
- Algorithm Performance Analysis: Comparing Sort Performance (120 min)
**Readings:** Textbook Chapter 7  
**Assessment:** Data Structures Implementation and Analysis Lab Report due

### **Week 6: Advanced Graph ApplicationsTopics:** Query optimization graphs, dependency analysis  
**Module:** Graph Algorithms: Breadth-First Search and Depth-First Search  
**Activities:**
- Algorithm Efficiency Analysis: Comparing Sort Performance (120 min)
**Readings:** Textbook Chapter 8  

### **Week 7: Performance Analysis and OptimizationTopics:** Query optimization, indexing strategies, performance tuning  
**Module:** Graph Algorithms: Search, Traversal, and Shortest Path  
**Activities:**
- Analyzing Time Complexity Trade-offs in Advanced Data Structure Implementations (130 min)
**Readings:** Textbook Chapters 9-10  

### **Week 8: Real-World System AnalysisTopics:** Transaction processing, concurrency control, ACID properties  
**Activities:**
- Critical Analysis of Database Query Optimization in E-commerce Transaction Systems (3 hours)
**Readings:** Textbook Chapters 11-12  
**Assessment:** Scalability Architecture Discussion: From Startup to Enterprise Scale

### **Week 9: Security and Distributed SystemsTopics:** Database security, distributed databases, NoSQL introduction  
**Activities:**
- Security Vulnerability Analysis in Web Authentication Systems (90 min)
- TCP/IP Protocol Stack Layer Functions and Headers Memorization Challenge (55 min)
**Readings:** Textbook Chapters 13-14  

### **Week 10: System Failures and RecoveryTopics:** Recovery systems, backup strategies, fault tolerance  
**Activities:**
- Distributed System Failure Analysis: Dissecting the 2017 GitLab Database Incident (140 min)
**Readings:** Textbook Chapter 15  

### **Week 11: Final Projects and Portfolio CompletionTopics:** Project presentations, course review, emerging technologies  
**Assessment:** Advanced Software Engineering Portfolio: Full-Stack Application Development due

The curriculum covers entity-relationship modeling, normalization theory, query optimization, transaction processing, and concurrent access control. Students will gain hands-on experience with popular database management systems including MySQL and PostgreSQL, learning to design efficient database schemas and write complex queries for real-world applications. The course emphasizes industry best practices for database security, backup and recovery procedures, and performance tuning. Through a combination of theoretical study and practical laboratory work, students will develop the skills necessary to design, implement, and maintain database systems in professional environments. This course serves as essential preparation for careers in software development, data analysis, system administration, and database administration. Students will complete a capstone project involving the design and implementation of a complete database application, demonstrating their ability to apply course concepts to solve practical business problems.

### Target Audience
Undergraduate computer science majors in their sophomore or junior year who have completed introductory programming courses and are interested in pursuing careers in software development, data management, or system administration. This course is ideal for students planning to work in enterprise environments, web development, or data-driven applications where database knowledge is essential.

---

## LEARNING OBJECTIVES

By the end of this course, students will be able to:

• Design normalized relational database schemas to eliminate data redundancy and ensure data integrity for complex business applications  
• Construct advanced SQL queries through joins, subqueries, and aggregate functions to extract meaningful information from multi-table databases  
• Implement database security measures by configuring user permissions, access controls, and data encryption protocols  
• Optimize database performance using indexing strategies, query execution plans, and database tuning tools in MySQL and PostgreSQL environments

---

# Database Systems and Design
**CS 245 | 4 Credits | [Semester/Quarter]**

---

## Course Description

This course provides a comprehensive introduction to database systems, covering both theoretical foundations and practical implementation skills essential for modern software development. Students will explore relational database design principles, SQL programming, transaction management, and database optimization techniques. The curriculum emphasizes hands-on experience with popular database management systems including MySQL and PostgreSQL, while also introducing NoSQL alternatives like MongoDB. Through a combination of theoretical lectures, laboratory exercises, and a capstone project, students will develop the skills necessary to design, implement, and maintain robust database solutions for real-world applications. Topics include entity-relationship modeling, normalization theory, indexing strategies, query optimization, concurrency control, and database security. Students will also examine emerging trends in database technology, including distributed databases, cloud database services, and big data processing frameworks. This course serves as a critical foundation for careers in software engineering, data analysis, web development, and systems administration, providing the database expertise that is highly valued across the technology industry.

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this course, students will be able to:

• Design normalized relational database schemas to effectively model complex business requirements and eliminate data redundancy  
• Construct advanced SQL queries through hands-on practice with joins, subqueries, stored procedures, and performance optimization techniques  
• Analyze database performance bottlenecks by implementing indexing strategies and query optimization methods in MySQL and PostgreSQL environments  
• Develop a full-stack web application using Node.js and React that demonstrates proper database integration, transaction handling, and security best practices  

## Prerequisites

- CS 142 (Data Structures and Algorithms) with grade of C+ or better
- CS 106 (Object-Oriented Programming in Java or Python)
- CS 163 (Discrete Mathematics for Computer Science)
- Proficiency in at least one programming language (Java, Python, or JavaScript preferred)
- Basic understanding of algorithmic complexity analysis

### Software & Accounts
- MySQL Community Server 8.0+ (free download)
- PostgreSQL 14+ (free download)
- MongoDB Community Edition (free download)
- Node.js 18+ and npm
- Visual Studio Code or preferred IDE
- Access to university cloud computing resources (provided)

## Weekly Schedule

### Week 1: Introduction to Database Systems and Hash Table Fundamentals
**Lectures:** Database concepts, DBMS architecture, data models overview  
**Module Focus:** Hash Tables and Collision Resolution Strategies - Understanding hash functions as foundation for database indexing, load factors, and separate chaining collision resolution methods that underpin database hash indexes  
**Learning Activity:** Binary Number System Flashcard Memory Drill (30 min) - Essential for understanding database storage and indexing mechanisms  
**Key Concepts:**  
- Hash Function: Mathematical function that maps data of arbitrary size to fixed-size values, determining where elements are stored in the hash table
- Collision Resolution: Techniques for handling situations where multiple keys hash to the same index, including chaining and open addressing methods
- Load Factor: Ratio of number of elements to table size, critical metric affecting performance and determining when table resizing is necessary

### Week 2: Relational Model and Entity-Relationship Design
**Lectures:** Relational model theory, ER diagrams, conceptual design  
**Learning Activity:** Database Schema Vulnerability Analysis and Optimization (90 min) - Examine e-commerce database schema for performance bottlenecks and security vulnerabilities  
**Reading:** Chapters 2-3 in primary textbook  
**Assignment:** ER Diagram Design (Due Week 3)

### Week 3: Normalization and Schema Design
**Lectures:** Functional dependencies, 1NF through BCNF, design guidelines  
**Module Focus:** Binary Search Trees: Implementation and Analysis - Understanding tree structures that form the basis for database B-trees and indexing strategies  
**Key Concepts:**  
- Binary Search Property: The fundamental ordering rule where left subtree values are less than parent node, and right subtree values are greater than parent node
- Tree Traversal Algorithms: Systematic methods for visiting nodes including in-order (sorted output), pre-order (structural replication), and post-order (bottom-up processing)
- BST Operations Complexity: Time complexity analysis showing O(log n) average case and O(n) worst case for search, insertion, and deletion operations

### Week 4: SQL Fundamentals and Basic Queries
**Lectures:** SQL syntax, SELECT statements, filtering, sorting  
**Learning Activity:** Binary Number System Flashcard Drill and Recall Challenge (45 min) - Reinforcement of binary concepts crucial for database storage understanding  
**Reading:** Chapters 4-5 in primary textbook  
**Assessment:Programming Fundamentals Portfolio: From Concepts to Code** assigned (Due Week 7)

### Week 5: Advanced SQL and Complex Queries
**Lectures:** Joins, subqueries, aggregation, window functions  
**Module Focus:** Graph Algorithms: Traversal and Shortest Path - Understanding graph traversal algorithms that apply to database query optimization and relationship navigation  
**Key Concepts:**  
- Breadth-First Search (BFS): Level-by-level graph traversal using queues, optimal for finding shortest unweighted paths
- Depth-First Search (DFS): Recursive graph exploration using stacks, ideal for detecting cycles and topological sorting
- Dijkstra's Algorithm: Greedy approach for finding shortest paths in weighted graphs with non-negative edges  
**Assessment:Data Structures and Algorithm Analysis Practical Exam** (100 points)

### Week 6: Database Programming and Stored Procedures
**Lectures:** Stored procedures, functions, triggers, cursors  
**Learning Activity:** Algorithm Performance Analysis: Time Complexity Investigation of Sorting Algorithms (3 hours) - Analyze sorting algorithms to understand query optimization principles  
**Reading:** Chapter 6 in primary textbook

### Week 7: Indexing and Physical Database Design
**Lectures:** B-trees, hash indexes, bitmap indexes, index selection strategies  
**Learning Activity:** Comparative Analysis of Sorting Algorithm Performance Under Varying Data Conditions (150 min) - Understanding how different data patterns affect database performance  
**Assessment:** Portfolio submission due

### Week 8: Query Optimization and Performance Tuning
**Lectures:** Query execution plans, optimization techniques, statistics  
**Module Focus:** Hash Tables: Implementation and Collision Resolution Strategies (Advanced) - Deep dive into hash table optimization techniques used in database hash joins and indexing  
**Key Concepts:**  
- Hash Function: A mathematical function that maps keys of arbitrary size to fixed-size hash codes, ideally distributing keys uniformly across the hash table array
- Load Factor: The ratio of occupied slots to total slots in a hash table (n/m), critically affecting performance and collision probability
- Separate Chaining: A collision resolution method using linked lists or dynamic arrays at each hash table index to store multiple key-value pairs

### Week 9: Transaction Management and Concurrency Control
**Lectures:** ACID properties, locking, deadlock detection, isolation levels  
**Learning Activity:** Distributed System Bottleneck Analysis: Decomposing a Microservices Architecture Performance Crisis (3 hours) - Understanding distributed database challenges  
**Reading:** Chapters 14-15 in primary textbook

### Week 10: NoSQL Databases and Modern Alternatives
**Lectures:** Document stores, key-value stores, MongoDB introduction  
**Assessment:Distributed Web Crawler System with Real-Time Analytics** project assigned (Due Finals Week)  
**Learning Activity:** Network Protocol Stack Memory Palace: TCP/IP Layer Recall Challenge (50 min) - Understanding network fundamentals for distributed databases

### Finals Week: Project Presentations and Final Assessment
**Assessment:Distributed System Architecture Design and Implementation Presentation** (100 points)  
**Project Due:** Complete web crawler system with documentation

---

## Assessment Plan

| Assessment Type | Points | Percentage | Due Date |
|----------------|--------|------------|----------|
| **Data Structures and Algorithm Analysis Practical Exam** | 100 | 20% | Week 5 |
| **Programming Fundamentals Portfolio** | 100 | 20% | Week 7 |
| **Distributed Web Crawler System Project** | 100 | 25% | Finals Week |
| **Final Presentation** | 100 | 25% | Finals Week |
| **Lab Assignments & Participation** | 50 | 10% | Ongoing |
| **Total** | **450** | **100%** | |

### Assessment Details

**Data Structures and Algorithm Analysis Practical Exam (100 points, Week 5):**  
Students will demonstrate understanding of fundamental data structures by implementing solutions to computational problems, analyzing time/space complexity, and explaining design decisions through both code implementation and written analysis. Focus on arrays, linked lists, stacks, queues, trees, and hash tables as they relate to database implementation.

**Programming Fundamentals Portfolio (100 points, Week 7):**  
A comprehensive portfolio showcasing understanding of basic programming concepts through four database-related projects: a simple database query tool, a data validation system, a basic indexing simulator, and a personal reflection on database design principles.

**Distributed Web Crawler System Project (100 points, Finals Week):**  
Design and implement a scalable, distributed web crawler system with real-time analytics dashboard. System must demonstrate proper database integration, concurrent crawling, data storage optimization, error handling, and meaningful content insights. Technologies: Node.js, React, MySQL/PostgreSQL, and cloud deployment.

**Final Presentation (100 points, Finals Week):**  
Present the distributed system project demonstrating deep understanding of database principles, architectural trade-offs, and implementation considerations. 15-minute presentation followed by Q&A session covering system design, scalability decisions, and performance optimization strategies.

---

## Additional Resources

### Online Resources
- **MySQL Documentation:** https://dev.mysql.com/doc/
- **PostgreSQL Documentation:** https://www.postgresql.org/docs/
- **Course GitHub Repository:** [To be provided Week 1]
- **Practice SQL Platform:** SQLBolt, W3Schools SQL Tutorial

### Tutoring Services
- CS Help Center: Monday-Friday, 9 AM-5 PM
- Peer tutoring available through Academic Success Center
- Study groups encouraged; contact TA for coordination

### Career Connections
This course prepares students for:
- Software Engineering Internships
- Database Administrator roles
- Full-Stack Web Development positions
- Data Analyst and Data Engineer careers
- Graduate studies in Computer Science

# Database Systems and Design
**CS 350 - Fall 2024**

---

## Course Description

This course provides a comprehensive introduction to database systems, covering fundamental concepts of data modeling, relational database design, and database management systems (DBMS). Students will learn to design efficient database schemas, write complex SQL queries, and understand the internal workings of modern database systems including storage, indexing, and transaction processing. The curriculum emphasizes both theoretical foundations and practical implementation, preparing students to work with enterprise-level database systems commonly used in software development, data analytics, and web applications. Students will gain hands-on experience with popular database platforms such as MySQL, PostgreSQL, and MongoDB, while exploring emerging trends in distributed databases and NoSQL systems. This course is essential for students pursuing careers in software engineering, data science, web development, or systems administration, as database knowledge is fundamental to virtually all modern computing applications. Upon completion, students will be equipped to design, implement, and optimize database solutions for real-world business problems.

---

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this course, students will be able to:

• **Design normalized relational database schemas** to efficiently store and organize complex business data structures  
• **Construct advanced SQL queries** including joins, subqueries, and aggregations through hands-on practice with real datasets  
• **Evaluate database performance and implement optimization strategies** by analyzing query execution plans and indexing approaches  
• **Implement database applications** using modern web frameworks such as Django or Node.js with ORM integration  

---

## Target Audience

Second or third-year Computer Science undergraduate students who have completed foundational programming courses and are interested in backend development, data management, or full-stack web development. Ideal for students planning careers in software engineering, data analytics, web development, or graduate studies in computer science.

---

## Weekly Schedule

### Week 1: Introduction to Database Systems
**Key Concepts:**
- Database system architecture and components
- Data models and database design lifecycle
- Introduction to relational model fundamentals

**Activities:**
- **Python Data Types Memory Card Matching Activity** (45 min) - Students will memorize and identify the six basic Python data types through structured card matching exercises
- Introduction to MySQL installation and setup

**Assignments Due:** None (first week)

---

### Week 2: Entity-Relationship Modeling
**Key Concepts:**
- Entity-relationship diagrams and notation
- Cardinality constraints and relationship types
- Weak entities and identifying relationships

**Activities:**
- **Python Data Type Memory Palace Challenge** (70 min) - Advanced memorization of Python data types with syntax examples using flashcard creation and peer testing
- ER diagram design workshop

**Assignments Due:** Database Software Installation Verification

---

### Week 3: Relational Model and Normalization
**Key Concepts:**
- Relational algebra operations
- Functional dependencies and normal forms
- First, second, and third normal forms

**Activities:**
- Normalization practice with real-world scenarios
- Schema design critique session

**Assignments Due:** ER Modeling Assignment

---

### Week 4: SQL Fundamentals
**Key Concepts:**
- Basic SQL syntax and data definition language (DDL)
- Data manipulation language (DML) operations
- Constraints and referential integrity

**Activities:**
- Hands-on SQL query writing lab
- Database creation and population exercise

**Assessment:Data Structures and Algorithm Analysis Quiz** (100 points) - Comprehensive quiz on fundamental database concepts and SQL basics

---

### Week 5: Advanced SQL Queries
**Key Concepts:**
- Complex joins and subqueries
- Aggregate functions and GROUP BY operations
- Window functions and common table expressions

**Activities:**
- **Database Query Performance Analysis** (85 min) - Students analyze SQL execution plans and identify bottlenecks in e-commerce transaction queries
- Advanced query optimization lab

**Assignments Due:** SQL Fundamentals Lab Report

---

### Week 6: Database Design and Implementation
**Key Concepts:**
- Physical database design considerations
- Index structures and B-tree organization
- Storage management and buffer pools

**Activities:**
- Index design and performance testing
- Physical schema optimization workshop

**Assessment:Database Design Discussion Forum** (100 points) - Structured discussion on normalization vs. denormalization trade-offs

---

### Week 7: Transaction Processing
**Key Concepts:**
- ACID properties and transaction management
- Concurrency control mechanisms
- Deadlock detection and prevention

**Activities:**
- Transaction isolation level experiments
- Concurrency simulation exercises

**Assignments Due:** Database Design Project (Phase 1)

---

### Week 8: Database Performance and Optimization
**Key Concepts:**
- Query execution plans and optimization
- Index selection and maintenance
- Database tuning methodologies

**Activities:**
- **Database Schema Vulnerability Analysis** (90 min) - Systematic identification of security flaws in e-commerce database systems
- Performance benchmarking lab

**Assessment:Midterm Exam** (100 points) - Comprehensive examination covering database design, SQL, and optimization

---

### Week 9: NoSQL Databases and MongoDB
**Key Concepts:**
- Document-oriented database concepts
- MongoDB architecture and data modeling
- CRUD operations in MongoDB

**Activities:**
- **Advanced Data Structure and Algorithm Complexity Memorization Challenge** (90 min) - Intensive recall of Big O notation for 25 advanced algorithms
- MongoDB hands-on workshop

**Assignments Due:** Database Performance Analysis Report

---

### Week 10: Distributed Databases
**Key Concepts:**
- Distributed database architecture
- Data fragmentation and replication strategies
- Consistency models and CAP theorem

**Activities:**
- **Distributed System Architecture Performance Bottleneck Analysis** (120 min) - Analysis of microservices architecture performance degradation
- Sharding and replica set configuration

**Assessment:NoSQL Implementation Lab Report** (100 points)

---

### Week 11: Web Application Integration
**Key Concepts:**
- Object-relational mapping (ORM) frameworks
- Database connectivity patterns
- Connection pooling and performance considerations

**Activities:**
- Django ORM hands-on development
- RESTful API design with database backend

**Assignments Due:** MongoDB Project Implementation

---

### Week 12: Database Security and Administration
**Key Concepts:**
- Access control and authentication mechanisms
- SQL injection prevention techniques
- Backup and recovery strategies

**Activities:**
- **Advanced Computer Architecture Component Identification** (45 min) - Recall of database server hardware optimization concepts
- Security audit simulation

**Assessment:Programming Paradigms Discussion** (100 points) - Analysis of ORM vs. direct SQL approaches

---

### Week 13: Advanced Topics and Emerging Trends
**Key Concepts:**
- Big Data and analytical databases
- Graph databases and Neo4j introduction
- Cloud database services overview

**Activities:**

Quarter System | Fall 2024

**Teaching Assistant:** [TA Name] ([PLACEHOLDER])  
**TA Office Hours:** Mondays & Wednesdays 3:00-5:00 PM

## COURSE DESCRIPTION

This graduate-level course focuses on the engineering and architectural aspects of deploying machine learning systems at scale. Students will explore the complete lifecycle of ML systems, from data pipeline design and model training infrastructure to deployment, monitoring, and maintenance in production environments. The course bridges the gap between theoretical machine learning knowledge and practical implementation challenges faced in industry settings. 

Topics include distributed training frameworks, model serving architectures, MLOps practices, data versioning, experiment tracking, A/B testing for ML models, and system reliability considerations. Students will work with cloud platforms, containerization technologies, and modern ML infrastructure tools while developing a comprehensive understanding of performance optimization, scalability, and security in ML systems. 

This course is essential for students pursuing careers as ML engineers, data scientists in production environments, or research scientists working on large-scale systems. By the end of the quarter, students will have hands-on experience building end-to-end ML pipelines and the theoretical foundation to make informed architectural decisions for complex machine learning applications in real-world scenarios.

---

## LEARNING OBJECTIVES

Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

• **Design and implement scalable ML data pipelines** to handle large-volume, multi-source data streams for production machine learning applications

• **Evaluate and deploy distributed training frameworks** through hands-on projects using TensorFlow, PyTorch, and cloud-based ML platforms

• **Analyze system performance bottlenecks and optimize ML inference systems** by implementing caching strategies, model compression, and load balancing techniques

• **Construct comprehensive MLOps workflows** using Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD pipelines, and monitoring tools like MLflow and Weights & Biases

---

## TARGET AUDIENCE & PREREQUISITES

**Target Audience:** Graduate students in Computer Science, Data Science, or related fields who have completed foundational machine learning coursework and seek to specialize in production ML systems. Ideal for students with 1-2 years of programming experience who are targeting careers as ML engineers, senior data scientists, or research engineers at technology companies, startups, or research institutions.

**Prerequisites:**
- Completion of undergraduate machine learning course (CS 229 or equivalent)
- Proficiency in Python programming
- Basic knowledge of linear algebra and statistics
- Familiarity with at least one deep learning framework (TensorFlow or PyTorch)
- Introductory experience with cloud computing platforms (AWS, GCP, or Azure)
- Completion of data structures and algorithms coursework

## WEEKLY SCHEDULE

### **Week 1: Hash Tables and Hash Functions for ML SystemsModule:** Hash Tables and Hash Functions: Implementation and Performance Analysis

**Key Concepts:**
- Hash Function: Mathematical function that maps keys of arbitrary size to fixed-size values (hash codes) with uniform distribution properties
- Collision Resolution: Techniques for handling situations when different keys produce the same hash value, including chaining and open addressing methods
- Load Factor: Ratio of stored elements to hash table size that directly impacts performance and determines when table resizing is necessary

**Learning Objectives:**
- Students will implement multiple hash table variants (separate chaining and open addressing) by coding complete data structures with insert, search, and delete operations in Python or Java
- Students will analyze hash function quality and collision patterns through empirical testing of different hash functions on various data sets

**Activities:**
- **Memory Palace: Recalling TCP/IP Protocol Stack Layer Functions and Port Numbers** (75 minutes) - Understanding network fundamentals for distributed ML systems
- **Python Data Types Memory Palace Challenge** (38 minutes) - Reinforcing Python fundamentals for ML development

---

### **Week 2: Binary Search Trees for Model Storage and IndexingModule:** Binary Search Trees: Implementation and Analysis

**Key Concepts:**
- Binary Search Property - left subtree contains values less than parent, right subtree contains values greater than parent
- In-order Traversal - visiting nodes in sorted order by recursively processing left subtree, current node, then right subtree
- Tree Rotation - restructuring operations that maintain BST property while improving balance

**Learning Objectives:**
- Students will implement insert, search, and delete operations for BSTs by writing recursive and iterative algorithms in Python or Java
- Students will analyze time and space complexity of BST operations through mathematical proof and empirical testing with various input distributions

**Activities:**
- **Binary Number System Flashcard Drill and Recognition Challenge** (45 minutes) - Building foundational computational thinking
- **Python Data Type Identification Challenge** (35 minutes) - Strengthening programming fundamentals

---

### **Week 3: Advanced Tree Structures for ML Model ManagementModule:** Advanced Binary Trees: AVL Trees and Balancing Algorithms

**Key Concepts:**
- Balance Factor: Integer value (-1, 0, +1) representing height difference between left and right subtrees
- Single Rotation: Fundamental restructuring operation that corrects simple imbalances through one pivot movement
- Double Rotation: Complex balancing operation combining two single rotations to fix inside-heavy imbalances

**Learning Objectives:**
- Students will implement complete AVL tree insertion and deletion algorithms by coding rotation functions and balance factor maintenance
- Students will analyze tree balance and height properties through mathematical proofs demonstrating O(log n) height guarantees

**Activities:**
- **Algorithm Efficiency Analysis: Comparing Sorting Algorithms Through Complexity Breakdown** (100 minutes)
- **Programming Language Syntax Recall Challenge** (45 minutes)

**Assessment:**
- **Advanced Algorithm Design and Complexity Analysis Quiz** (100 points) - Due Week 3 Friday

---

### **Week 4: Graph Algorithms for ML Pipeline DependenciesModule:** Graph Algorithms: Breadth-First Search and Depth-First Search

**Key Concepts:**
- Breadth-First Search (BFS): Algorithm that explores vertices level by level using a queue, guaranteeing shortest path in unweighted graphs
- Depth-First Search (DFS): Algorithm that explores as far as possible along each branch using a stack or recursion before backtracking
- Graph representation: Methods of storing graphs in memory including adjacency lists and adjacency matrices with trade-offs for different operations

**Learning Objectives:**
- Students will implement both BFS and DFS algorithms from scratch by writing complete Python functions that traverse adjacency list representations of graphs
- Students will analyze time and space complexity of graph traversal algorithms through mathematical proofs and empirical testing with graphs of varying sizes

**Activities:**
- **Analyzing Concurrency Bugs in Multi-threaded Banking System Code** (75 minutes)
- **Security Vulnerability Analysis of Web Authentication Systems** (90 minutes)

---

### **Week 5: Shortest Path Algorithms for Resource OptimizationModule:** Graph Algorithms: Shortest Path Problems

**Key Concepts:**
- Dijkstra's Algorithm - Greedy approach finding shortest paths from single source in weighted graphs with non-negative edges using priority queues
- Bellman-Ford Algorithm - Dynamic programming solution detecting negative cycles while computing shortest paths from single source in O(VE) time
- Floyd-Warshall Algorithm - All-pairs shortest path solution using dynamic programming with O(V³) complexity for dense graphs

**Learning Objectives:**
- Students will implement Dijkstra's, Bellman-Ford, and Floyd-Warshall algorithms in Python by writing complete, tested code solutions for each algorithm
- Students will analyze time and space complexity of shortest path algorithms through mathematical proof techniques and empirical testing with datasets of varying sizes

**Activities:**
- **Distributed System Architecture Analysis: Decomposing Netflix's Microservices Fault Tolerance Patterns** (3 hours)

**Assessment:**
- **Database Design Trade-offs: Relational vs. NoSQL Implementation Discussion** begins (ongoing through Week 6)

---

### **Week 6: Advanced Data Structures for High-Performance ML SystemsModule:** Hash Tables and Collision Resolution Strategies

**Key Concepts:**
- Hash Function: Mathematical function that maps keys to array indices, ideally distributing keys uniformly across the hash table
- Load Factor: Ratio of occupied slots to total table size, critical for maintaining performance and determining when to resize
- Collision Resolution: Techniques to handle multiple keys mapping to the same index, including chaining and open addressing methods

**Learning Objectives:**
- Students will implement hash tables with at least three different collision resolution strategies by coding complete data structures in Python or Java
- Students will analyze time and space complexity of various hashing approaches through mathematical analysis and empirical testing of their implementations

**Activities:**
- **Analyzing Time and Space Complexity Trade-offs in Advanced Data Structure Implementations** (120 minutes)
- **SQL Query Performance Analysis and Optimization Workshop** (100 minutes)

**Assessment:**
- **Database Design Trade-offs Discussion** continues (100 points)

---

### **Week 7: Graph Algorithms for Distributed ML SystemsModule:** Graph Algorithms: Traversal and Shortest Path

**Key Concepts:**
- Graph Representation: Methods for storing graphs in memory including adjacency matrices, adjacency lists, and edge lists with trade-offs analysis
- Breadth-First Search (BFS): Level-by-level graph traversal using queues, with applications in shortest unweighted paths and connected components
- Depth-First Search (DFS): Recursive and iterative graph exploration using stacks, essential for topological sorting and cycle detection

**Learning Objectives:**
- Students will implement BFS and DFS traversal algorithms by writing complete Python functions that handle both adjacency list and matrix representations
- Students will analyze shortest path problems through hands-on coding of Dijkstra's and Bellman-Ford algorithms using priority queues and dynamic programming techniques

**Activities:**
- **Advanced Algorithm Complexity Classification Memory Challenge** (60 minutes)
- **Distributed System Failure Point Analysis: Dissecting a Real-World Microservices Architecture** (3.5 hours)

---

### **Week 8: Advanced Memory Management and Performance OptimizationModule:** Hash Tables and Collision Resolution Strategies (Advanced Applications)

**Key Concepts:**
- Hash Function - A mathematical function that maps keys to array indices, ideally distributing keys uniformly across the hash table
- Load Factor - The ratio of occupied slots to total table size, critical for maintaining O(1) average-case performance
- Chaining - Collision resolution method using linked lists or dynamic arrays at each table position to store multiple key-value pairs

**Learning Objectives:**
- Students will implement a hash table with chaining collision resolution by writing complete Java or Python classes with insert, delete, and search methods
- Students will analyze the performance characteristics of different hash functions through empirical testing of distribution uniformity and collision rates

**Activities:**

**Assessment:**

**Activities:**

**Assessment:**

**Assessment:**

# ADVANCED MACHINE LEARNING FOR BIG DATA ANALYTICS
