# Course Syllabus
## Unearthing Digital Gold: A Survey of Modern Data Mining Frontiers

**Course Code:** DS 3350  
**Credits:** 3  
**Prerequisites:** Introduction to Programming (CS 1301), Statistics (MATH 2401), Database Systems (CS 2433)  
**Meeting Time:** MWF 10:00-10:50 AM  
**Semester:** Fall 2024  

---

## Course Description

This comprehensive survey course explores the evolving landscape of data mining techniques across diverse domains, from social media sentiment extraction to bioinformatics pattern discovery. Students will journey through both classical and cutting-edge mining methodologies, examining how different industries 'excavate' valuable insights from their data repositories. The course provides broad exposure to various mining paradigms including association rule mining, anomaly detection, stream mining, graph mining, and text mining, while investigating real-world applications in finance, healthcare, e-commerce, and cybersecurity. Rather than diving deep into any single technique, this survey approach allows students to develop a comprehensive understanding of the data mining ecosystem, comparing strengths and limitations of different approaches. Through hands-on projects using industry-standard tools like Weka, RapidMiner, and Python libraries, students will gain practical experience while building a foundation to specialize in specific mining areas in advanced coursework. The course emphasizes critical evaluation of mining results, ethical considerations in data excavation, and the strategic selection of appropriate mining techniques for given problem domains.

## Learning Objectives

Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

• **Evaluate and compare** diverse data mining algorithms across multiple application domains to select optimal approaches for specific business and research scenarios

• **Apply survey methodology principles** to systematically analyze the data mining landscape and identify emerging trends in mining technologies

• **Develop proficiency** in using multiple mining tools and platforms to extract, analyze, and interpret patterns from heterogeneous data sources

## Weekly Schedule

### **Week 1: Course Foundation & Data Mining Landscape**

# Course Syllabus

## Algorithmic Foundations of Pattern Discovery in Large-Scale Data Repositories

**Course Code:** DS 3400  
**Credits:** 3  
**Prerequisites:** Data Structures and Algorithms (CS 2400), Statistics (STAT 2100), Linear Algebra (MATH 2200)  
**Meeting Time:** Tuesday/Thursday 2:00-3:30 PM  
**Semester:** Fall 2024  

---

## Course Description

This course explores the theoretical underpinnings of extracting meaningful patterns from massive, heterogeneous data collections. Students will delve into the mathematical foundations of association rule mining, sequential pattern discovery, and graph mining algorithms. The curriculum emphasizes computational complexity analysis, algorithmic efficiency, and theoretical guarantees of mining techniques across diverse data types including transactional databases, time-series collections, and network structures. Through rigorous mathematical proofs and algorithmic design principles, students will understand how mining algorithms scale with data volume and dimensionality. The course covers advanced topics such as privacy-preserving mining, distributed mining architectures, and the theoretical limits of pattern discovery. Students will analyze the convergence properties of iterative mining algorithms, study approximation guarantees for NP-hard mining problems, and explore the statistical significance of discovered patterns. This theoretical foundation prepares students to design novel mining algorithms and critically evaluate existing approaches in research and industrial contexts.

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this course, students will be able to:

• Master the mathematical foundations of frequent itemset mining, sequential pattern mining, and subgraph mining algorithms  
• Apply complexity-theoretic analysis to evaluate the computational tractability of pattern discovery problems  
• Develop theoretical frameworks for assessing pattern significance and mining algorithm convergence properties  

## Weekly Schedule

### Week 1-2: Foundations of Pattern Discovery
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis and Statistical Visualization
- Univariate Analysis: Examination of single variables including measures of central tendency, dispersion, and distribution shape using histograms, box plots, and summary statistics
- Bivariate Analysis: Investigation of relationships between two variables through scatter plots, correlation analysis, cross-tabulation, and statistical association measures
- **Activity:** Evaluating Data Visualization Quality: Bar Chart vs. Pie Chart Effectiveness (35 min)
- **Reading:** Chapter 1-2 of textbook

### Week 3-4: Data Preprocessing and Feature Engineering
**Module:** Feature Engineering for Machine Learning: Creating Predictive Variables from Raw Data
- Feature scaling and normalization: Methods to standardize numerical features including StandardScaler, MinMaxScaler, and RobustScaler
- Categorical encoding: Techniques for converting categorical variables including one-hot encoding, label encoding, target encoding, and embedding methods
- **Activity:** Understanding Feature Selection Impact Through Correlation Matrix Analysis (75 min)
- **Assessment:** Customer Churn Analysis and Prediction Quiz (100 points)

### Week 5-6: Mathematical Foundations of Frequent Pattern Mining
**Module:** Advanced Exploratory Data Analysis with Python
- Multivariate Analysis: Investigation of relationships between multiple variables through correlation matrices, scatter plot matrices, and dimensionality reduction
- Statistical significance testing and pattern validation
- **Activity:** Interpreting Feature Correlation Patterns in Customer Churn Analysis (55 min)
- **Reading:** Chapter 6 of textbook

### Week 7-8: Association Rule Mining Algorithms
**Module:** Statistical Analysis and Pattern Recognition
- Apriori algorithm complexity analysis
- FP-Growth theoretical foundations
- Support and confidence measures
- **Activity:** Interpreting Correlation vs. Causation in Real-World Marketing Data (45 min)

### Week 9: Midterm Examination Period
- **Assessment:** Customer Churn Prediction Analysis Exam (100 points)

### Week 10-11: Sequential Pattern Mining
**Module:** Time-Series and Sequential Data Analysis
- Sequential pattern mining algorithms (GSP, PrefixSpan)
- Computational complexity of sequence mining
- **Activity:** Interpreting Bias-Variance Tradeoff Through Cross-Validation Learning Curves Analysis (80 min)
- **Reading:** Chapter 14 of textbook

### Week 12-13: Graph Mining and Network Analysis
**Module:** Network Data Analysis and Graph Algorithms
- Subgraph mining algorithms
- Graph isomorphism complexity
- Network motif discovery
- **Activity:** Comparative Evaluation of Machine Learning Model Deployment Strategies for Real-Time Fraud Detection (150 min)

### Week 14: Privacy-Preserving Mining and Distributed Algorithms
**Module:** Advanced Topics in Pattern Mining
- Differential privacy in pattern mining
- MapReduce frameworks for large-scale mining
- **Activity:** Evaluating Data Visualization Effectiveness for Business Decision-Making (95 min)

### Week 15: Algorithm Convergence and Statistical Significance
**Module:** Theoretical Analysis and Validation
- Convergence properties of iterative algorithms
- Multiple testing correction methods
- **Activity:** Critical Evaluation of Competing Machine Learning Models for Customer Churn Prediction (2 hours)

### Week 16: Final Projects and Presentations
- **Assessment:** End-to-End Data Science Solution Presentation (100 points)

---

| **Quizzes** | Customer Churn Analysis and Prediction Quiz | 100 | Week 4 |
| **Midterm Exam** | Customer Churn Prediction Analysis Exam | 100 | Week 9 |

## Course Description

This survey course explores the intersection of data science, visual design, and narrative communication across diverse domains. Students examine how organizations from Netflix to NASA leverage visualization to extract insights and communicate findings to stakeholders. The course surveys visualization methodologies spanning exploratory data analysis, interactive dashboards, geospatial mapping, network analysis, and emerging AR/VR applications. Through case studies from journalism, healthcare, finance, sports analytics, and social media, students analyze real-world visualization challenges and solutions. Topics include perceptual psychology principles, color theory, accessibility design, statistical graphics, and ethical considerations in data presentation. Students work with industry-standard tools including Tableau, D3.js, Python's visualization libraries, and R's ggplot2 to create compelling visual narratives. The survey approach exposes students to visualization applications across multiple sectors while developing critical evaluation skills for assessing visualization effectiveness. Emphasis is placed on translating complex analytical findings into clear, actionable visual communications for diverse audiences, from technical teams to executive leadership to general public consumption.

• Evaluate and critique visualization techniques across multiple industries and application domains  
• Design effective visual narratives that communicate complex data insights to diverse stakeholder audiences  
• Apply principles of visual perception, design theory, and accessibility to create inclusive data visualizations

# BEHAVIORAL ANALYTICS AND PREDICTIVE CUSTOMER INTELLIGENCE
**Course Code:** DSCI 485 | **Credits:** 3 | **Semester:** Fall 2024  
**Prerequisites:** Statistics (STAT 301), Programming with Python (CSCI 201), Machine Learning Fundamentals (DSCI 350)

---

## COURSE INFORMATION

**Class Meeting:** [days/times/location]  
**Lab Sessions:** [days/times/location]

---

## COURSE DESCRIPTION

This advanced course explores the intersection of behavioral psychology and data science to decode customer decision-making patterns and predict future behaviors. Students will dive deep into customer journey analytics, utilizing advanced statistical modeling techniques including survival analysis, propensity scoring, and sequential pattern mining to understand how customers interact with products and services over time. The course emphasizes real-world applications in e-commerce, digital marketing, and customer retention strategies. Students will work with large-scale transactional datasets, clickstream data, and multi-channel customer touchpoints to build sophisticated predictive models. Key topics include cohort analysis, customer lifetime value optimization, churn prediction models, recommendation system analytics, and A/B testing frameworks. The curriculum integrates machine learning techniques specifically tailored for behavioral data, including time-series forecasting, Markov chain modeling, and deep learning approaches for sequence prediction. Students will complete a capstone project analyzing real customer behavioral data to deliver actionable business insights and predictive models that drive strategic decision-making.

---

## LEARNING OBJECTIVES

By the end of this course, students will be able to:

1. **Master advanced analytical techniques** for modeling customer behavior patterns including survival analysis, sequential pattern mining, and propensity scoring methodologies
2. **Apply machine learning algorithms** specifically designed for behavioral data to build predictive models for customer lifetime value, churn prediction, and personalization systems
3. **Develop expertise in translating** complex behavioral analytics findings into strategic business recommendations and data-driven customer intelligence solutions

---

## REQUIRED MATERIALS

- **Textbook:** *Customer Analytics for Dummies* by Jeff Sauro (supplemented with course readings)
- **Software:** Python 3.8+, Jupyter Notebooks, scikit-learn, pandas, matplotlib, seaborn
- **Platform:** Course materials available on Canvas LMS
- **Hardware:** Laptop capable of running Python development environment

---

### Week 1: Foundations of Customer Behavioral Data
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis and Data Visualization with Python
- **Concepts:**
  - Descriptive Statistics - measures of central tendency, variability, and distribution shape used to summarize dataset characteristics
  - Data Profiling - systematic examination of data quality, completeness, consistency, and structure to understand dataset limitations
- **Activity:** Evaluating Data Cleaning Methods: Coffee Shop Sales Analysis (85 min)
- **Readings:** Chapter 1-2 (textbook), supplemental articles on behavioral data characteristics

### Week 2: Advanced EDA for Behavioral Patterns

- **Concepts:**
  - Univariate Analysis - Statistical summary and distribution examination of individual variables including measures of central tendency, dispersion, and shape
  - Bivariate and Multivariate Analysis - Investigation of relationships between two or more variables using correlation analysis, crosstabulation, and conditional distributions
- **Activity:** Evaluating Data Visualization Effectiveness for Business Decision-Making (45 min)

### Week 3: Feature Engineering for Customer Analytics
**Module:** Feature Engineering and Selection for Machine Learning
- **Concepts:**
  - Feature scaling and normalization - standardizing numerical features using min-max scaling, z-score normalization, and robust scaling techniques
  - Categorical encoding methods - converting categorical variables to numerical format using one-hot encoding, target encoding, and ordinal encoding
- **Activity:** Interpreting Correlation vs. Causation in Customer Purchase Data (100 min)

### Week 4: Advanced Feature Selection Strategies
**Module:** Feature Engineering and Selection for Machine Learning
- **Concepts:**
  - Feature transformation - systematic methods to convert raw variables into more predictive representations including scaling, encoding, and mathematical transformations
  - Feature selection - statistical and algorithmic techniques to identify the most informative subset of features while reducing dimensionality and overfitting
- **Assessment:** Exploratory Data Analysis Lab Report: Customer Purchase Behavior (Due)

### Weeks 5-6: Customer Segmentation and Cohort Analysis
- **Topics:** RFM analysis, behavioral segmentation, cohort analysis techniques
- **Focus:** Customer lifetime value foundations, retention analytics
- **Activity:** Interpreting Feature Importance in Random Forest Models for Customer Churn Prediction (60 min)

### Weeks 7-8: Predictive Modeling for Customer Behavior

- **Focus:** Advanced classification techniques for customer behavior
- **Activity:** Deconstructing Bias Sources in Machine Learning Pipeline Components (75 min)
- **Assessment:** Advanced Machine Learning Pipeline Design and Implementation Quiz (Due Week 8)

### Week 9: Sequential Pattern Mining and Journey Analytics
- **Topics:** Customer journey mapping, sequential pattern mining, Markov chain modeling
- **Focus:** Understanding customer pathways and decision sequences

### Week 10: Recommendation Systems and Personalization
- **Topics:** Collaborative filtering, content-based recommendations, hybrid approaches
- **Focus:** Building personalized customer experiences
- **Activity:** Interpreting Feature Importance and Model Performance Trade-offs in Ensemble Methods (100 min)

### Weeks 11-12: Time-Series Forecasting for Customer Behavior
- **Topics:** Time-series analysis, seasonal patterns, forecasting customer demand
- **Focus:** Temporal aspects of customer behavior prediction
- **Activity:** Critical Evaluation of Machine Learning Model Performance Across Competing Algorithmic Approaches (180 min)
- **Assessment:** Ethical Considerations in Machine Learning Model Deployment Discussion (Due Week 12)

### Weeks 13-14: A/B Testing and Experimental Design
- **Topics:** Statistical significance, experimental design, causal inference
- **Focus:** Measuring impact of behavioral interventions
- **Activity:** Comparative Evaluation of Machine Learning Pipeline Architectures for Production Deployment (240 min)

### Week 15: Capstone Project Implementation
- **Focus:** Final project completion, peer reviews, presentation preparation
- **Assessment:** Advanced Machine Learning Pipeline Design and Implementation Exam

# Probabilistic Reasoning and Statistical Inference in High-Dimensional Data
**Course Code:** DS 485 | **Credits:** 4 | **Semester:** Spring 2024

### Prerequisites
- Statistics (STAT 350) or equivalent
- Linear Algebra (MATH 250)  
- Programming experience in R or Python
- Calculus II (MATH 152)

## Course Description

This intensive course explores the statistical foundations underlying modern data science through the lens of high-dimensional data analysis. Students will master advanced probabilistic reasoning, Bayesian inference, and multivariate statistical methods essential for extracting meaningful insights from complex, large-scale datasets. The course emphasizes rigorous mathematical treatment of statistical concepts while maintaining practical relevance through hands-on implementation of algorithms from scratch. Topics include dimensionality reduction techniques, regularization methods, bootstrap and permutation testing, hierarchical modeling, and causal inference. Students will engage in weekly computational labs using R and Python, implementing statistical methods without relying on black-box functions. The intensive format includes daily problem-solving sessions, peer code reviews, and a capstone project involving real-world high-dimensional data analysis.

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this course, students will be able to:

1. **Advanced Statistical Mastery:** Develop expertise in statistical inference techniques for high-dimensional data including regularization, shrinkage estimators, and multiple testing corrections
2. **Algorithm Implementation:** Implement core statistical algorithms from mathematical foundations, demonstrating deep understanding of underlying probabilistic assumptions and computational complexity
3. **Bayesian Application:** Apply Bayesian reasoning and hierarchical modeling to real-world datasets, properly quantifying uncertainty and communicating statistical findings to technical and non-technical audiences

## Weekly Schedule

### Week 1: Foundations of High-Dimensional Data Analysis
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis and Data Visualization  
**Topics:**
- Univariate and bivariate analysis in high-dimensional contexts
- Statistical summaries and distribution analysis
- Visualization challenges with high-dimensional data
- Understanding correlation vs. causation in complex datasets

**Activity:** Interpreting Correlation vs Causation in Customer Churn Analysis (65 min)  
**Readings:** Course packet Ch. 1; Hastie et al. Ch. 1

### Week 2: Feature Engineering Foundations
**Module:** Feature Engineering and Selection for Machine Learning  
**Topics:**
- Feature transformation and scaling techniques
- Categorical encoding strategies for high-dimensional data
- Mathematical transformations and their statistical properties
- Domain knowledge integration in feature creation

**Activity:** Interpreting Feature Correlation Patterns in Customer Purchase Data (55 min)  
**Readings:** Hastie et al. Ch. 3; Selected papers on feature engineering

### Week 3: Probabilistic Foundations for High-Dimensional Inference
**Topics:**
- Multivariate probability distributions
- Curse of dimensionality and its statistical implications
- Maximum likelihood estimation in high dimensions
- Asymptotic behavior of estimators

**Activity:** Evaluating Data Visualization Effectiveness for Customer Survey Analysis (75 min)  
**Due:** Problem Set 1

### Week 4: Regularization and Shrinkage Methods
**Topics:**
- Ridge regression: theory and implementation
- LASSO: sparse solutions and variable selection
- Elastic net and generalizations
- Cross-validation for regularization parameter selection

**Activity:** Interpreting Bias-Variance Tradeoff Through Cross-Validation Learning Curves Analysis (85 min)  
**Readings:** Hastie et al. Ch. 3.4, 18.4

### Week 5: Bayesian Inference Fundamentals
**Topics:**
- Bayesian vs. frequentist paradigms
- Prior specification and sensitivity analysis
- Conjugate priors and posterior computation
- Bayesian model comparison

**Activity:** Critical Evaluation of Machine Learning Model Selection for Imbalanced Healthcare Dataset (140 min)  
**Due:** Problem Set 2

### Week 6: Hierarchical and Multilevel Modeling
**Topics:**
- Random effects and mixed models
- Bayesian hierarchical models
- Partial pooling and shrinkage
- Applications in genomics and social science

**Assessment:Quiz 1:** Advanced Machine Learning Pipeline Assessment (100 points)

### Week 7: Dimensionality Reduction Theory
**Topics:**
- Principal Component Analysis: mathematical foundations
- Singular Value Decomposition theory
- Random projections and Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma
- Manifold learning principles

**Activity:** Interpreting Customer Segmentation Results from K-Means Clustering Analysis (60 min)  
**Readings:** Hastie et al. Ch. 14.5

### Week 8: Advanced Dimensionality Reduction
**Topics:**
- Independent Component Analysis
- t-SNE and UMAP theory
- Sparse PCA and dictionary learning
- Nonlinear dimensionality reduction

**Due:** Problem Set 3

### Week 9: Multiple Testing and False Discovery Rate
**Topics:**
- Family-wise error rate control
- Benjamini-Hochberg procedure
- q-values and local false discovery rates
- Applications in genomics

**Activity:** Analyzing Bias Propagation in Multi-Stage Machine Learning Pipelines (110 min)

### Week 10: Bootstrap and Resampling Methods
**Topics:**
- Bootstrap theory and consistency
- Parametric vs. nonparametric bootstrap
- Permutation tests and exact inference
- Subsampling methods

**Assessment:Presentation:** Data Science Process Presentation: From Question to Insight (100 points)

### Week 11: Causal Inference in Observational Data
**Topics:**
- Potential outcomes framework
- Propensity score methods
- Instrumental variables
- Difference-in-differences

**Due:** Problem Set 4

### Week 12: High-Dimensional Hypothesis Testing
**Topics:**
- Sparse signal detection
- Minimax testing theory
- Higher criticism and innovations
- Applications to genomics data

**Activity:** Critical Evaluation of Predictive Models for Healthcare Risk Assessment (220 min)

### Week 13: Model Selection and Information Criteria
**Topics:**
- AIC, BIC, and extensions to high dimensions
- Cross-validation theory
- Information-theoretic model selection
- Prediction vs. explanation trade-offs

**Assessment:Discussion:** Bias Detection and Mitigation in Machine Learning Systems (100 points)

### Week 14: Advanced Topics and Applications
**Topics:**
- Sparse graphical models
- High-dimensional time series
- Functional data analysis
- Recent developments in statistical learning

**Activity:** Evaluating Data Visualization Effectiveness for Customer Sales Analysis (55 min)

### Week 15: Capstone Project Presentations
**Topics:**
- Student project presentations
- Peer review and feedback
- Integration of course concepts
- Future directions in statistical inference

**Assessment:Portfolio:** End-to-End Machine Learning Portfolio (100 points)  
**Assessment:Project:** Customer Churn Prediction Analysis Project (100 points)

# DISTRIBUTED ANALYTICS FOR STREAMING DATA ECOSYSTEMS

**Teaching Assistant:** [TA Name] |

## COURSE DESCRIPTION
This intensive course immerses students in the complexities of processing and analyzing massive, continuously flowing data streams in real-time distributed environments. Students will architect and implement scalable analytics pipelines capable of handling terabytes of streaming data from IoT sensors, social media feeds, financial transactions, and web clickstreams. # Visual Storytelling with Data: From Pixels to Persuasion

**Course Code:** DS 3XX  
**Credits:** 3  
**Prerequisites:** Introduction to Statistics, Programming Fundamentals  
**Meeting Time:** MWF 10:00-10:50 AM  
**Semester:** Fall 2024  

## Course Description

This survey course explores how data visualization serves as a bridge between raw data and human understanding across diverse domains. Students examine visualization techniques from traditional statistical graphics to cutting-edge interactive dashboards, virtual reality data environments, and artistic data representations. The course surveys real-world applications spanning journalism, business intelligence, scientific research, public policy, and social media analytics. Through hands-on projects, students learn to critically evaluate visualization choices, understand cognitive principles behind effective visual communication, and master tools ranging from Python/R libraries to specialized platforms like Tableau, D3.js, and emerging VR/AR visualization frameworks. Emphasis is placed on ethical considerations in data presentation, accessibility in visual design, and the psychological impact of visual choices on decision-making.

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this course, students will be able to:

1. **Evaluate and critique** visualization techniques across multiple domains including journalism, business, science, and public policy
2. **Apply cognitive and perceptual principles** to design effective visual narratives that communicate complex data insights to diverse audiences
3. **Develop proficiency** in a survey of visualization tools and platforms, from programming libraries to enterprise dashboards and emerging technologies

## Weekly Schedule

### Week 1: Foundations of Visual Data Communication

  - Univariate Analysis: examining individual variables through measures of central tendency, dispersion, and distribution shape using histograms, box plots, and summary statistics

### Week 3: Python for Visual Storytelling

# Course Syllabus

## CS 3820: Algorithmic Intelligence: From Raw Data to Predictive Systems

- Lecture: MWF 10:00-10:50 AM
- Lab: T/Th 2:00-4:00 PM (mandatory)

---

## Course Description

This intensive course transforms students into machine learning practitioners through hands-on development of complete predictive systems. Students work with real-world messy datasets to build end-to-end ML pipelines, from data ingestion and preprocessing to model deployment and monitoring. The course emphasizes algorithmic thinking and practical implementation over theoretical foundations, requiring students to code solutions from scratch before using high-level libraries. Through weekly hackathons and industry case studies, students tackle complex problems in computer vision, natural language processing, and time series forecasting. The curriculum integrates modern MLOps practices, including version control for models, automated testing, and continuous integration. Students collaborate on a semester-long capstone project with external industry partners, delivering production-ready ML systems. The intensive format includes mandatory lab sessions, peer code reviews, and real-time debugging workshops. By course completion, students possess a portfolio of deployed ML applications and the technical confidence to architect scalable predictive systems in professional environments.

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this course, students will be able to:

• **Design and implement complete machine learning pipelines** from raw data collection through model deployment and monitoring  
• **Master algorithmic problem-solving** by coding ML algorithms from fundamentals before utilizing advanced frameworks  
• **Develop production-ready predictive systems** using industry-standard MLOps practices and collaborative development workflows  
• **Apply machine learning techniques** across diverse domains including computer vision, NLP, and time series analysis through intensive project-based learning

---

## Weekly Schedule

### Week 1: Foundations of Data Analysis
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) and Statistical Visualization
- **Concepts:**
  - Descriptive Statistics: Measures of central tendency, dispersion, and distribution shape including mean, median, mode, variance, standard deviation, skewness, and kurtosis
  - Data Distribution Analysis: Understanding normal, skewed, and multimodal distributions through histograms, box plots, Q-Q plots, and statistical tests for normality
- **Lab Activity:** Interpreting Data Distribution Patterns Through Real-World Sales Analytics (60 min)
- **Assignment:** Data profiling report on provided messy dataset

### Week 2: Data Understanding and Visualization
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis and Data Visualization Fundamentals
- **Concepts:**
  - Data profiling: Systematic examination of dataset structure, completeness, and quality including missing value patterns and data type validation
  - Distribution analysis: Understanding data spread, central tendency, skewness, and kurtosis through histograms, box plots, and statistical measures
- **Lab Activity:** Interpreting Data Distribution Patterns Using Real-World Sales Dataset (90 min)
- **Mini-Hackathon:** Visualization dashboard creation

### Week 3: Relationship Analysis
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis and Data Visualization with Python
- **Concepts:**
  - Univariate Analysis - Statistical examination of individual variables including measures of central tendency, dispersion, and distribution shape
  - Bivariate and Multivariate Analysis - Exploration of relationships between multiple variables using correlation matrices, scatter plots, and cross-tabulations
- **Lab Activity:** Interpreting Feature Correlation Patterns in Customer Purchase Data (65 min)
- **Quiz:** Customer Churn Analysis and Model Development Quiz (100 points)

### Week 4: Advanced Correlation Analysis
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis and Feature Engineering
- **Concepts:**

syllabus_content:
# Data-Driven Decision Making for Business Performance
**Course Syllabus - Spring 2024**

## Course Description

This course bridges the gap between raw data and strategic business decisions by teaching students how to transform organizational data into actionable intelligence. Students learn to identify key performance indicators, design executive dashboards, and communicate data insights to stakeholders across different business functions. The curriculum emphasizes practical applications in sales forecasting, customer segmentation, market analysis, and operational efficiency measurement. Through hands-on projects using real business datasets, students master essential tools like Excel, Tableau, and SQL while developing critical thinking skills to evaluate data quality and bias. The course covers fundamental statistical concepts within business contexts, teaching students to recognize patterns, trends, and anomalies that impact organizational performance. Students work on collaborative projects that simulate real-world business scenarios, learning to present findings to non-technical audiences and make recommendations based on data analysis. By course completion, students understand how to leverage data science techniques to solve common business challenges, create compelling visualizations, and establish data governance practices. This practical approach prepares students for entry-level business analyst roles or advanced coursework in data science, emphasizing the strategic value of data in modern organizations.

## Learning Objectives

Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

• **Design and implement business intelligence dashboards** that translate complex data into actionable insights for organizational decision-making
• **Apply statistical analysis techniques** to solve real-world business problems including sales forecasting, customer behavior analysis, and operational optimization
• **Develop proficiency in communicating data-driven recommendations** to diverse stakeholders through compelling visualizations and executive presentations

### Software & Tools
- Microsoft Excel (Office 365)
- Tableau Desktop (Student License)
- SQL Server Management Studio
- Python 3.x with Jupyter Notebooks
- Access to university's business database systems

## Weekly Schedule

### Week 1: Course Introduction & Data Landscape
**Topics:** Course overview, role of data in business decisions, data types and sources
**Readings:** Chapter 1-2 from primary textbook
**Activities:** Course introduction and business data exploration

### Week 2: Exploratory Data Analysis Fundamentals
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis and Statistical Visualization
**Key Concepts:** 
- Univariate Analysis - Statistical examination of individual variables including measures of central tendency, dispersion, and distribution shape
- Bivariate and Multivariate Analysis - Exploring relationships between two or more variables using correlation analysis, cross-tabulations, and multi-dimensional visualizations
**Activities:** Interpreting Correlation vs. Causation in Customer Purchase Data Analysis (60 minutes)

### Week 3: Data Quality and Assessment
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) with Python
**Key Concepts:**
- Descriptive Statistics - measures of central tendency, variability, and distribution shape that summarize dataset characteristics
- Data Quality Assessment - systematic evaluation of completeness, consistency, accuracy, and validity of datasets
**Activities:** Evaluating Data Visualization Effectiveness for Sales Performance Analysis (45 minutes)

### Week 4: Advanced EDA and Visualization
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis and Visualization with Python
**Key Concepts:**
- Univariate Analysis - Examining individual variables through histograms, box plots, and summary statistics to understand distributions and identify outliers
- Bivariate and Multivariate Analysis - Exploring relationships between variables using correlation matrices, scatter plots, and cross-tabulations
**Activities:** Evaluating Data Visualization Effectiveness for Customer Satisfaction Analysis (50 minutes)

### Week 5: Statistical Analysis for Business
**Topics:** Hypothesis testing, confidence intervals, A/B testing for business applications
**Activities:** Interpreting Bias-Variance Trade-off Through Cross-Validation Learning Curves (75 minutes)
**Assessment:** Advanced Machine Learning Pipeline Optimization and Model Interpretability Quiz (100 points)

### Week 6: Feature Engineering Foundations
**Module:** Feature Engineering and Selection for Machine Learning
**Key Concepts:**
- Feature scaling and normalization - techniques including StandardScaler, MinMaxScaler, and RobustScaler to prepare numerical features for machine learning algorithms
- Categorical encoding strategies - one-hot encoding, target encoding, and embedding approaches for converting categorical variables into numerical representations
**Activities:** Interpreting Feature Importance in Random Forest Models for Customer Churn Prediction (80 minutes)

### Week 7: Advanced Feature Engineering
**Module:** Feature Engineering and Selection for Predictive Modeling
**Key Concepts:**
- Feature Engineering: The process of creating new features from existing data to improve model performance, including mathematical transformations, domain-specific features, and interaction terms
- Feature Selection: Systematic methods for identifying the most relevant features while removing redundant or irrelevant ones, including univariate selection, recursive feature elimination, and regularization-based selection
**Activities:** Evaluating Data Visualization Effectiveness for Customer Sales Analysis (45 minutes)

### Week 8: Midterm Week
**Assessment:** Advanced Predictive Modeling and Analysis Comprehensive Exam (100 points)

### Week 9: Customer Analytics and Segmentation
**Topics:** RFM analysis, clustering techniques, customer lifetime value
**Activities:** Critical Evaluation of Predictive Models for Business Impact Assessment (120 minutes)
**Project:** Customer Segmentation Analysis Project begins

### Week 10: Sales Forecasting and Demand Planning
**Topics:** Time series analysis, seasonal decomposition, forecasting methods
**Activities:** Interpreting Feature Importance in Random Forest Models for Customer Churn Prediction (105 minutes)

### Week 11: Business Intelligence Dashboards
**Topics:** KPI identification, dashboard design principles, Tableau advanced features
**Activities:** Dashboard design workshop and peer review

### Week 12: Predictive Modeling for Business
**Topics:** Regression analysis, classification models, model validation
**Activities:** Comparative Evaluation of Machine Learning Models for Predicting Customer Churn Using Industry-Standard Metrics (180 minutes)

### Week 13: Model Interpretation and Communication
**Topics:** Feature importance, SHAP values, communicating uncertainty
**Activities:** Interpreting Bias-Variance Tradeoff Through Cross-Validation Learning Curves (85 minutes)
**Assessment:** Customer Segmentation Analysis Project due (100 points)

### Week 14: Data Governance and Ethics
**Topics:** Data privacy, ethical considerations, regulatory compliance
**Activities:** Case study discussions on data ethics in business

### Week 15: Final Projects and Presentations
**Assessment:** End-to-End Machine Learning Pipeline: Business Impact Analysis and Technical Implementation (100 points)

### Week 16: Final Assessments
**Assessment:** End-to-End Customer Churn Prediction Portfolio Project due (100 points)

## Assessment Plan

| Assessment Type | Assignment | Points | Weight | Due Date |
|----------------|------------|--------|---------|----------|
| Quiz | Advanced Machine Learning Pipeline Quiz | 100 | 10% | Week 5 |
| Exam | Advanced Predictive Modeling Comprehensive Exam | 100 | 20% | Week 8 |
| Project | Customer Segmentation Analysis Project | 100 | 25% | Week 13 |
| Presentation | End-to-End ML Pipeline Presentation | 100 | 20% | Week 15 |
| Portfolio | Customer Churn Prediction Portfolio | 100 | 25% | Week 16 |
| **Total** | | **500** | **100%** | |

### Late Assignment Policy
- Assignments submitted up to 24 hours late: 10% deduction
- Assignments submitted 24-48 hours late: 20% deduction
- Assignments submitted more than 48 hours late: 50% deduction
- No assignments accepted more than one week late without prior arrangement

### Make-up Policy
Make-up exams and quizzes will only be allowed for documented emergencies or illness. Students must notify the instructor within 24 hours of the missed assessment and provide appropriate documentation.

### Professional Development
Students are encouraged to:
- Join relevant professional organizations (ASA, INFORMS)
- Attend data science meetups and conferences
- Develop LinkedIn profiles showcasing course projects
- Consider internship opportunities in business analytics

# Strategic Business Intelligence: End-to-End Analytics Pipeline Development

## Course Description

This capstone course challenges students to design, implement, and deploy comprehensive analytics pipelines that solve real-world business problems. Working directly with industry partners, students will navigate the complete data science lifecycle from stakeholder interviews and business problem formulation to model deployment and performance monitoring. The course emphasizes strategic decision-making, requiring students to justify analytical approaches, communicate findings to non-technical executives, and measure business impact. Students will work in cross-functional teams to tackle complex, ambiguous problems where the 'right' answer isn't predetermined. Key focus areas include predictive modeling for business forecasting, customer segmentation strategies, operational efficiency optimization, and risk assessment frameworks. The course culminates in a client presentation where students defend their analytical choices, demonstrate ROI calculations, and propose implementation roadmaps. Unlike traditional academic projects, students must consider real constraints including data privacy regulations, computational costs, and organizational change management. This intensive, project-based experience bridges the gap between academic theory and professional practice, preparing graduates to immediately contribute as analytics professionals in data-driven organizations.

## Learning Objectives

Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

• **Design and implement end-to-end analytics pipelines** that address authentic business challenges with measurable outcomes
• **Develop advanced competencies** in business intelligence tools, predictive modeling, and strategic data visualization for executive decision-making
• **Demonstrate professional communication skills** by translating complex analytical findings into actionable business recommendations for diverse stakeholder audiences

### Week 4: Comprehensive Data Exploration

# Course Syllabus
## Extracting Gold from Digital Noise: Advanced Pattern Mining in Complex Data Ecosystems

**Course Code:** DS 385  
**Credits:** 3  
**Prerequisites:** Data Structures and Algorithms, Statistics, Python Programming  
**Meeting Time:** Tuesday/Thursday 2:00-3:30 PM  
**Semester:** Fall 2024  

---

## Course Description

This comprehensive course transforms students into data archaeologists, teaching them to unearth valuable insights from massive, noisy datasets across diverse domains. Students master advanced mining techniques including sequential pattern discovery, anomaly detection, association rule mining, and temporal pattern extraction. The curriculum emphasizes real-world applications from social media streams, financial transactions, IoT sensor networks, and biological sequences. Through hands-on projects, students learn to handle incomplete data, scale mining algorithms for big data environments, and validate discovered patterns. The course bridges theoretical foundations with practical implementation, covering both classical algorithms (Apriori, FP-Growth) and cutting-edge techniques (deep pattern mining, graph mining). Students work with industry-standard tools including Apache Spark, Weka, and specialized mining libraries while developing critical thinking skills to distinguish meaningful patterns from statistical artifacts. By semester's end, students can design end-to-end mining pipelines, optimize algorithms for specific data characteristics, and communicate findings to stakeholders.

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this course, students will be able to:

1. **Master Advanced Pattern Mining Techniques:** Students will master advanced pattern mining algorithms and select appropriate techniques for specific data types and business contexts including sequential patterns, association rules, and anomaly detection.

2. **Design Scalable Mining Solutions:** Students will design and implement scalable mining pipelines capable of processing real-world datasets with noise, missing values, and temporal complexity using industry-standard tools.

3. **Validate and Communicate Insights:** Students will develop expertise in validating, interpreting, and communicating discovered patterns while avoiding common pitfalls like spurious correlations and overfitting.

---

# BEHAVIORAL ANALYTICS LAB: DECODING HUMAN PATTERNS THROUGH DATA

**Course Code:** DS 385  
**Credits:** 3  
**Prerequisites:** Introduction to Statistics, Programming Fundamentals (Python), Introduction to Data Science  
**Meeting Time:** Tuesdays & Thursdays, 2:00-3:50 PM  

## INSTRUCTOR INFORMATION

## COURSE DESCRIPTION

This hands-on laboratory course immerses students in the fascinating world of behavioral analytics, where human actions become data stories waiting to be decoded. Students work with real-world datasets from social media platforms, e-commerce sites, mobile applications, and digital marketing campaigns to uncover hidden patterns in human behavior. Through intensive lab sessions, students master advanced analytics techniques including cohort analysis, funnel optimization, A/B testing frameworks, customer journey mapping, and predictive behavioral modeling. The course emphasizes practical application over theory, with students designing and executing their own behavioral experiments, building interactive dashboards to visualize user engagement patterns, and developing machine learning models to predict customer churn, conversion likelihood, and user lifetime value. Each week focuses on a different behavioral analytics challenge, from analyzing click-through patterns and shopping cart abandonment to understanding social network dynamics and content virality. Students leave with a portfolio of behavioral analytics projects and the skills to transform raw user interaction data into actionable business insights that drive strategic decision-making.

## LEARNING OBJECTIVES

By the end of this course, students will be able to:

• **Master behavioral analytics techniques** including cohort analysis, funnel optimization, and customer journey mapping using industry-standard tools  
• **Design and execute controlled behavioral experiments** through A/B testing frameworks and statistical analysis methods  
• **Develop predictive models** for user behavior including churn prediction, conversion optimization, and lifetime value estimation  
• **Create interactive dashboards and visualizations** that effectively communicate behavioral insights to stakeholders  
• **Apply ethical frameworks** for analyzing human behavioral data while maintaining privacy and consent standards  

## REQUIRED MATERIALS

- **Textbook:** *Behavioral Analytics in Practice* (available through course website)
- **Software:** Python 3.8+, Jupyter Notebooks, Tableau/Power BI (student licenses provided)
- **Hardware:** Personal laptop capable of running data analysis software
- **Datasets:** Provided through course management system (anonymized real-world data)

---

# WEEKLY SCHEDULE

## Week 1: Foundation & Data Exploration
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) and Data Visualization Fundamentals  
**Topics:**
- Descriptive Statistics: Measures of central tendency, variability, and distribution shape used to summarize dataset characteristics
- Data Profiling: Systematic examination of data structure, completeness, uniqueness, and validity to assess dataset quality

**Lab Activities:**
- Interpreting Distribution Patterns in Customer Purchase Data (50 min)
- Evaluating Data Visualization Effectiveness for Customer Survey Analysis (65 min)

## Week 2: Advanced EDA Techniques
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) with Python  
**Topics:**
- Descriptive Statistics: Measures of central tendency, dispersion, and distribution shape including mean, median, mode, standard deviation, skewness, and kurtosis
- Data Quality Assessment: Systematic identification and treatment of missing values, duplicate records, outliers, and inconsistent data formats

**Lab Activities:**
- Evaluating Data Visualization Quality: Chart Detective Challenge (75 min)

## Week 3: Understanding Relationships in Data
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) and Data Visualization  
**Topics:**
- Univariate Analysis: Statistical examination of individual variables including measures of central tendency, dispersion, and distribution shape
- Bivariate and Multivariate Analysis: Investigation of relationships between two or more variables using correlation analysis, cross-tabulation, and dimensionality reduction

**Lab Activities:**
- Interpreting Feature Correlation Heatmaps for Customer Churn Prediction (55 min)
- Evaluating Data Visualization Choices for Restaurant Sales Analysis (55 min)

## Week 4: Preparing Data for Behavioral Analysis
**Module:** Feature Engineering for Machine Learning: Transforming Raw Data into Predictive Power  
**Topics:**
- Feature Scaling and Normalization: Mathematical transformations (standardization, min-max scaling, robust scaling) that ensure features contribute equally to model training
- Categorical Encoding Strategies: Techniques including one-hot encoding, target encoding, and embedding methods for converting categorical data into numerical representations

## Week 5: Feature Engineering Deep Dive
**Module:** Feature Engineering and Selection for Machine Learning  
**Topics:**
- Feature Transformation: Converting raw data into more useful representations through mathematical operations, binning, and aggregation
- Dimensionality Reduction: Reducing the number of features while preserving important information using PCA, feature selection, and regularization

**Assessment Due:** Beginner Data Science Portfolio: Customer Sales Analysis Project (100 points)

## Week 6: Statistical Foundations for Behavioral Analytics
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis and Data Visualization  
**Topics:**
- Univariate Analysis: examining single variables through histograms, box plots, and summary statistics to understand distributions and identify outliers
- Bivariate and Multivariate Analysis: exploring relationships between variables using correlation matrices, scatter plots, and dimensionality reduction techniques

**Lab Activities:**
- Interpreting Correlation vs. Causation in Real-World Marketing Data (60 min)

## Week 7: Model Selection and Evaluation
**Module:** Feature Engineering and Selection for Machine Learning  
**Topics:**
- Feature transformation: mathematical operations applied to raw variables to create more predictive features (log transforms, polynomial features, binning)
- Feature selection methods: systematic approaches to identify the most relevant features including univariate statistics, recursive feature elimination, and LASSO regularization

**Lab Activities:**
- Deconstructing Bias-Variance Tradeoff Through Model Performance Decomposition Analysis (85 min)
- Interpreting Bias-Variance Tradeoff Through Cross-Validation Learning Curves Analysis (80 min)

## Week 8: Mid-Semester Assessment Week
**Assessment:** Customer Segmentation Analysis and Predictive Modeling Exam (100 points)

## Week 9: Cohort Analysis & Customer Journey Mapping
**Focus:** Applied behavioral analytics techniques  
**Lab Activities:**
- Evaluating Machine Learning Model Performance Across Multiple Business Scenarios (180 min)

**Assessment Due:** Predictive Analytics Pipeline: Customer Churn Analysis Lab Report (100 points)

## Week 10: A/B Testing & Experimental Design
**Focus:** Controlled behavioral experiments and statistical testing

## Week 11: Predictive Behavioral Modeling
**Focus:** Machine learning applications for behavior prediction

## Week 12: Advanced Visualization & Dashboard Creation
**Focus:** Interactive dashboards and stakeholder communication

## Week 13: Ethics in Behavioral Analytics
**Focus:** Privacy, consent, and responsible data use

## Week 14: Industry Applications & Case Studies
**Focus:** Real-world implementation and business impact

**Lab Activities:**
- Critical Evaluation of Competing Machine Learning Models for Customer Churn Prediction (240 min)

## Week 15: Final Projects & Presentations
**Assessment Due:** End-to-End Predictive Analytics Pipeline: Customer Churn Prediction System (100 points)

## Finals Week: Project Presentations
**Assessment:** End-to-End Machine Learning Pipeline: Business Impact Analysis and Presentation (100 points)

---

# ASSESSMENT PLAN

| Assessment Type | Points | Percentage | 
|----------------|--------|------------|
| Lab Reports | 100 | 20% |
| Exams | 100 | 20% |
| Portfolio Project | 100 | 20% |
| Final Project | 100 | 20% |
| Final Presentation | 100 | 20% |
| **Total** | **500** | **100%** |

## Grading Scale
- A: 93-100% (465-500 points)
- A-: 90-92% (450-464 points)
- B+: 87-89% (435-449 points)
- B: 83-86% (415-434 points)
- B-: 80-82% (400-414 points)

- C: 73-76% (365-384 points)
- C-: 70-72% (350-364 points)
- D: 60-69% (300-349 points)

## Assessment Details

### 1. Predictive Analytics Pipeline: Customer Churn Analysis Lab Report (100 points - 20%)
**Due:** Week 9  
Students will complete a comprehensive analysis of customer churn using real e-commerce data, demonstrating mastery of data preprocessing, feature engineering, model selection, and evaluation techniques.

### 2. Customer Segmentation Analysis and Predictive Modeling Exam (100 points - 20%)
**Date:** Week 8  
Comprehensive examination covering statistical foundations, feature engineering techniques, and behavioral analytics concepts through practical problem-solving scenarios.

### 3. Beginner Data Science Portfolio: Customer Sales Analysis Project (100 points - 20%)
**Due:** Week 5  
Students develop a portfolio showcasing EDA skills, visualization techniques, and basic predictive modeling using customer sales data from multiple business domains.

### 4. End-to-End Predictive Analytics Pipeline: Customer Churn Prediction System (100 points - 20%)
**Due:** Week 15  
Capstone project requiring students to build a complete behavioral analytics system including data ingestion, feature engineering, model training, evaluation, and deployment considerations.

### 5. End-to-End Machine Learning Pipeline: Business Impact Analysis and Presentation (100 points - 20%)
**Date:** Finals Week  
Professional presentation of final project findings, including business recommendations, technical methodology, and ethical considerations for stakeholder audiences.

---

# COURSE POLICIES

## Attendance Policy
Regular attendance is essential for success in this hands-on laboratory course. Students are expected to attend all class sessions. More than two unexcused absences may result in a reduction of the final grade. Students must notify the instructor in advance of any planned absence and arrange to make up missed lab work.

## Late Assignment Policy
- Assignments submitted within 24 hours of the deadline: 10% penalty
- Assignments submitted within 48 hours of the deadline: 25% penalty  
- Assignments submitted more than 48 hours late: 50% penalty

## Technology Policy
Personal laptops are required for all lab sessions. Students must come prepared with necessary software installed and datasets downloaded. Mobile phones should be silenced during class. Use of technology should be limited to course-related activities during instruction.

## Academic Integrity
All work submitted must be original and completed individually unless explicitly designated as group work. Students may discuss concepts and approaches but must complete all coding, analysis, and writing independently. Plagiarism of code, analysis, or written work will result in course failure. Proper citation of data sources and external libraries is required.

## Collaboration Policy
While students are encouraged to discuss concepts and troubleshoot technical issues together, all submitted work must be completed individually. Students may:

Students may NOT:

## Accommodation Statement
Students with documented disabilities who may need accommodations should schedule an appointment with the instructor as soon as possible. All discussions will remain confidential. Students with disabilities should contact the Office of Disability Services to verify their eligibility for reasonable accommodations.

## Communication Policy
- Email responses within 48 hours during weekdays

- Office hours available for individual consultation on projects and concepts

## Data Ethics and Privacy
This course involves working with sensitive behavioral data. Students must:
- Maintain confidentiality of all provided datasets
- Follow ethical guidelines for data analysis and interpretation
- Respect privacy considerations in all projects and presentations  
- Complete required training on responsible data use

## Course Evaluation
Students will have multiple opportunities to provide feedback on course content, pace, and effectiveness through:
- Mid-semester feedback survey
- Weekly reflection prompts
- End-of-semester course evaluation
- Optional individual feedback sessions

syllabus_content:
# STREAMING ANALYTICS AND REAL-TIME DECISION SYSTEMS
**Course Code:** DS 485  
**Credits:** 4  
**Prerequisites:** Data Structures and Algorithms, Statistics, Database Systems, Introduction to Machine Learning  
**Meeting Time:** MWF 10:00-11:00 AM + Lab W 2:00-4:50 PM  

## INSTRUCTOR INFORMATION

## COURSE DESCRIPTION
This hands-on course immerses students in the world of streaming data analytics, where decisions must be made in milliseconds using massive, continuously flowing datasets. Students work with live data streams from social media APIs, IoT sensor networks, financial markets, and e-commerce platforms to build real-time analytics pipelines. The course emphasizes practical implementation using Apache Kafka, Apache Storm, and Apache Flink for stream processing, combined with machine learning models that adapt and learn from incoming data. Students tackle real-world scenarios including fraud detection systems that process thousands of transactions per second, recommendation engines that update user profiles in real-time, and monitoring systems that detect anomalies in network traffic as they occur. Through project-based learning, students design and deploy scalable architectures that handle data velocities exceeding millions of events per hour, while maintaining low latency and high availability. The course culminates in a capstone project where teams build end-to-end streaming analytics solutions for industry partners, addressing genuine business challenges that require immediate data-driven responses.

## LEARNING OBJECTIVES
Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:
• Design and implement real-time data processing pipelines capable of handling high-velocity streaming data from multiple sources
• Develop online machine learning models that continuously adapt to streaming data patterns without batch retraining
• Architect fault-tolerant distributed systems for stream processing using industry-standard tools like Kafka, Storm, and Flink
• Optimize streaming analytics systems for low-latency decision making in time-critical applications such as fraud detection and dynamic pricing
• Evaluate and select appropriate streaming technologies based on specific business requirements and data characteristics

## REQUIRED TEXTBOOKS AND MATERIALS
**Primary Textbook:**
- Psaltis, A. G. (2017). *Streaming Data: Understanding the Real-Time Pipeline*. Manning Publications.

**Supplementary Resources:**
- Chen, J. (2018). *Real-Time Analytics with Apache Storm*. Packt Publishing.
- Garg, N. (2017). *Apache Kafka*. Packt Publishing.
- Online documentation for Apache Kafka, Flink, and Storm

**Software Requirements:**
- Apache Kafka, Apache Flink, Apache Storm
- Python 3.8+ with scikit-learn, pandas, NumPy
- Docker and Kubernetes
- AWS/Google Cloud Platform access (provided)

## WEEKLY SCHEDULE

### Week 1: Course Introduction and Streaming Data Fundamentals
**Topics:**
- Introduction to streaming analytics vs. batch processing
- Real-time data characteristics: velocity, volume, variety
- Stream processing paradigms and use cases

**Activities:**
- Evaluating Data Visualization Effectiveness for Business Decision-Making (50 minutes)

### Week 2: Stream Processing Architectures
**Topics:**
- Lambda and Kappa architectures
- Event-driven architectures
- Microservices for streaming applications

### Week 3: Apache Kafka Fundamentals
**Topics:**
- Kafka architecture: brokers, topics, partitions
- Producer and consumer APIs
- Stream processing with Kafka Streams

### Week 4: Advanced Kafka and Data Ingestion
**Topics:**
- Kafka Connect for data integration
- Schema registry and Avro serialization
- Handling backpressure and flow control

**Activities:**
- Interpreting Statistical Significance in A/B Test Results for E-commerce Conversion Rates (45 minutes)

### Week 5: Apache Storm for Real-Time Processing
**Topics:**
- Storm topology design: spouts and bolts
- Guaranteed message processing
- Parallelization and fault tolerance

**Assessment:** Customer Churn Analysis: Feature Engineering and Model Evaluation Quiz (100 points)

### Week 6: Apache Flink Stream Processing
**Topics:**
- Flink's datastream API
- Event time vs. processing time
- Windowing operations

**Activities:**
- Interpreting Bias-Variance Tradeoff Through Model Complexity Analysis (60 minutes)

### Week 7: Complex Event Processing and Pattern Detection
**Topics:**
- CEP libraries and pattern matching
- Stateful stream processing
- Time-based aggregations

### Week 8: Online Machine Learning for Streams
**Topics:**
- Incremental learning algorithms
- Concept drift detection and adaptation
- Model updates without retraining

syllabus_content:
# Digital Archaeologists: Mining Hidden Patterns in Complex Data Ecosystems
**Course Syllabus - Spring 2024**

## Course Description

This capstone course transforms students into digital archaeologists who excavate valuable insights from complex, multi-layered data ecosystems. Students work in teams to tackle real-world mining challenges across diverse domains including social media sentiment evolution, supply chain anomaly detection, financial fraud networks, and biomedical pattern discovery. The course emphasizes advanced mining techniques including sequential pattern mining, graph mining, stream mining, and multi-dimensional association rule mining. Students develop end-to-end mining pipelines, from raw data ingestion through pattern discovery to actionable insights. Each team collaborates with industry partners or research organizations to address authentic problems requiring sophisticated mining approaches. The capstone project involves designing, implementing, and evaluating a complete mining solution that demonstrates mastery of multiple mining methodologies. Students present findings to stakeholder panels and submit work suitable for conference publication. Unlike traditional data science courses that cover broad analytical techniques, this course specifically focuses on the art and science of pattern discovery, anomaly detection, and knowledge extraction from complex data structures. The curriculum balances theoretical mining foundations with hands-on implementation using cutting-edge tools and frameworks for large-scale data mining applications.

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this course, students will be able to:

• Master advanced mining algorithms including sequential pattern mining, graph mining, and frequent itemset mining for complex data structures  
• Design and implement complete end-to-end mining pipelines that transform raw data into actionable business or research insights  
• Evaluate and compare multiple mining methodologies to select optimal approaches for specific problem domains and data characteristics  
• Collaborate effectively with external stakeholders to define mining objectives, validate results, and communicate findings to technical and non-technical audiences  
• Demonstrate professional competency by delivering publication-quality mining solutions that address real-world challenges in industry or research settings  

## Weekly Schedule

### Week 1: Foundations of Data Archaeology
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) with Python: Uncovering Data Stories
- Univariate Analysis - Statistical examination of individual variables including measures of central tendency, dispersion, and distribution shape
- Bivariate Analysis - Investigation of relationships between pairs of variables using correlation coefficients, cross-tabulations, and comparative visualizations

**Activity:** Interpreting Data Distribution Patterns Through Statistical Visualizations (90 minutes)

### Week 2: Data Preparation for Mining Operations
**Module:** Feature Engineering and Selection for Machine Learning
- Feature scaling and normalization - standardizing numerical features to improve model convergence and performance
- Categorical encoding strategies - methods to convert categorical variables into numerical representations suitable for machine learning algorithms

**Activity:** Evaluating Data Cleaning Approaches for Customer Purchase Dataset (75 minutes)

### Week 3: Advanced Feature Engineering
**Module:** Feature Engineering and Selection for Machine Learning
- Feature Transformation - Mathematical operations like scaling, log transforms, and polynomial features that modify existing variables to better capture relationships
- Dimensionality Reduction - Techniques like Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and t-SNE that reduce feature space while preserving important information

**Activity:** Interpreting Feature Correlation Patterns in Customer Churn Analysis (95 minutes)

### Week 4: Pattern Discovery Fundamentals
**Focus:** Sequential Pattern Mining and Frequent Itemset Mining
- Apriori algorithm and FP-Growth for association rule mining
- Sequential pattern mining algorithms (PrefixSpan, GSP)
- Applications in market basket analysis and user behavior

**Activity:** Interpreting Feature Importance Techniques in Complex Machine Learning Pipelines (150 minutes)

### Week 5: Graph Mining and Network Analysis
**Focus:** Complex Network Pattern Discovery
- Graph mining algorithms for social networks and knowledge graphs
- Community detection and centrality measures
- Anomaly detection in network structures

**Activity:** Interpreting Feature Correlation Heatmaps for Customer Churn Prediction (65 minutes)

### Week 6: Stream Mining and Real-Time Analytics
**Focus:** Dynamic Pattern Discovery
- Stream mining algorithms for continuous data
- Concept drift detection and adaptation
- Real-time anomaly detection systems

**Activity:** Evaluating Data Visualization Quality: Chart Type Selection Critique (75 minutes)

### Week 7: Multi-Dimensional Association Mining
**Focus:** Complex Pattern Relationships
- Multi-dimensional association rules
- Spatial and temporal pattern mining
- Cross-domain pattern discovery

**Activity:** Critical Evaluation of Machine Learning Model Performance in Healthcare Fraud Detection (180 minutes)

### Week 8: **Midterm Project Presentations**
Team presentations of initial mining pipeline implementations

### Week 9: Industry Partner Collaboration Begins
**Focus:** Real-World Problem Definition and Scoping
- Stakeholder requirement gathering
- Problem formulation for mining applications
- Data access and ethical considerations

### Week 10: Advanced Anomaly Detection
**Focus:** Sophisticated Outlier Discovery
- Statistical and machine learning approaches to anomaly detection
- Ensemble methods for robust detection
- Domain-specific anomaly patterns

**Activity:** Interpreting Deep Learning Model Interpretability Through SHAP Value Analysis (130 minutes)

### Week 11: Ensemble Mining Techniques
**Focus:** Combining Multiple Mining Approaches
- Voting and bagging for pattern discovery
- Stacking mining algorithms
- Hybrid mining frameworks

**Activity:** Evaluating Data Visualization Choices for Customer Sales Analysis (60 minutes)

### Week 12: Scalability and Big Data Mining
**Focus:** Large-Scale Pattern Discovery
- Distributed mining algorithms
- MapReduce and Spark for mining applications
- Cloud-based mining platforms

### Week 13: Evaluation and Validation of Mining Results
**Focus:** Assessing Mining Effectiveness
- Pattern quality metrics and validation techniques
- Statistical significance testing for discovered patterns
- Business impact assessment

### Week 14: Capstone Project Development
**Focus:** Final Implementation and Testing
- Integration of multiple mining techniques
- Performance optimization and scalability testing
- Preparation for stakeholder presentations

### Week 15: **Final Presentations and Industry Panel**
Capstone project presentations to industry partners and academic panel

## Assessment Plan

| Assessment | Type | Points | Week Due |
|------------|------|--------|----------|
| Customer Churn Analysis Lab Report | Lab Report | 100 | Week 4 |
| Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Models for Business Problem Solving | Discussion | 100 | Week 7 |
| Customer Churn Prediction and Business Impact Analysis | Project | 100 | Week 8 |
| End-to-End Data Science Project Presentation: Customer Churn Analysis | Presentation | 100 | Week 8 |
| Customer Churn Prediction: End-to-End Data Science Portfolio Project | Portfolio | 200 | Week 15 |
| **Industry Capstone Project** | **Project** | **300** | **Week 15** |

**Total Points: 900**

### Late Assignment Policy
Late submissions will be penalized 10% per day unless prior arrangements are made with the instructor. Industry presentation dates cannot be changed, and missing your team's presentation will result in a zero for that assignment.

### Team Collaboration
Students will work in teams of 3-4 for the capstone project. Team formation will occur in Week 2, and teams are expected to maintain consistent collaboration throughout the semester. Peer evaluation forms will be used to assess individual contributions to team projects.

### Industry Partnership Requirements
Teams working with industry partners must:
- Sign appropriate non-disclosure agreements
- Maintain professional communication standards
- Meet agreed-upon deadlines and deliverables
- Respect proprietary data and confidentiality requirements

### Technology Requirements
Students need access to:
- Python programming environment with data science libraries (pandas, scikit-learn, networkx, etc.)
- Cloud computing resources (provided through course accounts)
- Version control system (GitHub)
- Presentation software and video conferencing capabilities

### Final Project Publication Option
Outstanding capstone projects may be submitted to appropriate conferences or workshops with instructor guidance. Students retain ownership of their work while the university may use projects for promotional purposes with student consent.

# Machine Learning Lifecycle: From Raw Data to Production Models
**Course Number:** CS 3XX | **Credits:** 3 | **Semester:** Fall/Spring 2024

---

## Course Description

This foundational course guides students through the complete machine learning pipeline, emphasizing the practical journey from messy, real-world datasets to deployable predictive models. Students learn to navigate the iterative process of data collection, preprocessing, feature engineering, model selection, validation, and deployment while understanding the critical decisions that impact model performance. The course balances theoretical foundations with hands-on experience using industry-standard tools like Python, scikit-learn, and cloud platforms. 

Through project-based learning, students work with diverse datasets including text, images, and structured data to build classification, regression, and clustering models. Special attention is given to model evaluation, bias detection, interpretability, and ethical considerations in machine learning deployment. Students develop proficiency in version control for machine learning projects, automated testing of models, and basic MLOps practices. 

By course completion, students possess a comprehensive understanding of the machine learning workflow and can independently execute end-to-end projects. The curriculum emphasizes reproducible research practices, collaborative development, and the communication of technical findings to both technical and non-technical stakeholders, preparing students for data science roles in industry or advanced academic study.

---

## Learning Objectives

Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

• **Design and implement** complete machine learning pipelines from data ingestion through model deployment and monitoring  
• **Evaluate and compare** multiple machine learning algorithms using appropriate validation techniques and performance metrics  
• **Apply feature engineering** techniques and dimensionality reduction methods to improve model performance on real-world datasets  
• **Identify and mitigate bias** in machine learning models while implementing ethical AI practices  
• **Demonstrate proficiency** in MLOps fundamentals including version control, automated testing, and model versioning  

---

## Weekly Schedule

### Week 1: Course Introduction & ML Lifecycle Overview
**Topics:** Course overview, ML project lifecycle, setting up development environment  
**Module:** Introduction to Machine Learning Workflows  
**Activity:** Environment setup and first data exploration (60 minutes)  
**Due:** GitHub repository setup

### Week 2: Exploratory Data Analysis Fundamentals
**Topics:** Data profiling, statistical summaries, initial data assessment  
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) and Statistical Profiling  
**Concepts:** 
- Descriptive Statistics - measures of central tendency, dispersion, and shape
- Data Profiling - systematic examination of data completeness, uniqueness, validity  
**Activity:** Evaluating Data Quality Issues in Customer Purchase Dataset (60 minutes)  

### Week 3: Advanced EDA and Statistical Visualization
**Topics:** Distribution analysis, relationship identification, visualization best practices  
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis and Statistical Visualization  
**Concepts:**
- Data profiling - systematic examination of dataset structure and quality metrics
- Distribution analysis - understanding variables through histograms, box plots, statistical measures  
**Activity:** Comparing Data Visualization Types for Customer Purchase Pattern Analysis (60 minutes)  

### Week 4: Understanding Variable Relationships
**Topics:** Univariate, bivariate, and multivariate analysis techniques  
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) and Data Visualization Fundamentals  
**Concepts:**
- Univariate Analysis - statistical examination of individual variables
- Bivariate and Multivariate Analysis - investigation of relationships between variables  
**Activity:** Interpreting Correlation Matrices and Identifying Feature Relationships (60 minutes)  
**Due:** EDA Project Milestone

### Week 5: Data Preprocessing and Cleaning
**Topics:** Missing data strategies, outlier detection, data validation  
**Module:** Feature Engineering for Machine Learning  
**Concepts:**
- Missing Data Imputation - strategies including deletion methods, statistical and predictive imputation
- Feature Scaling and Normalization - standardization techniques for ML algorithms  
**Activity:** Evaluating Data Cleaning Approaches for Customer Survey Analysis (90 minutes)

### Week 6: Feature Engineering Fundamentals
**Topics:** Feature scaling, normalization, categorical encoding  
**Module:** Feature Engineering and Selection for Machine Learning  
**Concepts:**
- Feature scaling and normalization - StandardScaler, MinMaxScaler, RobustScaler techniques
- Categorical encoding methods - one-hot encoding, target encoding, ordinal encoding  
**Activity:** Hands-on feature engineering workshop (90 minutes)  
**Assessment:** Customer Churn Prediction EDA Quiz (100 points)

### Week 7: Advanced Feature Engineering
**Topics:** Feature creation, mathematical transformations, interaction terms  
**Module:** Feature Engineering for Predictive Modeling  
**Concepts:**
- Feature Creation - mathematical transformations, binning strategies, interaction terms
- Feature Selection Methods - filter, wrapper, and embedded methods  
**Activity:** Feature engineering competition (120 minutes)

### Week 8: Model Selection and Training
**Topics:** Algorithm selection, hyperparameter tuning, cross-validation  
**Concepts:** Supervised learning algorithms, model complexity, training procedures  
**Activity:** Model comparison workshop (90 minutes)  
**Due:** Feature Engineering Assignment

### Week 9: Model Evaluation and Validation
**Topics:** Performance metrics, validation strategies, statistical significance testing  
**Concepts:** Confusion matrices, ROC curves, precision-recall, validation techniques  
**Activity:** Understanding Bias-Variance Tradeoff Analysis (70 minutes)

### Week 10: Model Interpretation and Explainability
**Topics:** Feature importance, SHAP values, model interpretability techniques  
**Concepts:** Global vs local explanations, interpretation methods for different algorithms  
**Activity:** Interpreting Feature Importance in Ensemble Models (3.5 hours)  
**Assessment:** Ethics in Machine Learning Discussion (100 points)

### Week 11: Bias Detection and Ethical AI
**Topics:** Algorithmic bias, fairness metrics, ethical considerations in ML  
**Concepts:** Types of bias, fairness definitions, mitigation strategies  
**Activity:** Critical Evaluation of ML Models in Healthcare (2.5 hours)

### Week 12: Model Deployment Fundamentals
**Topics:** MLOps introduction, model versioning, deployment strategies  
**Concepts:** CI/CD for ML, containerization, model monitoring  
**Activity:** Basic model deployment exercise (2 hours)  
**Due:** Mid-term Project Checkpoint

### Week 13: Advanced MLOps and Monitoring  
**Topics:** Model monitoring, performance tracking, automated retraining  
**Concepts:** Drift detection, A/B testing, production ML systems  
**Activity:** Setting up model monitoring pipeline (2 hours)

### Week 14: Production Considerations and Scaling
**Topics:** Scalability, reliability, maintenance of ML systems  
**Concepts:** Infrastructure considerations, cost optimization, system design  
**Activity:** Critical Evaluation of Predictive Models for Business Impact (3.5 hours)  
**Assessment:** Customer Churn Prediction Exam (100 points)

### Week 15: Project Presentations and Course Review
**Topics:** Student project presentations, course synthesis, industry trends  
**Activity:** Final project presentations and peer review  
**Due:** End-to-End Data Science Project Portfolio (100 points)
