# COURSE SYLLABUS

## CS 3450: Extracting Intelligence from Raw Data: Advanced Mining Techniques for Business Analytics

**Semester:** Fall 2024  
**Credits:** 3  
**Prerequisites:** CS 2250 (Data Structures), STAT 2600 (Statistics), CS 2800 (Database Systems)  
**Meeting Time:** MWF 10:00-10:50 AM  

---

## COURSE DESCRIPTION

This comprehensive course transforms students into data archaeologists capable of unearthing valuable insights from complex, unstructured datasets. Students will master the art and science of extracting actionable intelligence from diverse data sources including social media streams, sensor networks, transaction logs, and multimedia content. The curriculum integrates cutting-edge mining algorithms with real-world business scenarios, covering pattern recognition, anomaly detection, predictive modeling, and knowledge discovery processes. Students will work with industry-standard tools and frameworks to implement end-to-end mining pipelines, from data ingestion and preprocessing to model deployment and visualization. Through hands-on projects with partner organizations, learners will tackle authentic challenges such as customer behavior analysis, fraud detection, market trend identification, and operational optimization. The course emphasizes both technical proficiency and strategic thinking, preparing students to communicate mining results effectively to stakeholders and translate discoveries into business value. By semester's end, students will possess a comprehensive toolkit for transforming raw data into competitive advantage.

## LEARNING OBJECTIVES

By the end of this course, students will be able to:

• Master advanced data mining algorithms including clustering, classification, association rules, and sequential pattern mining for diverse data types
• Apply comprehensive end-to-end mining workflows from data acquisition through model validation to business insight generation  
• Develop practical expertise in implementing scalable mining solutions using distributed computing frameworks and cloud-based platforms

**Textbooks:**
- *Data Mining: Concepts and Techniques* by Han, Kamber & Pei (4th Edition)
- *Python for Data Analysis* by Wes McKinney (3rd Edition)

- Python 3.9+ with Anaconda distribution
- Jupyter Notebooks
- Apache Spark (provided via university cluster)
- Tableau (student license provided)

**Hardware:**
- Laptop capable of running Python and Jupyter Notebooks
- Minimum 8GB RAM recommended

---

- Feature Selection: Statistical methods to identify predictive features while reducing dimensionality
**Activities:**
- Interpreting Feature Engineering Impact Through Correlation Matrix Decomposition (130 min)

### Week 5: Advanced Feature Engineering

# Business Intelligence Through Data Storytelling: Analytics Across Industries

**Course Code:** DS 3XX  
**Credits:** 3  
**Prerequisites:** Introduction to Statistics, Fundamentals of Data Science  
**Meeting Time:** MWF 10:00-10:50 AM  

---

## Instructor Information

---

## Course Description

This survey course explores how data analytics transforms decision-making across diverse industry sectors, emphasizing the art and science of extracting actionable insights from complex datasets. Students will examine real-world analytics applications spanning healthcare, finance, retail, entertainment, sports, and public policy. The course adopts a storytelling framework, teaching students to identify compelling narratives hidden within data and communicate findings effectively to non-technical stakeholders. Through case studies, interactive visualizations, and hands-on projects using industry-standard tools, students will discover how different sectors approach similar analytical challenges using varied methodologies. Topics include predictive modeling for customer behavior, operational analytics for supply chain optimization, sentiment analysis for brand management, risk assessment frameworks, and performance metrics design. Students will develop a comprehensive understanding of the analytics landscape while building practical skills in data interpretation, visualization design, and strategic recommendation formulation. The course emphasizes critical thinking about data quality, ethical considerations, and the limitations of analytical models in different organizational contexts.

---

## Learning Objectives

Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

• **Evaluate and compare** analytics methodologies across different industry sectors and organizational contexts  
• **Design compelling data narratives** that effectively communicate analytical insights to diverse stakeholder audiences  
• **Apply survey-level knowledge** of business intelligence tools and techniques to solve cross-industry analytical challenges  
• **Critically assess** the ethical implications and limitations of data-driven decision making in various professional settings  
• **Synthesize analytical findings** into strategic recommendations that drive organizational value and competitive advantage

**Meeting Time:** TuTh 2:00-3:30 PM

## Course Description

This hands-on course treats digital interactions as archaeological artifacts, teaching students to excavate meaningful behavioral patterns from the vast data trails left by human-computer interactions. Students will learn specialized mining techniques to uncover hidden user behaviors, interaction patterns, and digital footprints across web analytics, mobile app usage, gaming platforms, and social media interfaces. The course emphasizes real-world applications including user experience optimization, digital marketing personalization, cybersecurity threat detection, and accessibility improvement. Through partnerships with local businesses and organizations, students will work with actual datasets to solve genuine problems such as reducing shopping cart abandonment, improving educational software engagement, or identifying fraudulent online behaviors. The curriculum combines traditional data mining algorithms with cutting-edge techniques like sequence mining, clickstream analysis, and temporal pattern discovery. Students will master tools including R, Python, Tableau, and specialized HCI analytics platforms while developing a portfolio of applied projects that demonstrate their ability to transform raw interaction data into actionable business intelligence and user experience insights.

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this course, students will be able to:

1. **Master specialized mining techniques** for extracting behavioral patterns from clickstreams, user sessions, and interaction sequences
2. **Apply temporal data mining methods** to real-world HCI datasets from industry partners to solve authentic business problems
3. **Develop practical expertise** in translating discovered interaction patterns into actionable recommendations for UX design, marketing strategies, and system optimization

**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) with Python

  - Data profiling: Systematic examination of dataset structure, completeness, and basic statistical properties

- **Readings:** Course packet Ch. 1-2

**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis and Data Visualization with Python

- **Activity:** Interpreting Feature Correlation Heatmaps in Customer Behavior Analysis (65 minutes)
- **Readings:** Course packet Ch. 3

### Week 3: Statistical Foundations for Behavioral Pattern Discovery
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) with Statistical Visualization
- **Topics:**
  - Descriptive Statistics - measures of central tendency, variability, and distribution shape for summarizing data

### Week 4: Multi-dimensional Interaction Analysis

- **Topics:**
  - Univariate analysis - examination of individual variables including measures of central tendency, dispersion, and distribution shape

- **Activity:** Interpreting Correlation vs. Causation in Real-World Marketing Dataset Analysis (60 minutes)
- **Readings:** Course packet Ch. 4-5

### Week 5: Advanced Pattern Recognition in User Data
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) and Data Visualization
- **Topics:**
  - Univariate Analysis - Statistical summaries and distributions of individual variables including measures of central tendency, dispersion, and shape
  - Bivariate and Multivariate Analysis - Examining relationships between two or more variables using correlation analysis, cross-tabulations, and scatter plot matrices
- **Activity:** Interpreting Correlation vs. Causation in Real-World Data Scenarios (50 minutes)

### Week 6: Preparing HCI Data for Mining
**Module:** Feature Engineering for Machine Learning
- **Topics:**
  - Feature scaling and normalization - techniques to standardize numerical features including min-max scaling, z-score normalization, and robust scaling methods
  - Categorical encoding strategies - methods for converting categorical variables including one-hot encoding, target encoding, frequency encoding, and embedding approaches
- **Activity:** Evaluating Data Visualization Effectiveness: Chart Type Selection Critique (45 minutes)
- **Assessment:** Exploratory Data Analysis and Basic Statistics Exam (100 points)

### Week 7: Advanced Feature Engineering for Behavioral Data
**Module:** Feature Engineering and Selection for Machine Learning
- **Topics:**
  - Feature transformation - Converting raw data into numerical representations suitable for ML algorithms through scaling, encoding, and mathematical transformations
  - Dimensionality reduction - Reducing the number of features while preserving information content using statistical and algorithmic approaches
- **Activity:** Interpreting Advanced A/B Test Results with Multiple Confounding Variables and Statistical Nuances (115 minutes)

### Week 8: **MIDTERM WEEK** - Industry Partner Project Launch
- Project team formation
- Dataset introduction from industry partners
- **Assessment:** Predictive Analytics Case Study: Customer Churn Analysis Presentation (100 points)

### Week 9: Temporal Patterns and Sequence Mining

# COURSE SYLLABUS

## CSE 4820: Scalable Data Ecosystems: Engineering Insights from Terabytes to Petabytes

**Department:** Computer Science and Engineering  
**Level:** Undergraduate (Senior-level)  
**Credits:** 3 credit hours  
**Duration:** 15-week semester  
**Prerequisites:** CSE 3530 (Database Systems), CSE 3720 (Data Structures and Algorithms), STAT 3010 (Statistics for Data Science)

### INSTRUCTOR INFORMATION

---

## COURSE DESCRIPTION

This comprehensive course bridges the gap between traditional data science and industrial-scale data engineering, focusing on the complete lifecycle of massive datasets. Students will navigate the complexities of distributed computing architectures, real-time streaming analytics, and cloud-native data pipelines while solving authentic business problems with datasets exceeding conventional memory limits. The curriculum emphasizes hands-on experience with Apache Spark, Kafka, and Hadoop ecosystems, combined with advanced machine learning techniques optimized for big data environments. Students will design fault-tolerant systems, implement data lakes and warehouses, and master the art of horizontal scaling. Through industry partnerships, learners will work with real-world datasets from telecommunications, e-commerce, and IoT sensors, developing expertise in data ingestion, transformation, and visualization at enterprise scale. The course culminates in a capstone project where teams architect complete data solutions handling multi-terabyte datasets, incorporating MLOps practices, monitoring systems, and cost optimization strategies essential for production environments.

## LEARNING OBJECTIVES

Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

1. **Master Distributed Computing Frameworks:** Students will master distributed computing frameworks and design scalable data processing pipelines capable of handling petabyte-scale datasets
2. **Apply Big Data Architectures:** Students will apply comprehensive big data architectures including batch and stream processing to solve complex real-world analytical challenges
3. **Develop Production-Ready Systems:** Students will develop practical expertise in cloud-native data engineering tools and implement production-ready machine learning systems with automated monitoring and deployment

---

## WEEKLY SCHEDULE

### Week 1: Foundations of Scalable Data Analysis
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis and Visualization with Python
- **Concepts:**
  - Descriptive statistics - measures of central tendency (mean, median, mode), dispersion (variance, standard deviation, IQR), and shape (skewness, kurtosis)
  - Data profiling - systematic assessment of data quality including completeness, consistency, validity, and accuracy across dataset dimensions
- **Activities:**

# Visual Storytelling with Data: From Raw Numbers to Compelling Narratives

**Course Code:** DS 4950  
**Credits:** 3  
**Prerequisites:** Statistical Analysis (DS 3200), Data Visualization Fundamentals (DS 3400), Database Management (DS 2800)  
**Meeting Time:** Tuesdays & Thursdays, 2:00-3:30 PM  
**Semester:** Spring 2024  

## Instructor Information
**Response Time:** Within 24 hours on weekdays, 48 hours on weekends  

## Course Description
This capstone course transforms students into data storytellers who can craft compelling visual narratives from complex datasets. Students work with real-world client projects to design and implement comprehensive data visualization solutions that drive decision-making. The course emphasizes the intersection of cognitive psychology, design principles, and statistical communication to create impactful visual stories. Students master advanced visualization tools including D3.js, Tableau, and Python's visualization ecosystem while learning to critically evaluate visual design choices. The capstone project involves partnering with local organizations, nonprofits, or businesses to solve authentic problems through visual data analysis. Students present their work through interactive dashboards, infographic series, and data-driven presentations to stakeholder audiences. The curriculum integrates ethical considerations in data representation, accessibility in visual design, and cross-cultural communication through data. By semester's end, students will have built a professional portfolio demonstrating their ability to transform raw data into actionable insights through thoughtful, evidence-based visual communication that serves real organizational needs.

## Learning Objectives
By the end of this course, students will be able to:

1. **Design and implement interactive dashboards and data visualizations** that effectively communicate complex analytical findings to diverse stakeholder audiences
2. **Apply cognitive psychology and design principles** to create accessible, ethically-responsible visual narratives that avoid misrepresentation and bias in data storytelling
3. **Complete a client-based capstone project** demonstrating professional competency in visual data analysis, stakeholder communication, and project management skills

## Weekly Schedule

### Week 1-2: Foundation - Understanding Data Through Visual Exploration
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) and Data Visualization
- **Concepts:**
  - Descriptive Statistics: Measures of central tendency, variability, and distribution shape including mean, median, mode, standard deviation, quartiles, and skewness
  - Data Quality Assessment: Techniques for identifying and handling missing values, outliers, duplicates, and inconsistencies in real-world datasets
  - Univariate Analysis - Statistical examination of individual variables including measures of central tendency, dispersion, and distribution shape
  - Correlation vs Causation - Understanding the critical distinction between variables that move together versus those with causal relationships

**Activities:**
- Week 1: Interpreting Feature Correlation Patterns in Customer Purchase Data (55 min)
- Week 2: Evaluating Data Visualization Effectiveness for Customer Survey Analysis (75 min)

### Week 3-4: Data Preparation for Visual Storytelling
**Module:** Feature Engineering and Selection for Predictive Modeling
- **Concepts:**
  - Feature transformation - Converting raw variables into more useful representations through scaling, normalization, encoding, and mathematical transformations
  - Feature selection methods - Filter methods (correlation, chi-square), wrapper methods (recursive feature elimination), and embedded methods (L1/L2 regularization)
  - Feature scaling and normalization - standardizing numerical features to similar ranges using techniques like StandardScaler, MinMaxScaler, and RobustScaler
  - Categorical encoding methods - converting categorical variables to numerical format using one-hot encoding, target encoding, and embedding techniques

**Activities:**
- Week 3: Interpreting Customer Segmentation Results from K-Means Clustering Analysis (60 min)
- Week 4: Evaluating Data Visualization Effectiveness for Sales Dashboard Design (50 min)

**Assessment:** Data Science Fundamentals Quiz: Exploring Customer Purchase Patterns (Week 4)

### Week 5-6: Advanced Visual Analysis Techniques
**Module:** Advanced Feature Engineering for Visual Analytics
- **Concepts:**
  - Feature Engineering: The process of creating new features from existing data through mathematical transformations, domain knowledge, and statistical techniques
  - Feature Selection: Methods for identifying the most relevant subset of features including univariate selection, recursive feature elimination, and regularization-based approaches
  - Mathematical transformations for visualization clarity
  - Handling complex categorical relationships in visual contexts

**Activities:**
- Week 5: Interpreting Feature Correlation Patterns in Customer Churn Analysis (60 min)
- Week 6: Interpreting Bias-Variance Tradeoff Through Cross-Validation Learning Curves Analysis (85 min)

### Week 7-8: Client Project Initiation & Stakeholder Analysis
**Focus:** Real-world client project begins, stakeholder interviews, project scoping
- Client matching and project proposal development
- Stakeholder analysis and communication planning
- Data audit and visualization strategy design
- Ethics and bias consideration workshops

**Activities:**
- Week 7: Critical Evaluation of Machine Learning Model Selection for Imbalanced Healthcare Dataset (140 min)
- Week 8: Evaluating Data Visualization Effectiveness for Customer Sales Analysis (55 min)

**Assessment:** Fundamentals of Data Science: Practical Analysis Exam (Week 8)

### Week 9-10: Interactive Dashboard Development
**Focus:** Advanced visualization tools (D3.js, Tableau, Python ecosystem)
- Dashboard design principles and user experience
- Interactive visualization techniques
- Performance optimization for large datasets
- Cross-platform compatibility considerations

**Activities:**
- Week 9: Interpreting Bias-Variance Decomposition in Ensemble Model Performance (90 min)
- Week 10: Critical Evaluation of Machine Learning Model Deployment Strategies for Real-World Business Impact (160 min)

### Week 11-12: Visual Design Psychology & Accessibility
**Focus:** Cognitive psychology in data visualization, accessibility standards
- Color theory and cultural considerations
- Accessibility compliance (WCAG guidelines)
- Cognitive load optimization
- Cross-cultural visual communication

**Mid-term Project Check-in:** Client project progress presentations

### Week 13-14: Ethical Data Storytelling & Bias Mitigation
**Focus:** Ethics in data representation, avoiding misleading visualizations
- Identifying and preventing visual bias
- Transparency in data limitations
- Responsible storytelling practices
- Legal and ethical frameworks

**Assessment:** Predictive Analytics Case Study Presentation (Week 14)

### Week 15: Capstone Project Completion & Portfolio Development
**Focus:** Final client project completion, portfolio assembly
- Client deliverable finalization
- Professional portfolio development
- Peer review and feedback sessions
- Industry presentation preparation

### Week 16: Final Presentations & Professional Showcase
**Focus:** Client presentations, industry stakeholder showcase
- Client project presentations to real stakeholders
- Portfolio presentations to industry professionals
- Course reflection and career planning
- Professional network building event

**Assessment:** End-to-End Predictive Analytics Portfolio: Customer Churn Prevention System (Due Week 16)
**Assessment:** End-to-End Machine Learning Pipeline for Customer Churn Prediction (Due Week 16)

# Statistical Modeling for Business Intelligence and Decision Analytics
**Course Code:** DS 3XX | **Credits:** 3 | **Semester:** Fall/Spring 2024

## Course Description

This applied course bridges statistical theory and business decision-making through hands-on modeling experiences. Students work with real corporate datasets to build predictive models, conduct A/B testing, and perform customer segmentation using advanced statistical techniques. The curriculum emphasizes practical implementation of regression analysis, time series forecasting, hypothesis testing, and Bayesian inference within business contexts. Students learn to communicate statistical findings to non-technical stakeholders through compelling visualizations and executive summaries. Key applications include sales forecasting, customer lifetime value prediction, market basket analysis, and operational optimization. The course features guest lectures from industry practitioners and culminates in a capstone project where students solve actual business problems using statistical modeling.

## Learning Objectives

Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

• Master advanced statistical modeling techniques including regression, time series analysis, and Bayesian methods for business applications  
• Apply hypothesis testing and experimental design principles to conduct meaningful A/B tests and market research studies  
• Develop expertise in model validation, assumption checking, and uncertainty quantification for reliable business predictions  
• Create compelling statistical visualizations and executive reports that communicate insights to business stakeholders  
• Design and implement complete statistical workflows from data collection through model deployment using R and Python

## Weekly Schedule

**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis and Data Visualization

- **Activity:** Interpreting Data Distribution Patterns in Customer Purchase Behavior (70 min)
- 
### Week 3-4: Data Preparation for Statistical Modeling
**Module:** Feature Engineering and Selection for Machine Learning
- **Topics:** Feature scaling, normalization, categorical encoding methods
- **Activity:** Interpreting Feature Correlation Heatmaps in Customer Churn Analysis (55 min)

### Week 5-6: Statistical Inference for Business

- **Activity:** Interpreting Statistical Significance in A/B Test Results for E-commerce Conversion Rates (60 min)
- 
### Week 7-8: Regression Analysis and Applications
- **Topics:** Linear/multiple regression, logistic regression, model assumptions
- **Activity:** Interpreting Feature Importance in Machine Learning Models Using Real Estate Data (125 min)
- 
### Week 9: Midterm Examination Period
- **Assessment:** Customer Churn Prediction Analysis Exam

### Week 10-11: Advanced Statistical Modeling
- **Topics:** Time series forecasting, seasonal decomposition, ARIMA models
- **Activity:** Interpreting Correlation vs. Causation Through Real Estate Market Analysis (85 min)
- 
### Week 12-13: Customer Analytics and Segmentation
- **Topics:** Customer lifetime value, RFM analysis, clustering techniques
- **Activity:** Interpreting Customer Churn Patterns Through Exploratory Data Analysis Visualizations (75 min)
- 
### Week 14: Bayesian Methods and Uncertainty Quantification
- **Topics:** Bayesian inference, prior/posterior distributions, credible intervals
- **Activity:** Interpreting Distribution Patterns in Real Estate Price Data (85 min)
- 
### Week 15: Ethics and Model Deployment
- **Topics:** Algorithmic bias, model interpretability, deployment considerations
- **Discussion:** Ethical AI and Algorithmic Bias Mitigation Strategy
- **Presentations:** Final project presentations

### Week 16: Finals Week
- **Due:** Final project reports and portfolios

# Streaming Analytics and Real-Time Decision Systems
**Course Code:** DS 4XX | **Credits:** 3 | **Semester:** Fall/Spring 2024

## Course Description

This specialized course focuses on the design, implementation, and optimization of real-time data processing systems that handle continuous streams of big data. Students will master the complexities of processing massive volumes of data as it arrives, learning to build systems that make instantaneous decisions from live data feeds. The course emphasizes practical applications in domains such as financial trading algorithms, IoT sensor networks, social media monitoring, and fraud detection systems. Students will work with industry-standard streaming platforms including Apache Kafka, Apache Storm, and Apache Flink, while developing expertise in stream processing architectures, windowing techniques, and low-latency analytics. The curriculum combines theoretical foundations of distributed computing with hands-on projects involving real-world streaming datasets. Advanced topics include complex event processing, stream joins, backpressure handling, and fault-tolerant stream processing. By course completion, students will have built end-to-end streaming analytics pipelines capable of processing millions of events per second, preparing them for roles in high-velocity data environments where traditional batch processing approaches are inadequate.

## Learning Objectives

Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

1. **Design and implement distributed streaming data architectures** capable of processing high-velocity big data in real-time
2. **Master advanced stream processing techniques** including windowing, watermarking, and stateful computations for continuous analytics  
3. **Develop expertise in building fault-tolerant, scalable streaming systems** using industry-standard platforms and evaluate performance trade-offs in real-time decision making

## Weekly Schedule

### Week 1: Foundations of Data Analysis for Streaming Systems
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis and Data Visualization Fundamentals
- Data profiling: Systematic examination of dataset structure, completeness, and quality including missing value patterns and data type validation
- Distribution analysis: Understanding data spread, central tendency, skewness, and kurtosis through histograms, box plots, and statistical measures
- **Activity:** Interpreting Data Distribution Patterns Using Real-World Sales Dataset (90 min)
- **Reading:** Course packet Ch. 1-2

### Week 2: Feature Engineering for Real-Time Analytics
**Module:** Feature Engineering and Selection for Machine Learning  
- Feature Engineering: The process of creating new features from existing data through mathematical transformations, domain knowledge application, and data combination techniques
- Feature Selection: Statistical and algorithmic methods for identifying the most relevant subset of features, including filter, wrapper, and embedded methods
- **Activity:** Interpreting Feature Correlation Patterns in Customer Purchase Data (65 min)
- **Reading:** Course packet Ch. 3

### Week 3: Introduction to Streaming Data and Real-Time Processing
- Batch vs. Stream processing paradigms
- Characteristics of streaming data: velocity, volume, variety
- Real-time vs. near-real-time processing requirements
- **Activity:** Setting up streaming data simulation environments
- **Reading:** Textbook Ch. 1-2

### Week 4: Stream Processing Architectures and Patterns
- Lambda and Kappa architectures
- Event-driven architectures
- Microservices for streaming applications
- **Activity:** Designing architecture for IoT sensor network
- **Reading:** Textbook Ch. 3

### Week 5: Apache Kafka Fundamentals
- Kafka architecture: topics, partitions, producers, consumers
- Message ordering and delivery guarantees
- Kafka Connect and Schema Registry
- - **Reading:** Kafka documentation

### Week 6: Stream Processing with Apache Flink
- Flink runtime architecture and execution model
- DataStream API fundamentals
- Time semantics and watermarks
- **Activity:** Interpreting Statistical Relationships in Customer Churn Analysis (85 min)
- **Reading:** Textbook Ch. 4-5

### Week 7: Windowing and Time-Based Operations
- Tumbling, sliding, and session windows
- Event time vs. processing time
- Late data handling strategies
- - **Reading:** Textbook Ch. 6

### Week 8: Stateful Stream Processing
- Managed state in stream processing
- Keyed state and operator state
- State backends and checkpointing
- **Activity:** Interpreting Correlation vs. Causation Through Real Estate Data Analysis (85 min)
- **Assessment:** Advanced Machine Learning Model Evaluation and Optimization Quiz (100 pts)

### Week 9: Complex Event Processing (CEP)
- Pattern detection in event streams
- CEP libraries and frameworks
- Use cases: fraud detection, system monitoring
- - **Reading:** Research papers on CEP

### Week 10: Stream Joins and Multi-Stream Processing
- Stream-stream joins
- Stream-table joins
- Temporal joins and their challenges
- **Activity:** Interpreting Feature Importance in Random Forest Models (60 min)
- **Reading:** Textbook Ch. 7

### Week 11: Fault Tolerance and Exactly-Once Processing
- Checkpointing mechanisms
- Exactly-once semantic guarantees
- Recovery strategies
- - **Assessment:** Feature Engineering Strategy Discussion: Customer Churn Prediction (100 pts)

### Week 12: Performance Optimization and Monitoring
- Backpressure handling
- Resource allocation and scaling
- Monitoring streaming applications
- **Activity:** Interpreting Statistical Distributions in Real Estate Price Data (75 min)
- **Reading:** Performance tuning guides

### Week 13: Advanced Topics and Industry Applications
- Machine learning on streaming data
- Edge computing and streaming
- Industry case studies
- **Assessment:** Customer Purchase Behavior Analysis Project Due (100 pts)

### Week 14: Project Presentations and Integration
- Student project presentations
- Integration patterns and best practices
- Future trends in streaming analytics
- **Assessment:** End-to-End Machine Learning Pipeline Presentation (100 pts)

### Week 15: Course Review and Final Project
- Comprehensive review of concepts
- Troubleshooting streaming systems
- **Assessment:** End-to-End Customer Churn Prediction Portfolio Project Due (100 pts)

### Week 16: Finals Week
- Final project demonstrations
- Peer review sessions

context.course_description: This course explores the theoretical underpinnings of predictive modeling through rigorous mathematical frameworks. Students delve into the geometric interpretations of high-dimensional data spaces, examining how different model architectures navigate bias-variance trade-offs through mathematical lens. The curriculum emphasizes understanding why certain models work rather than simply how to implement them. Topics include convex optimization theory in machine learning, statistical learning theory, information-theoretic approaches to model selection, and the mathematical foundations of regularization techniques. Students analyze the theoretical guarantees of various algorithms, exploring convergence properties, generalization bounds, and computational complexity. The course bridges abstract mathematical concepts with practical modeling decisions, examining how theoretical insights inform model architecture choices. Through rigorous proofs and mathematical derivations, students develop intuition for model behavior in different data scenarios. Special attention is given to understanding loss function geometry, optimization landscapes, and the mathematical principles governing ensemble methods. This theoretical foundation enables students to design novel modeling approaches and critically evaluate existing methodologies from first principles rather than empirical observation alone.

# Course Syllabus

## Statistical Inference and Uncertainty Quantification in Data-Driven Decision Making

**Course Code:** DSCI 3XXX  
**Credits:** 3  
**Prerequisites:** Calculus III, Linear Algebra, Probability Theory, Introduction to Statistics  
**Semester:** Fall/Spring 2024  
**Meeting Time:** MWF 10:00-10:50 AM  

---

## Course Description

This course explores the theoretical foundations of statistical inference as applied to modern data science challenges, with particular emphasis on uncertainty quantification and probabilistic reasoning. Students will delve into advanced statistical theory including asymptotic analysis, convergence theorems, and the mathematical properties of estimators in high-dimensional settings. The curriculum emphasizes rigorous mathematical treatment of hypothesis testing, confidence intervals, and Bayesian inference within the context of big data environments. Key topics include multiple testing corrections, empirical process theory, concentration inequalities, and the statistical theory underlying machine learning algorithms. Students will analyze the theoretical guarantees and limitations of popular data science methods, examining when and why these methods succeed or fail from a statistical perspective. The course bridges classical statistical theory with contemporary challenges in data science, including non-parametric inference, robust statistics, and the interplay between computational constraints and statistical optimality. Through mathematical proofs, theoretical exercises, and conceptual problem-solving, students develop a deep understanding of the statistical principles that govern reliable inference from data.

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this course, students will be able to:

• Master advanced statistical inference theory including asymptotic properties of estimators and convergence theorems in high-dimensional settings
• Apply theoretical frameworks to analyze the statistical properties and limitations of machine learning algorithms and data science methodologies  
• Develop expertise in uncertainty quantification, multiple testing procedures, and Bayesian inference for complex data structures

## Weekly Schedule

### Week 1: Foundations of Statistical Data Analysis
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis and Statistical Visualization  
**Concepts:**
- Descriptive Statistics - measures of central tendency, variability, and distribution shape including mean, median, mode, standard deviation, quartiles, and skewness
- Data Profiling - systematic examination of data quality, completeness, consistency, and validity including missing value patterns and outlier detection

**Activity:** Interpreting Data Distribution Patterns in Customer Purchase Behavior (85 minutes)

### Week 2: Advanced Exploratory Analysis
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis and Data Visualization  
**Concepts:**
- Univariate Analysis - Statistical examination of individual variables including measures of central tendency, dispersion, and distribution shape
- Bivariate and Multivariate Analysis - Investigation of relationships between two or more variables using correlation matrices, cross-tabulations, and scatter plot matrices

**Activity:** Interpreting Correlation vs. Causation Through Real-World Data Scenarios (90 minutes)

### Week 3: Statistical Foundations and Data Quality
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis and Data Visualization  
**Concepts:**
- Descriptive Statistics: Measures of central tendency, variability, and distribution shape including mean, median, standard deviation, skewness, and kurtosis
- Data Quality Assessment: Systematic identification of missing values, duplicates, outliers, and inconsistencies that may impact analysis reliability

**Activity:** Evaluating Data Cleaning Approaches for Customer Survey Analysis (85 minutes)

### Week 4: Feature Engineering Theory
**Module:** Feature Engineering for Machine Learning Models  
**Concepts:**
- Data Leakage: The inadvertent inclusion of information from the future or target variable in training features, leading to overly optimistic model performance estimates
- Feature Scaling: Normalizing features to similar ranges using standardization (z-score) or min-max scaling to prevent features with larger magnitudes from dominating model training

**Activity:** Evaluating Data Visualization Quality: Chart Type Selection and Design Assessment (45 minutes)

**Assessment:** Customer Churn Analysis and Prediction Quiz (100 points)

### Week 5: Advanced Feature Engineering
**Module:** Feature Engineering and Selection for Predictive Modeling  
**Concepts:**
- Feature Creation - Mathematical transformations, polynomial features, binning, and encoding techniques to generate new variables from existing data
- Feature Selection - Statistical and algorithmic methods (correlation analysis, mutual information, LASSO, RFE) to identify most predictive variables

**Activity:** Evaluating Data Cleaning Approaches for Customer Purchase Dataset (95 minutes)

### Week 6: Statistical Bias and Healthcare Data
**Module:** Advanced Statistical Theory in Data Applications  
**Focus:** Bias identification and correction in high-stakes domains

**Activity:** Interpreting Statistical Bias in Real-World Healthcare Datasets (70 minutes)

### Week 7: Bias-Variance Decomposition
**Module:** Model Performance Theory  
**Focus:** Theoretical understanding of model complexity trade-offs

**Activity:** Interpreting Bias-Variance Decomposition in Cross-Validated Model Performance (90 minutes)

### Week 8: Midterm Examination
**Assessment:** Customer Churn Prediction Analysis Exam (100 points)

### Week 9: Multiple Testing and Statistical Significance
**Module:** Advanced Hypothesis Testing Theory  
**Focus:** Controlling Type I error in multiple comparisons

**Activity:** Interpreting Statistical Significance in A/B Test Results with Multiple Testing Corrections (95 minutes)

### Week 10: Model Selection Theory
**Module:** Decision Theory in Model Selection  
**Focus:** Statistical criteria for model comparison

**Activity:** Evaluating Machine Learning Model Selection for Real-World Business Impact: A Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (120 minutes)

### Week 11: Advanced Model Evaluation
**Module:** Comprehensive Model Assessment  
**Focus:** Beyond accuracy: statistical guarantees and uncertainty

**Activity:** Evaluating and Defending Model Selection for Customer Churn Prediction (140 minutes)

### Week 12: Portfolio Development Week
**Focus:** Integration of theoretical concepts into practical applications

**Assessment:** Beginner Data Science Portfolio: Customer Shopping Analysis (100 points)

### Week 13: Project Development
**Focus:** End-to-end statistical analysis with uncertainty quantification

# Distributed Computing Paradigms for Massive Dataset Analysis
**CS 4XX | Data Science Program | Fall 2024**

---

## Course Description

This course explores the theoretical foundations and computational architectures that enable analysis of petabyte-scale datasets across distributed systems. Students examine the mathematical principles underlying MapReduce, Apache Spark, and emerging distributed computing frameworks, focusing on algorithmic complexity, fault tolerance mechanisms, and scalability theory. The curriculum emphasizes theoretical models of parallel computation, distributed consensus algorithms, and the mathematical trade-offs between consistency, availability, and partition tolerance in big data systems. Students analyze case studies from genomics, social networks, and IoT sensor networks to understand how theoretical concepts translate to real-world distributed data processing challenges. Topics include distributed hash tables, consistent hashing, Byzantine fault tolerance, streaming algorithms, and approximate computing methods. The course develops deep understanding of how data partitioning strategies, load balancing algorithms, and network topology affect computational efficiency in massive-scale analytics. Students engage with research papers on cutting-edge distributed systems and explore theoretical limitations of current big data architectures, preparing them to design novel solutions for next-generation data processing challenges.

---

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this course, students will be able to:

• Master theoretical principles of distributed computing architectures and their application to massive dataset processing  
• Apply mathematical models of parallel computation to analyze algorithmic complexity and scalability in big data systems  
• Develop expertise in distributed consensus algorithms, fault tolerance mechanisms, and consistency models for large-scale data analytics

syllabus_content:
# COURSE SYLLABUS

## Statistical Inference in the Wild: Real-World Data Challenges and Robust Analytics

**Course Code:** DSCI 3850  
**Credits:** 3  
**Prerequisites:** STAT 2010 (Introductory Statistics), DSCI 2020 (Introduction to Data Science), MATH 1920 (Calculus II)  
**Meeting Time:** MWF 10:00-10:50 AM, Lab: T 2:00-3:50 PM  
**Semester:** Spring 2024  

---

## COURSE DESCRIPTION

This intensive course transforms students into statistical detectives capable of extracting meaningful insights from messy, real-world datasets. Unlike traditional statistics courses that rely on clean textbook examples, students grapple with authentic data problems from industry partners, government agencies, and research institutions. The course emphasizes robust statistical methods that perform well under violations of classical assumptions—a reality in most real-world scenarios. Students work with missing data, outliers, non-normal distributions, and correlated observations while learning advanced techniques including bootstrapping, permutation tests, robust regression, and Bayesian inference. Through weekly case studies, students analyze everything from social media sentiment to financial market volatility, developing expertise in choosing appropriate statistical methods for specific data contexts. The intensive format includes daily problem-solving sessions, peer code reviews, and presentations to industry mentors. By semester's end, students possess a sophisticated understanding of when classical statistical methods fail and how to adapt their analytical approach accordingly, making them highly valuable in today's data-driven workplace.

## LEARNING OBJECTIVES

By the end of this course, students will be able to:

• **Master robust statistical inference techniques** that perform reliably with real-world data violations and irregularities  
• **Develop expertise in diagnosing data quality issues** and selecting appropriate statistical methods for non-ideal datasets  
• **Apply advanced statistical concepts** including bootstrapping, permutation testing, and Bayesian methods to solve authentic industry problems  
• **Demonstrate proficiency in communicating statistical uncertainty** and limitations to non-technical stakeholders through compelling visualizations and reports  

## REQUIRED MATERIALS

- **Textbook:** *Statistical Rethinking: A Bayesian Course with Examples in R and Stan* by Richard McElreath
- **Software:** Python 3.8+, R 4.0+, Jupyter Notebooks, RStudio
- **Hardware:** Laptop capable of running statistical software
- **Access:** Course datasets will be provided via course management system

---

## WEEKLY SCHEDULE

### Week 1: Foundations of Real-World Data Analysis
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis and Data Visualization  
**Topics:**
- Data profiling: Systematic examination of data structure, completeness, validity, and consistency
- Statistical summaries: Measures of central tendency, variability, and distribution shape
- Introduction to robust statistics philosophy

**Lab Activity:** Evaluating Data Quality and Visualization Effectiveness in Student Survey Analysis (50 minutes)

### Week 2: Deep Dive into EDA Techniques
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) and Data Visualization with Python  
**Topics:**
- Descriptive statistics: Mean, median, mode, standard deviation, skewness
- Data quality assessment: Missing values, duplicates, outliers, inconsistencies
- Python tools for robust EDA

**Lab Activity:** Evaluating Data Visualization Effectiveness for Customer Survey Results (45 minutes)

### Week 3: Understanding Variable Relationships
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis and Data Visualization with Python  
**Topics:**
- Univariate analysis: Distribution characteristics and anomaly detection
- Bivariate and multivariate analysis: Correlation, scatter plots, cross-tabulations
- Identifying patterns and dependencies in messy data

**Lab Activity:** Interpreting Correlation Patterns in Real-World Marketing Dataset Analysis (65 minutes)

### Week 4: Advanced EDA and Statistical Visualization
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) with Statistical Visualization  
**Topics:**
- Advanced univariate techniques: Histograms, box plots, distribution fitting
- Sophisticated bivariate analysis: Correlation analysis, statistical significance testing
- Visualization best practices for uncertain data

**Assessment Due:** Exploratory Data Analysis Lab Report: Customer Purchase Behavior (100 points)

### Week 5: Data Preprocessing for Robust Analysis
**Module:** Feature Engineering and Selection for Machine Learning  
**Topics:**
- Feature transformation: Scaling, normalization, log transforms, polynomial expansions
- Target encoding: Converting categorical variables with cross-validation
- Handling missing data and outliers

**Lab Activity:** Evaluating Data Visualization Effectiveness for Customer Sales Insights (70 minutes)

### Week 6: Robust Statistical Methods - Part I
**Topics:**
- When classical assumptions fail: Normality, independence, homoscedasticity
- Introduction to bootstrap methods
- Permutation tests and their applications
- Robust measures of central tendency and spread

**Assessment:** Advanced Machine Learning Pipeline Design and Implementation Quiz (100 points)

### Week 7: Robust Statistical Methods - Part II
**Topics:**
- Robust regression techniques: Huber regression, RANSAC
- Dealing with influential observations
- M-estimators and their properties
- Case study: Financial data analysis with outliers

**Lab Activity:** Interpreting Statistical Significance in A/B Test Results for E-commerce Conversion Rates (55 minutes)

### Week 8: Bootstrap and Resampling Methods
**Topics:**
- Bootstrap confidence intervals
- Bootstrap hypothesis testing
- Jackknife methods
- Cross-validation as a resampling technique
- When and why bootstrap fails

**Lab Activity:** Interpreting Bias-Variance Decomposition in Cross-Validated Model Performance (90 minutes)

### Week 9: MIDTERM WEEK
**Assessment:** Advanced Machine Learning Pipeline Design and Implementation Exam (100 points)

### Week 10: Introduction to Bayesian Inference
**Topics:**
- Bayesian vs. frequentist paradigms
- Prior specification and sensitivity analysis
- Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) basics
- Bayesian model comparison

**Lab Activity:** Interpreting Bias-Variance Decomposition in Model Performance Scenarios (75 minutes)

### Week 11: Bayesian Methods for Real-World Problems
**Topics:**
- Hierarchical models for grouped data
- Handling missing data with Bayesian methods
- Bayesian robust regression
- Model averaging and uncertainty quantification

**Lab Activity:** Interpreting Feature Importance in Random Forest Models for Customer Churn Prediction (60 minutes)

### Week 12: Time Series and Dependent Data
**Topics:**
- Autocorrelation and its implications
- Robust time series methods
- Changepoint detection
- Handling temporal dependencies in statistical inference

**Assessment:** Ethical Considerations in Machine Learning Model Deployment Discussion (100 points)

### Week 13: Advanced Topics in Robust Statistics
**Topics:**
- Multiple testing corrections in exploratory settings
- Causal inference with observational data
- Propensity score matching
- Sensitivity analysis for unmeasured confounding

**Lab Activity:** Critical Evaluation of Machine Learning Model Performance in Production Environment (170 minutes)

### Week 14: Communication and Visualization of Uncertainty
**Topics:**
- Visualizing confidence intervals and prediction intervals
- Communicating statistical uncertainty to stakeholders
- Error bars, credible intervals, and prediction bands
- Interactive visualizations for exploratory analysis

**Lab Activity:** Critical Evaluation of Machine Learning Model Performance Across Multiple Deployment Scenarios (225 minutes)

### Week 15: Industry Applications and Case Studies
**Topics:**
- Healthcare analytics with missing data
- Social media sentiment analysis with non-standard distributions
- Financial risk modeling with heavy tails
- A/B testing in practice with multiple endpoints

### Week 16: FINAL PRESENTATIONS
**Assessment:** End-to-End Machine Learning Pipeline Analysis and Presentation (100 points)

---

## ASSESSMENT PLAN

| Assessment | Type | Points | Due Date | Learning Objectives |

# Statistical Inference Laboratory: Hypothesis Testing in Real-World Data
**Course Code:** STAT 3850 | **Credits:** 3 | **Prerequisites:** STAT 2010 (Inferential Statistics), MATH 1220 (Calculus II)

---

## COURSE INFORMATION

**Class Meeting:** [Days/Times]  
**Semester:** [Term Year]

---

## COURSE DESCRIPTION

This hands-on laboratory course immerses students in the practical application of statistical inference methods to solve authentic data science problems. Students work with messy, real-world datasets from various domains including healthcare, finance, environmental science, and social media to design, execute, and interpret hypothesis tests. The course emphasizes the statistical reasoning process from initial data exploration through assumption validation, test selection, and results interpretation. Weekly lab sessions involve collaborative analysis of case studies where students must justify their statistical choices, handle violations of assumptions, address multiple testing problems, and communicate findings to non-technical stakeholders. Students gain experience with both classical frequentist approaches and modern computational methods including bootstrap resampling, permutation tests, and Bayesian inference. The laboratory format ensures extensive hands-on experience with statistical software (R/Python) while developing critical thinking skills about when and how to apply different inferential techniques. By semester's end, students will have completed a portfolio of statistical investigations demonstrating their ability to navigate the complexities of real data analysis.

---

## LEARNING OBJECTIVES

By the end of this course, students will be able to:

• **Design and Execute Hypothesis Tests:** Students will design and execute appropriate hypothesis tests for diverse data types and research questions  
• **Address Statistical Assumptions:** Students will evaluate and address violations of statistical assumptions using diagnostic tools and robust alternatives  
• **Handle Multiple Testing:** Students will apply multiple testing corrections and control false discovery rates in high-dimensional data scenarios  
• **Implement Computational Methods:** Students will implement computational inference methods including bootstrap, permutation tests, and MCMC sampling  
• **Communicate Statistical Findings:** Students will communicate statistical findings effectively to both technical and non-technical audiences through reproducible reports

---

## REQUIRED MATERIALS

- **Textbook:** *Statistical Inference via Data Science* by Ismay & Kim (free online)
- **Software:** R/RStudio and Python/Jupyter (free installations required)
- **Hardware:** Personal laptop recommended for lab sessions
- **Supplementary:** Course materials available on [LMS Platform]

---

## WEEKLY SCHEDULE

### Week 1: Foundations of Statistical Inference in Practice
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) and Data Visualization  
**Topics:**
- Data profiling: systematic examination of data structure, completeness, and quality metrics
- Statistical summaries: descriptive statistics including measures of central tendency, dispersion, and distribution shape
- Univariate analysis: examination of individual variables including distribution shape assessment
- Introduction to hypothesis testing framework

**Lab Activity:** Interpreting Feature Correlation Heatmaps for Customer Churn Prediction (65 minutes)

### Week 2: Data Quality and Initial Exploration
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) and Data Visualization  
**Topics:**
- Bivariate and multivariate analysis: investigation of relationships using correlation, covariance, and cross-tabulation
- Data quality assessment: handling missing values, outliers, and inconsistent formats
- Assumption checking for parametric tests
- Visual diagnostics for statistical assumptions

**Lab Activity:** Evaluating Data Visualization Quality: Chart Type Selection Critique (75 minutes)

### Week 3: One-Sample and Two-Sample Tests
**Topics:**
- One-sample t-tests and non-parametric alternatives
- Two-sample comparisons: independent and paired samples
- Effect size estimation and practical significance
- Power analysis and sample size determination

**Lab Activity:** Interpreting Correlation vs. Causation in Healthcare Data Visualization (70 minutes)

### Week 4: Tests for Categorical Data
**Topics:**
- Chi-square tests of independence and goodness of fit
- Fisher's exact test for small samples
- McNemar's test for paired categorical data
- Odds ratios and relative risk estimation

**Lab Activity:** Evaluating Data Visualization Effectiveness for Customer Satisfaction Analysis (55 minutes)

### Week 5: ANOVA and Multiple Comparisons
**Topics:**
- One-way and two-way ANOVA
- Post-hoc testing and multiple comparison corrections
- Bonferroni, Holm, and FDR control methods
- Non-parametric alternatives: Kruskal-Wallis test

**Lab Activity:** Interpreting Feature Correlation Patterns in Customer Churn Analysis (95 minutes)

### Week 6: Correlation and Regression Testing
**Topics:**
- Testing correlation coefficients
- Simple and multiple regression inference
- Model assumptions and diagnostic plots
- Bootstrap confidence intervals for regression parameters

**Lab Activity:** Evaluating Data Visualization Choices for Customer Sales Analysis (60 minutes)

### Week 7: Robust and Non-parametric Methods
**Topics:**
- Rank-based tests: Mann-Whitney U, Wilcoxon signed-rank
- Robust statistics and trimmed means
- Permutation tests for any test statistic
- When to choose non-parametric approaches

**Lab Activity:** Interpreting Complex Machine Learning Model Performance Through Multi-Metric Analysis (80 minutes)

### Week 8: Bootstrap Methods and Resampling
**Topics:**
- Bootstrap sampling principles
- Bootstrap confidence intervals (percentile, BCa)
- Bootstrap hypothesis testing
- Jackknife and cross-validation methods

### Week 9: Multiple Testing and High-Dimensional Data
**Topics:**
- Family-wise error rate vs. false discovery rate
- Benjamini-Hochberg procedure
- q-values and local FDR
- Multiple testing in genomics and social science applications

### Week 10: Bayesian Inference Foundations
**Topics:**
- Bayesian vs. frequentist paradigms
- Prior specification and posterior computation
- Credible intervals vs. confidence intervals
- Simple conjugate analyses

### Week 11: Computational Bayesian Methods
**Topics:**
- Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) basics
- Gibbs sampling and Metropolis-Hastings
- Convergence diagnostics
- Using Stan/PyMC for practical analyses

**Lab Activity:** Critical Evaluation of Machine Learning Model Performance in Healthcare Fraud Detection (180 minutes)

### Week 12: Advanced Topics and Model Selection
**Topics:**
- Information criteria (AIC, BIC) for model comparison
- Cross-validation for model assessment
- Regularization and penalized methods
- Handling model uncertainty

### Week 13: Survival Analysis and Time-to-Event Data
**Topics:**
- Kaplan-Meier estimation
- Log-rank tests
- Cox proportional hazards models
- Censoring mechanisms and their impact

### Week 14: Causal Inference and Experimental Design
**Topics:**
- Randomized experiments vs. observational studies
- Confounding and selection bias
- Propensity score methods
- A/B testing in industry applications

**Lab Activity:** Critical Evaluation of Machine Learning Model Performance in High-Stakes Healthcare Prediction (210 minutes)

### Week 15: Communication and Reproducibility
**Topics:**
- Statistical reporting best practices
- Reproducible research with R Markdown/Jupyter
- Presenting uncertainty to stakeholders
- Ethical considerations in statistical inference

### Week 16: Final Project Presentations and Portfolio Review

---

## ASSESSMENT PLAN

| Assessment Type | Title | Points | Due Week | Weight |
|----------------|-------|---------|----------|---------|
| **Portfolio** | End-to-End Statistical Inference Portfolio: Real-World Hypothesis Testing with Impact Analysis | 100 | Week 16 | 30% |
| **Project** | Statistical Investigation Project: Healthcare Data Analysis | 100 | Week 12 | 25% |
| **Presentation** | Data Science Process Presentation: From Question to Insight | 100 | Week 15 | 20% |
| **Quiz** | Advanced Statistical Inference Pipeline Assessment: End-to-End Hypothesis Testing | 100 | Week 8 | 15% |
| **Discussion** | Bias Detection and Mitigation in Statistical Inference: A Critical Analysis Discussion | 100 | Week 10 | 10% |

**Total Points:** 500

### Grade Scale
- A: 93-100% | A-: 90-92%
- B+: 87-89% | B: 83-86% | B-: 80-82%
- C+: 77-79% | C: 73-76% | C-: 70-72%
- D+: 67-69% | D: 60-66%
- F: Below 60%

---

## DETAILED ASSESSMENT DESCRIPTIONS

### Portfolio (30% - Due Week 16)
**End-to-End Statistical Inference Portfolio:** A comprehensive collection of 5-6 statistical investigations demonstrating mastery of different inference techniques applied to real-world problems. Each investigation must include data exploration, assumption checking, appropriate test selection, results interpretation, and communication to non-technical audiences.

### Project (25% - Due Week 12)
**Statistical Investigation Project:** Teams of 2-3 students conduct an original statistical investigation using a real dataset from healthcare, addressing a genuine research question through appropriate hypothesis testing methodology.

This course prepares students for professional data science work. Professional communication, punctuality, and collaborative skills are expected and will be reflected in participation grades.

# COURSE SYLLABUS

## DSCI 3850: Bayesian Methods for Uncertainty Quantification in Data Science

**Semester:** Fall 2024  
**Credits:** 3  
**Prerequisites:** Statistics (STAT 2510), Probability Theory (MATH 3820), Programming in Python (CSCI 1200)  
**Meeting Time:** Tuesday/Thursday 2:00-3:30 PM  

---

## COURSE DESCRIPTION

This specialized course explores Bayesian statistical frameworks as the foundation for handling uncertainty in modern data science applications. Students will master probabilistic reasoning, prior-posterior relationships, and computational methods for Bayesian inference including MCMC sampling and variational approximation. The course emphasizes real-world applications where uncertainty quantification is critical: medical diagnosis systems, financial risk modeling, climate prediction, and A/B testing optimization. Students will work extensively with probabilistic programming languages like Stan and PyMC to implement hierarchical models, Bayesian neural networks, and decision theory under uncertainty. Key topics include conjugate priors, non-informative priors, model selection via Bayes factors, credible intervals versus confidence intervals, and the philosophical foundations distinguishing frequentist from Bayesian approaches. The curriculum integrates theoretical understanding with hands-on projects involving messy, incomplete datasets where traditional point estimates fail to capture the full picture. By course completion, students will confidently apply Bayesian thinking to quantify and communicate uncertainty in data-driven recommendations, making them valuable contributors to organizations requiring robust, probabilistically-informed decision making in high-stakes environments.

---

## LEARNING OBJECTIVES

By the end of this course, students will be able to:

• **Implement advanced Bayesian inference techniques** using MCMC and variational methods for complex hierarchical models
• **Quantify and communicate uncertainty** in predictive models through credible intervals, posterior distributions, and decision-theoretic frameworks  
• **Critically evaluate when Bayesian approaches outperform frequentist methods** in real-world data science scenarios involving prior knowledge and small sample sizes

---

## REQUIRED MATERIALS

**Textbooks:**
- *Bayesian Data Analysis* (3rd Edition) by Gelman, Carlin, Stern, Dunson, Vehtari, and Rubin
- *Statistical Rethinking* (2nd Edition) by Richard McElreath

**Software:**
- Python 3.8+ with PyMC, Stan, NumPy, Pandas, Matplotlib, Seaborn
- R with Stan, brms, and tidyverse packages
- Jupyter Notebook environment

**Hardware:**
- Laptop capable of running statistical computing software
- Access to university computing cluster for intensive MCMC computations

---

## WEEKLY SCHEDULE

### Week 1-2: Foundations of Data Analysis and Bayesian Thinking
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) and Data Visualization  
**Topics:**
- Data profiling - systematic examination of data structure, completeness, and quality including missing values, duplicates, and data types
- Univariate analysis - statistical and visual exploration of individual variables including distributions, central tendency, and variability measures
- Introduction to Bayesian vs. Frequentist paradigms
- Probability review and Bayes' theorem

**Activities:**
- Interpreting Data Distribution Patterns Through Statistical Visualization Analysis (45 min)
- Comparing Data Visualization Types for Customer Purchase Pattern Analysis (60 min)

### Week 3-4: Feature Engineering and Prior Specification
**Module:** Feature Engineering for Machine Learning  
**Topics:**
- Feature scaling and normalization - techniques like StandardScaler and MinMaxScaler to ensure features are on comparable scales for machine learning algorithms
- Categorical encoding methods - strategies including one-hot encoding, ordinal encoding, and target encoding to convert categorical variables into numerical representations
- Prior distributions: informative, non-informative, and conjugate priors
- Eliciting expert knowledge for prior specification

**Activities:**
- Evaluating Data Cleaning Methods: Email Marketing Dataset Analysis (60 min)
- Evaluating Data Cleaning Approaches for Customer Survey Analysis (90 min)

### Week 5-6: Bayesian Inference and Conjugate Analysis
**Topics:**
- Posterior distributions and conjugate families
- Beta-binomial, normal-normal conjugate pairs
- Credible intervals vs. confidence intervals
- Bayesian point estimation: posterior mean, median, mode

**Activities:**
- Interpreting Feature Correlation Heatmaps in Customer Churn Analysis (50 min)

### Week 7-8: Computational Bayesian Methods - MCMC
**Topics:**
- Markov Chain Monte Carlo fundamentals
- Metropolis-Hastings algorithm
- Gibbs sampling
- Convergence diagnostics and chain assessment
- Introduction to Stan and PyMC

**Activities:**
- Critical Evaluation of Machine Learning Model Performance in High-Stakes Healthcare Applications (150 min)

### Week 9: **MIDTERM EXAM**

### Week 10-11: Advanced MCMC and Variational Inference
**Topics:**
- Hamiltonian Monte Carlo and NUTS
- Variational Bayes approximation
- Automatic differentiation variational inference (ADVI)
- Computational efficiency and scalability

**Activities:**
- Interpreting Feature Importance in Ensemble Models: Understanding SHAP Values vs Permutation Importance (3.5 hours)

### Week 12-13: Hierarchical and Multilevel Models
**Topics:**
- Hierarchical modeling concepts
- Partial pooling and shrinkage
- Random effects and mixed models
- Applications in A/B testing and medical studies

**Activities:**
- Deconstructing Bias in Machine Learning Model Performance Across Demographic Subgroups (3 hours)

### Week 14-15: Model Selection and Decision Theory
**Topics:**
- Bayes factors and model comparison
- Cross-validation for Bayesian models
- Decision theory under uncertainty
- Value of information analysis
- Bayesian optimization

**Activities:**
- Model Selection Tribunal: Evaluating and Defending Machine Learning Approaches for Real-World Business Problems (165 min)

### Week 16: Advanced Applications and Course Integration
**Topics:**
- Bayesian neural networks
- Gaussian processes
- Time series and forecasting under uncertainty
- Ethics of uncertainty communication

---

## ASSESSMENT PLAN

|------------|------|--------|----------|---------|
| **Bayesian Inference Fundamentals Exam** | Exam | 100 | Week 9 | 20% |
| **Uncertainty Quantification Lab Reports (2)** | Lab Report | 100 each | Weeks 6, 12 | 40% |
| **Bayesian Analytics Portfolio Project** | Portfolio | 100 | Week 15 | 25% |
| **Uncertainty Communication Presentation** | Presentation | 100 | Week 16 | 15% |

**Total Points: 500**

### Assessment Descriptions:

**Midterm Exam (20%):** Comprehensive examination covering Bayesian fundamentals, conjugate analysis, basic MCMC, and conceptual understanding of uncertainty quantification.

**Lab Reports (40%):** Two detailed technical reports demonstrating mastery of computational Bayesian methods:
1. MCMC implementation and convergence analysis
2. Hierarchical model development and interpretation

**Portfolio Project (25%):** End-to-end Bayesian analysis of a real-world dataset requiring uncertainty quantification. Students will implement multiple models, perform model selection, and provide decision-theoretic recommendations.

# Mathematical Foundations of Predictive Modeling
**Course Syllabus - Fall 2024**

---

## Course Description

This course explores the mathematical principles underlying predictive modeling in data science, bridging theoretical foundations with practical implementation. Students will develop deep understanding of how statistical concepts, linear algebra, and optimization theory form the backbone of modern machine learning algorithms. The curriculum emphasizes building models from first principles, understanding their mathematical assumptions, and recognizing when specific modeling approaches are appropriate. Through hands-on projects, students will implement core algorithms from scratch before utilizing industry-standard libraries. Topics include linear and polynomial regression, classification methods, regularization techniques, dimensionality reduction, and model validation strategies. The course prioritizes mathematical intuition over software proficiency, ensuring students can critically evaluate model performance, diagnose problems, and make informed decisions about model selection. By semester's end, students will possess a solid mathematical foundation for advanced data science coursework and understand the theoretical underpinnings that make predictive modeling both powerful and reliable.

---

## Learning Objectives

Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

• Derive and implement fundamental machine learning algorithms from mathematical first principles  
• Evaluate model assumptions, limitations, and appropriate application contexts using statistical theory  
• Apply linear algebra and calculus concepts to understand optimization in machine learning models  
• Design and execute rigorous model validation strategies using cross-validation and statistical testing  
• Analyze the mathematical trade-offs between model complexity, interpretability, and predictive performance  

---

## Weekly Schedule

### Week 1: Introduction and Mathematical Prerequisites
**Topics:**
- Course overview and mathematical foundations review
- Linear algebra essentials: vectors, matrices, eigenvalues
- Calculus review: gradients, optimization basics
- Statistical foundations: probability distributions, hypothesis testing

**Readings:** Textbook Ch. 1-2  
**Activities:** Mathematical prerequisites self-assessment

---

### Week 2: Exploratory Data Analysis Foundations
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis and Data Visualization  
**Concepts:**
- Univariate Analysis: Statistical summaries, distribution analysis, outlier detection
- Bivariate and Multivariate Analysis: Correlation analysis, scatter plots, relationship identification

**Activities:** 
- Interpreting Feature Correlation Patterns in Customer Purchase Behavior Dataset (45 min)
- Evaluating Data Visualization Effectiveness for Customer Sales Analysis (60 min)

**Readings:** Textbook Ch. 3.1-3.3

---

### Week 3: Feature Engineering Mathematical Foundations
**Module:** Feature Engineering and Selection for Machine Learning  
**Concepts:**
- Feature transformation: Mathematical operations (scaling, normalization, transforms)
- Feature selection methods: Filter, wrapper, and embedded approaches

**Activities:** 
- Evaluating Data Visualization Quality: Comparing Chart Types for Sales Data Analysis (60 min)

**Readings:** Textbook Ch. 3.4-3.5  
**Assessment:** Data Science Fundamentals Quiz (100 points) - **Due Friday**

---

### Week 4: Linear Regression Theory
**Topics:**
- Derivation of least squares solution using calculus
- Matrix formulation: β = (X'X)⁻¹X'y
- Geometric interpretation of regression
- Assumptions and mathematical conditions for validity

**Activities:** Deriving linear regression from first principles (hands-on implementation)  
**Readings:** Textbook Ch. 3.6-3.8

---

### Week 5: Polynomial Regression and Model Complexity
**Topics:**
- Mathematical basis for polynomial features
- Overfitting through mathematical lens
- Bias-variance decomposition derivation
- Cross-validation theory and implementation

**Activities:** 
- Interpreting Bias-Variance Trade-off Through Cross-Validation Decomposition Analysis (90 min)

**Readings:** Textbook Ch. 7.1-7.3

---

### Week 6: Regularization Theory
**Topics:**
- Ridge regression: L2 penalty mathematical derivation
- LASSO: L1 penalty and sparsity theory
- Elastic Net: combining penalties mathematically
- Regularization path analysis

**Activities:** Implementing regularization algorithms from scratch  
**Readings:** Textbook Ch. 3.9-3.11

---

### Week 7: Classification Foundations
**Topics:**
- Logistic regression: sigmoid function derivation
- Maximum likelihood estimation
- Decision boundaries and mathematical interpretation
- Multiclass extensions

**Activities:** Mathematical derivation of logistic regression  
**Readings:** Textbook Ch. 4.1-4.3  
**Assessment:** Data Science Foundations Portfolio: Exploratory Data Analysis Project (100 points) - **Due Friday**

---

### Week 8: Advanced Classification Methods
**Topics:**
- Support Vector Machines: optimization formulation
- Kernel trick mathematical theory
- Decision trees: information theory foundations
- Entropy and information gain calculations

**Activities:** 
- Interpreting Statistical Significance in A/B Test Results for E-commerce Conversion Rates (55 min)

**Readings:** Textbook Ch. 4.4-4.6, Ch. 9.1-9.2

---

### Week 9: **SPRING BREAK - NO CLASSES**

---

### Week 10: Dimensionality Reduction Theory
**Topics:**
- Principal Component Analysis: eigenvalue decomposition
- Singular Value Decomposition mathematical foundations
- Variance explained and mathematical interpretation
- Non-negative matrix factorization

**Activities:** PCA implementation from eigenvalue decomposition  
**Readings:** Textbook Ch. 14.5, supplementary materials

---

### Week 11: Model Validation and Statistical Testing
**Topics:**
- Cross-validation mathematical framework
- Bootstrap methods and statistical theory
- Hypothesis testing for model comparison
- Confidence intervals for predictions

**Activities:** 
- Interpreting Bias-Variance Tradeoff Through Cross-Validation Curves Analysis (75 min)

**Readings:** Textbook Ch. 7.4-7.6

---

### Week 12: Optimization in Machine Learning
**Topics:**
- Gradient descent mathematical derivation
- Stochastic gradient descent theory
- Convex optimization foundations
- Convergence analysis and stopping criteria

**Activities:** Implementing optimization algorithms from calculus principles  
**Readings:** Supplementary optimization materials  
**Assessment:** Ethical AI and Bias Mitigation Discussion (100 points) - **Due Wednesday**

---

### Week 13: Ensemble Methods Mathematical Framework
**Topics:**
- Bagging: variance reduction theory
- Boosting: bias reduction mathematical analysis
- Random Forest mathematical foundations
- Combining weak learners theory

**Activities:** 
- Evaluating Machine Learning Model Performance for Real Estate Price Prediction (120 min)

**Readings:** Textbook Ch. 8.1-8.3, Ch. 15.1-15.3

---

### Week 14: Advanced Topics and Model Interpretation
**Topics:**
- Feature importance mathematical measures
- SHAP values and game theory connections
- Model interpretability vs. complexity trade-offs
- Uncertainty quantification in predictions

**Activities:** 
- Critical Evaluation of Machine Learning Model Performance in High-Stakes Healthcare Prediction (160 min)

**Readings:** Current research papers (provided)

---

### Week 15: Integration and Real-World Applications
**Topics:**
- Putting it all together: end-to-end mathematical pipeline
- Model selection criteria mathematical foundations
- Production considerations for mathematical models
- Future directions in mathematical machine learning

**Assessment:** Advanced Machine Learning Pipeline Lab Report (100 points) - **Due Friday**

---
