# Course Syllabus

## Building Connected Systems: API-First Software Architecture
**Course Code:** CS 3350  
**Credits:** 3  
**Prerequisites:** CS 2350 (Object-Oriented Programming), CS 2400 (Data Structures)  
**Semester:** Spring 2024  

---

## Course Description

This foundational course explores software development through the lens of API-first design principles, teaching students to architect and build interconnected systems from the ground up. Students learn to design, implement, and consume RESTful and GraphQL APIs while understanding how modern applications communicate across distributed environments. The course emphasizes hands-on development of microservices, third-party API integration, and real-world connectivity patterns. Through progressive projects, students build a complete ecosystem of communicating services, from simple data endpoints to complex authentication systems. Topics include API specification languages (OpenAPI/Swagger), versioning strategies, error handling, rate limiting, and security considerations. Students gain practical experience with popular frameworks, testing methodologies for API endpoints, and documentation practices that enable effective team collaboration. The curriculum balances theoretical concepts with industry-standard tools and practices, preparing students to contribute immediately to modern software teams. By course completion, students understand how APIs serve as the backbone of contemporary software architecture and can confidently design systems that scale across web, mobile, and IoT platforms while maintaining security and performance standards.

---

## Learning Objectives

Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

• **Design and implement RESTful and GraphQL APIs** using industry-standard frameworks and specification languages
• **Architect connected systems** using API-first principles and microservices patterns for scalable software solutions  
• **Integrate third-party services** and develop secure authentication mechanisms for distributed application ecosystems

### Week 11: Third-Party API Integration

- **Activity:** Code Quality Assessment: Evaluating Password Validation Functions (55 min)

### Week 13: Performance and Scalability

### Week 14: Production Deployment

# COMP 3850: Test-Driven Software Architecture
## Building Bulletproof Applications from the Ground Up

#### Course Description

This intensive, project-driven course revolutionizes how students approach software development by placing testing at the absolute center of the development process. Students will master the art of writing tests before code, designing software architectures that are inherently testable, and implementing comprehensive testing strategies across multiple layers of complex applications. Through hands-on development of three major projects—a distributed microservices system, a real-time collaborative application, and a data-intensive analytics platform—students will experience the full spectrum of testing challenges in modern software development. The course emphasizes practical mastery of advanced testing frameworks, continuous integration pipelines, mutation testing, property-based testing, and performance testing under realistic load conditions. Students will work in rotating teams, conducting rigorous code reviews focused on testability and test coverage. By semester's end, students will have internalized a test-first mindset and possess the technical skills to architect, build, and maintain enterprise-grade software systems with confidence. This course bridges the gap between academic computer science and professional software development practices.

### Learning Objectives

By the end of this course, students will be able to:

• **Design and implement comprehensive test suites** using TDD/BDD methodologies for complex, multi-tier software architectures
• **Architect software systems with testability** as a primary design constraint, demonstrating mastery of dependency injection, mocking, and modular design patterns  
• **Deploy and maintain automated testing pipelines** integrating unit, integration, end-to-end, and performance testing in CI/CD environments

---

## Weekly Schedule

### Week 1: TDD Fundamentals and JavaScript Testing
**Module:** Test-Driven Development (TDD) with JavaScript
- **Concepts:**
  - Red-Green-Refactor Cycle: The core TDD workflow of writing failing tests (Red), implementing minimal code to pass (Green), and improving code structure (Refactor)
  - Unit Testing: Writing isolated tests that verify individual functions or components work correctly with specific inputs and expected outputs
- **Activities:** Code Quality Detective: Evaluating Bug-Prone vs. Clean Code Samples (55 min)
- 
### Week 2: Unit Testing Frameworks Deep Dive
**Module:** Test-Driven Development (TDD) with Unit Testing Frameworks
- **Concepts:**
  - Red-Green-Refactor Cycle: The three-phase TDD process of writing failing tests (Red), implementing minimal passing code (Green), and improving code structure (Refactor)
  - Unit Testing: Testing individual components or functions in isolation to verify they behave as expected with various inputs and edge cases
- **Activities:** Code Review Battle: Evaluating Bug-Prone vs Clean Code Solutions (50 min)
- 
### Week 3: Test Coverage and Measurement
**Module:** Test-Driven Development (TDD) with JavaScript and Jest
- **Concepts:**
  - Red-Green-Refactor Cycle: The three-phase TDD process of writing failing tests (Red), making tests pass (Green), and improving code structure (Refactor)
  - Test Coverage: Measurement of how much source code is executed during testing, including line, branch, and function coverage metrics
- **Activities:** Code Review Quality Assessment: Evaluating Bug Fixes in Simple Python Functions (55 min)
- - **Assessment:** Software Development Fundamentals Quiz (100 points)

### Week 4: Advanced TDD Implementation
**Module:** Test-Driven Development (TDD) Implementation and Best Practices
- **Concepts:**
  - Red-Green-Refactor Cycle: The core TDD workflow of writing failing tests, implementing passing code, then improving design
  - Unit Testing: Creating isolated tests that verify individual components or functions work correctly in isolation
- **Activities:** Code Review Evaluation: Assessing Bug Fixes in a Simple Calculator Program (50 min)
- 
### Week 5: TDD with Complex Systems
**Module:** Test-Driven Development (TDD) Implementation
- **Concepts:**
  - Red-Green-Refactor Cycle: The three-phase TDD process of writing failing tests, implementing minimal code to pass, then improving code structure
  - Unit Testing: Isolated testing of individual components or functions to verify correct behavior independent of external dependencies
- **Activities:** Code Review Quality Assessment: Evaluating Bug Fixes and Best Practices (65 min)
- 
### Week 6: Testing Frameworks Mastery
**Module:** Test-Driven Development (TDD) Fundamentals
- **Concepts:**
  - Red-Green-Refactor Cycle: The three-phase TDD process of writing failing tests, implementing minimal code, and improving design
  - Unit Testing Frameworks: Tools like JUnit, pytest, or Mocha that provide structure and assertions for automated testing
- **Activities:** Code Quality Assessment: Evaluating HTML/CSS Web Page Implementations (60 min)
- - **Assessment:** Introduction to Programming Languages and Development Tools Discussion (100 points)

### Week 7: API Testing and RESTful Services
**Module:** API Design and RESTful Web Services
- **Concepts:**
  - REST (Representational State Transfer): Architectural style for distributed systems emphasizing stateless communication and resource-based URLs
  - HTTP Methods: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH operations that define actions performed on API resources
- **Activities:** Code Review Battle: Evaluating Bug-Fix Solutions (65 min)
- 
### Week 8: **PROJECT 1 WEEK - Distributed Microservices System**
- **Focus:** Apply TDD principles to build a distributed microservices system
- **Activities:** Code Review Quality Assessment: Evaluating Bug Fixes in HTML/CSS Projects (55 min)
- - **Assessment:** Personal Portfolio Website Development Project (100 points)

### Week 9: Integration Testing and Test Doubles
**Module:** Advanced Testing Patterns
- **Concepts:**
  - Integration Testing: Testing interactions between multiple components or systems
  - Test Doubles: Mocks, stubs, fakes, and spies for isolating units under test
- **Activities:** Code Review Quality Assessment: Evaluating Bug Fixes in a Simple Calculator Program (50 min)
- 
### Week 10: Behavior-Driven Development (BDD)
**Module:** BDD and Specification by Example
- **Concepts:**
  - BDD Framework: Using natural language specifications to drive development
  - Acceptance Testing: Verifying system behavior from user perspective
- **Activities:** Code Review Evaluation: Assessing Bug Fix Quality and Implementation Approaches (45 min)
- 
### Week 11: **PROJECT 2 WEEK - Real-time Collaborative Application**
- **Focus:** Implement BDD practices for real-time systems
- - **Assessment:** Personal Portfolio Website Development Exam (100 points)

### Week 12: Performance Testing and Load Testing
**Module:** Non-Functional Testing
- **Concepts:**
  - Performance Testing: Measuring system responsiveness and stability under load
  - Load Testing: Simulating realistic user loads to identify bottlenecks
- 
### Week 13: CI/CD Pipeline Integration
**Module:** Automated Testing in DevOps
- **Concepts:**
  - Continuous Integration: Automated testing on code changes
  - Deployment Pipeline: Automated testing stages from unit to production
- 
### Week 14: **PROJECT 3 WEEK - Data-Intensive Analytics Platform**
- **Focus:** Testing data processing, ETL pipelines, and analytics
- 
### Week 15: Advanced Testing Topics
**Module:** Mutation Testing and Property-Based Testing
- **Concepts:**
  - Mutation Testing: Evaluating test quality by introducing code changes
  - Property-Based Testing: Generating test cases based on system properties
- - **Assessment:** My First Programming Project - Interactive Calculator Presentation (100 points)

### Week 16: **FINAL PROJECT PRESENTATIONS**
- Student presentations of major projects
- Peer code reviews and testing strategy evaluations
- Course wrap-up and industry best practices discussion

---

## Assessment Plan

| Assessment | Type | Points | Week Due | Weight |
|------------|------|--------|----------|---------|
| Software Development Fundamentals Quiz | Quiz | 100 | Week 3 | 10% |
| Programming Languages Discussion | Discussion | 100 | Week 6 | 10% |
| Portfolio Website Development | Portfolio | 100 | Week 8 | 15% |
| Portfolio Website Development Exam | Exam | 100 | Week 11 | 15% |
| Calculator Project Presentation | Presentation | 100 | Week 15 | 10% |
| **Major Project 1:** Microservices System | Project | 200 | Week 8 | 15% |
| **Major Project 2:** Real-time Collaborative App | Project | 200 | Week 11 | 15% |
| **Major Project 3:** Analytics Platform | Project | 200 | Week 14 | 20% |

**Total Points:** 1100  
**Grading Scale:** A (93-100%), A- (90-92%), B+ (87-89%), B (83-86%), B- (80-82%), C+ (77-79%), C (70-76%), D (60-69%), F (<60%)

---

### Late Assignment Policy
- **Projects:** 10% penalty per day late (maximum 3 days, then 0 points)
- **Quizzes/Exams:** No makeup without documented excuse
- **Discussions:** Must be completed by due date (no late submissions)

### Collaboration Policy
- **Encouraged:** Peer programming during lab sessions, code reviews, discussing concepts
- **Prohibited:** Copying code, sharing project solutions, unauthorized collaboration on individual assessments
- **Required:** Proper attribution for any external code or resources used

### Technology Requirements
- **Required Software:** Git, Node.js, Jest, Python, pytest, Docker, IDE of choice
- **Accounts Needed:** GitHub, cloud platform access (provided)
- **Hardware:** Laptop capable of running development tools and virtual machines

### Code Quality Standards
All submitted code must:
- Follow established style guidelines (ESLint, Prettier)
- Include comprehensive tests (minimum 80% coverage)
- Be properly documented with JSDoc/docstring comments
- Pass all CI/CD pipeline checks

### Final Notes
This is an intensive, project-heavy course designed to prepare you for professional software development. Success requires consistent effort, active participation, and a commitment to learning industry-standard practices. The skills you develop here will directly transfer to your internships and full-time positions.

# Strategic Foresight Analytics: Building Decision Intelligence Systems
**Course Syllabus - Fall 2024**

---

## COURSE INFORMATION

**Course Code:** DATA 495  
**Credits:** 3  
**Prerequisites:** Statistics (STAT 301), Database Management (DATA 301), Machine Learning (DATA 401)  
**Meeting Time:** Tuesday/Thursday 2:00-3:30 PM  

### Course Description
This capstone course transforms students into strategic forecasting consultants who design and implement comprehensive decision intelligence systems for real-world organizations. Students work directly with industry partners to tackle complex forecasting challenges across diverse sectors including retail demand planning, financial risk assessment, supply chain optimization, and market trend prediction. The course integrates advanced time series analysis, machine learning forecasting models, scenario planning methodologies, and uncertainty quantification techniques. Students develop end-to-end forecasting pipelines that incorporate multiple data sources, handle missing data and outliers, and provide actionable insights with confidence intervals. The capstone project requires teams to deliver a fully functional forecasting system complete with interactive dashboards, automated reporting, and business recommendations. Emphasis is placed on communicating forecast uncertainty to stakeholders, validating model performance over time, and adapting models to changing business conditions. By semester's end, students present their systems to industry partners and academic faculty, demonstrating both technical proficiency and strategic business acumen in transforming data into forward-looking intelligence.

### Learning Objectives
By the end of this course, students will be able to:

1. **Design and deploy enterprise-level forecasting systems** that integrate multiple algorithms and data sources for robust prediction accuracy
2. **Master advanced uncertainty quantification techniques** and communicate forecast reliability to non-technical stakeholders through compelling visualizations  
3. **Demonstrate consulting-level expertise** by delivering actionable strategic recommendations based on forecasting insights to real industry partners

---

## WEEKLY SCHEDULE

### Week 1: Foundations of Strategic Forecasting
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) with Python: Uncovering Insights Through Visualization and Statistical Summaries
- **Key Concepts:**
  - Data profiling - systematic examination of dataset structure, completeness, and quality metrics
  - Univariate analysis - statistical and visual exploration of individual variables including measures of central tendency, dispersion, and distribution shape
- **Activities:** Course introduction, industry partner presentations, team formation
- **Deliverables:** Team contracts, initial industry partner matching

### Week 2: Advanced Pattern Recognition
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis: Uncovering Patterns and Anomalies

  - Outlier Detection: Systematic identification of data points that deviate significantly from expected patterns using statistical methods
- **Activities:** Begin Customer Retention Dashboard project (Part 1)
- **Deliverables:** Data Quality Assessment discussion post due

### Week 3: Relationship Analysis and Dependencies
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) and Data Visualization
- **Key Concepts:**
  - Univariate Analysis - examining individual variables through statistical measures
  - Bivariate Analysis - exploring relationships between pairs of variables using correlation coefficients, cross-tabulations, and scatter plots
- **Activities:** Continue Customer Retention Dashboard project (Part 2)
- **Deliverables:** Weekly progress report

### Week 4: Time Series Fundamentals
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis with Python: Unveiling Data Stories Through Visualization and Statistics

  - Data profiling - systematic examination of dataset structure and quality metrics
  - Statistical summaries - central tendency, dispersion, and distribution shape measures

### Week 5: Forecasting Model Architecture

  - Data Profiling: Systematic assessment of data quality and completeness
- **Activities:** Predictive Dashboard for Employee Retention (Session 1)

### Week 7: Multi-Source Data Integration

  - Univariate Analysis: Statistical examination of single variables
  - Bivariate Analysis: Investigation of relationships between variables
- **Activities:** Predictive Dashboard for Employee Retention (Session 2)
- **Deliverables:** Mid-term progress presentation preparation

### Week 8: Mid-Term Presentations
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) and Data Visualization Fundamentals

  - Data Profiling: Systematic examination of data structure and quality
  - Univariate Analysis: Statistical and visual exploration techniques
- **Activities:** Mid-term project presentations to industry partners
- **Deliverables:** Customer Behavior Data Analysis Presentation

### Week 9: Advanced Machine Learning for Forecasting
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis: Uncovering Patterns Through Statistical Investigation
- **Key Concepts:**
  - Univariate Analysis: Statistical examination of individual variables
  - Bivariate Analysis: Investigation of variable relationships
- **Activities:** Customer Churn Prediction Dashboard Creation
- **Deliverables:** Refined project proposals based on partner feedback

### Week 10: Ensemble Methods and Model Selection

  - Univariate Analysis - Statistical examination of single variables

- **Focus:** Interactive visualization, uncertainty communication, executive summaries

context.course_title: Digital Archaeology: Mining Hidden Patterns in Complex Datasets

syllabus_content:
# Digital Archaeology: Mining Hidden Patterns in Complex Datasets
**Course Code:** DATA 385  
**Credits:** 4  
**Prerequisites:** Introduction to Statistics, Programming Fundamentals (Python preferred)  
**Meeting Time:** Tuesdays & Thursdays, 2:00-4:30 PM  
**Semester:** Fall 2024  

## Course Description

This hands-on laboratory course transforms students into digital archaeologists who uncover hidden insights buried within complex, real-world datasets. Through intensive lab sessions, students excavate meaningful patterns from messy, unstructured data using advanced data mining techniques including association rule mining, clustering algorithms, anomaly detection, and sequential pattern discovery. The course emphasizes practical application through weekly laboratory exercises where students work with diverse datasets from social media streams, financial transactions, sensor networks, and customer behavior logs. Students learn to clean, preprocess, and systematically explore large datasets while developing proficiency in Python-based mining tools such as scikit-learn, Weka, and specialized libraries. Each lab session builds toward a capstone project where teams conduct an original data archaeology expedition on a dataset of their choice, presenting their discoveries through comprehensive reports and interactive visualizations. The laboratory environment simulates real-world data science scenarios, emphasizing reproducible research practices, ethical data handling, and effective communication of complex findings to non-technical stakeholders.

## Learning Objectives

Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

• Master core data mining algorithms including clustering, classification, association rules, and outlier detection through hands-on implementation  
• Develop proficiency in excavating actionable insights from noisy, heterogeneous datasets using systematic exploration methodologies  
• Construct end-to-end data mining pipelines incorporating preprocessing, feature engineering, pattern discovery, and validation techniques  
• Demonstrate expertise in Python-based mining frameworks and visualization tools for presenting complex analytical findings  
• Apply ethical data mining practices and statistical validation methods to ensure reliable and responsible pattern discovery  

## Weekly Schedule

### Week 1: Foundation of Digital Archaeology
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis: Uncovering Patterns and Insights  
**Topics:**
- Descriptive Statistics: Summary measures including central tendency, variability, and distribution shape that provide initial dataset understanding
- Data Distribution Analysis: Examining how values are spread across variables using histograms, box plots, and probability plots to identify skewness and outliers

**Lab Activity:** Introduction to Python data mining environment setup and basic dataset exploration

### Week 2: Statistical Foundations for Data Mining
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis and Statistical Visualization  
**Topics:**
- Univariate Analysis: Statistical examination of individual variables including measures of central tendency, dispersion, and distribution shape
- Bivariate Analysis: Investigation of relationships between two variables using correlation coefficients, cross-tabulations, and scatter plots

**Lab Activity:** Statistical profiling of real-world datasets

### Week 3: Advanced Data Profiling Techniques
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) with Python  
**Topics:**
- Data profiling: systematic examination of dataset characteristics including dimensions, data types, and basic statistics
- Univariate analysis: exploring individual variables through histograms, box plots, and summary statistics to understand distributions

**Lab Activity:** Comprehensive data quality assessment workshop

### Week 4: Multivariate Exploration Methods
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) and Data Visualization Fundamentals  
**Topics:**
- Univariate analysis: examining individual variables through measures of central tendency, dispersion, and distribution shape
- Bivariate and multivariate analysis: exploring relationships between variables using correlation, cross-tabulation, and comparative visualizations

**Lab Activity:** Design and Build a Customer Segmentation Dashboard for E-commerce Strategy (3 hours)

### Week 5: Data Preprocessing and Cleaning Archaeology
**Topics:**
- Missing data imputation strategies
- Outlier detection and handling
- Data transformation techniques
- Feature engineering fundamentals

**Lab Activity:** Data cleaning pipeline construction

### Week 6: Association Rule Mining
**Topics:**
- Market basket analysis
- Apriori algorithm implementation
- Support, confidence, and lift metrics
- Association rule validation

**Lab Activity:** Mining shopping patterns from retail transaction data

### Week 7: Clustering Algorithms and Applications
**Topics:**
- K-means clustering
- Hierarchical clustering
- DBSCAN for density-based clustering
- Cluster validation metrics

**Lab Activity:** Design and Build a Customer Churn Prediction Dashboard with Actionable Insights (225 minutes)

### Week 8: Classification Techniques
**Topics:**
- Decision trees and random forests
- Support vector machines
- Naive Bayes classification
- Model evaluation and cross-validation

**Lab Activity:** Building predictive models for customer behavior

**Assessment:** E-commerce Customer Behavior Analysis Quiz (100 points)

### Week 9: Anomaly Detection Methods
**Topics:**
- Statistical outlier detection
- Isolation forests
- One-class SVM
- Anomaly detection in time series

**Lab Activity:** Fraud detection in financial transaction data

### Week 10: Sequential Pattern Mining
**Topics:**
- Time series pattern discovery
- Sequential rule mining
- Web usage pattern analysis
- Temporal data preprocessing

**Lab Activity:** Design and Build a Multi-Source Sales Performance Dashboard (210 minutes)

### Week 11: Text Mining and Natural Language Processing
**Topics:**
- Text preprocessing techniques
- Term frequency-inverse document frequency (TF-IDF)
- Topic modeling with LDA
- Sentiment analysis

**Lab Activity:** Mining insights from social media datasets

### Week 12: Advanced Visualization and Dashboard Design
**Topics:**
- Interactive visualization principles
- Dashboard design best practices
- Storytelling with data
- Communication strategies for technical findings

**Lab Activity:** Design a Municipal Budget Dashboard for City Council Decision-Making (4.5 hours)

### Week 13: Ethics and Validation in Data Mining
**Topics:**
- Ethical considerations in data mining
- Privacy preservation techniques
- Statistical significance testing
- Reproducible research practices

**Lab Activity:** Ethical review of data mining projects

**Assessment:** Comparative Analysis Discussion: Statistical Methods for Business Decision-Making (100 points)

### Week 14: Capstone Project Development
**Topics:**
- Project methodology design
- Advanced mining technique integration
- Team collaboration strategies

**Lab Activity:** Intensive capstone project work session

### Week 15: Project Presentations and Peer Review
**Topics:**
- Presentation techniques for technical audiences
- Peer evaluation methods
- Professional portfolio development

**Activity:** Final project presentations and demonstrations

### Week 16: Final Examinations
**Assessment:** E-commerce Customer Behavior Analysis Exam (100 points)

## Assessment Plan

| Assessment Type | Assignment | Points | Due Date |
|----------------|------------|---------|----------|
| Quiz | E-commerce Customer Behavior Analysis Quiz | 100 | Week 8 |
| Discussion | Comparative Analysis Discussion: Statistical Methods for Business Decision-Making | 100 | Week 13 |
| Exam | E-commerce Customer Behavior Analysis Exam | 100 | Week 16 |
| Portfolio | Retail Sales Performance Analytics Portfolio | 100 | Week 15 |
| Capstone Project | E-commerce Customer Segmentation and Revenue Optimization Analysis | 100 | Week 15 |
| Lab Participation | Weekly lab activities and attendance | 100 | Ongoing |
| **Total** | | **600** | |

### Collaboration Policy
- Lab activities: Collaboration encouraged
- Capstone project: Team-based with individual accountability
- Quizzes and exams: Individual work only
- Discussions: Original posts required, thoughtful responses to peers encouraged

### Technology Requirements
Students must have access to a laptop capable of running Python and Jupyter Notebook environments. The university computer lab is available during designated hours for students without adequate personal equipment.

### Accommodations
Students with documented disabilities should contact the Office of Disability Services to arrange appropriate accommodations. Please inform the instructor of any needed accommodations within the first two weeks of the semester.

### Data Ethics and Privacy
Students will work with real-world datasets that may contain sensitive information. All data handling must comply with ethical guidelines discussed in class. Students must sign a data use agreement and maintain confidentiality of any proprietary datasets used in the course.

### Course Evaluation
Student feedback is valuable for course improvement. Mid-semester feedback will be collected informally, and formal evaluations will be conducted at the end of the semester. Students are encouraged to provide constructive feedback throughout the course.

# Course Syllabus

## Transforming Numbers into Narratives: Visual Storytelling and Communicating Data Insights

**Course Code:** DATA 2400  
**Credits:** 3  
**Semester:** Fall/Spring 2024  
**Prerequisites:** Introduction to Statistics, Basic Data Analysis  

---

## Course Description

This foundational course bridges the gap between raw data analysis and effective communication by teaching students how to craft compelling data stories for diverse audiences. Students learn to transform statistical findings into clear, actionable narratives using visualization principles, report design, and audience-centered communication strategies. The course emphasizes practical skills in creating executive summaries, dashboard design, infographic development, and presentation techniques that make complex data accessible to non-technical stakeholders. Through hands-on projects using real-world datasets, students practice translating analytical results into business recommendations, policy briefs, and public communications. Key topics include visual hierarchy, color psychology in data presentation, interactive reporting tools, ethical considerations in data storytelling, and adapting technical findings for different organizational levels. Students will develop a portfolio of data communication artifacts including written reports, visual dashboards, and oral presentations. This course prepares students to serve as effective data communicators who can ensure analytical insights drive informed decision-making across organizations, making it essential preparation for careers in business analytics, policy research, journalism, and consulting.

## Learning Objectives

Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

• Master the principles of visual storytelling to transform complex datasets into clear, compelling narratives for diverse audiences  
• Apply foundational design and communication theories to create professional reports, dashboards, and presentations that drive decision-making  
• Develop practical expertise in audience analysis, ethical data presentation, and adaptive communication strategies for technical and non-technical stakeholders

# Temporal Pattern Mining and Predictive Analytics for Strategic Decision Making

**Course Code:** DATA 485  
**Credits:** 3  
**Prerequisites:** STAT 201 (Statistics), COMP 201 (Programming Fundamentals), DATA 301 (Introduction to Data Analytics)  
**Semester:** Fall 2024

## Instructor Information

## Course Description

This specialized course explores advanced forecasting methodologies through the lens of temporal pattern recognition and strategic business applications. Students will master cutting-edge techniques for extracting meaningful patterns from time-dependent data and translating these insights into actionable business forecasts. The curriculum emphasizes real-world applications across industries including supply chain optimization, financial market prediction, consumer behavior forecasting, and operational planning. Students will work with complex datasets featuring seasonal variations, trend analysis, and cyclical patterns while learning to handle data irregularities, missing values, and external shock events. The course integrates machine learning approaches with traditional econometric methods, covering ARIMA modeling, exponential smoothing, ensemble forecasting methods, and neural network-based prediction systems. Through hands-on projects using Python and R, students will build comprehensive forecasting pipelines that include data preprocessing, model selection, validation techniques, and uncertainty quantification. Special emphasis is placed on forecast accuracy assessment, business impact measurement, and communicating predictive insights to stakeholders. By semester's end, students will possess the technical expertise and strategic thinking necessary to drive data-informed decision-making in dynamic business environments.

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this course, students will be able to:

1. **Master advanced time series decomposition techniques** and identify complex temporal patterns in multidimensional business data
2. **Apply ensemble forecasting methods and hybrid modeling approaches** to create robust predictive systems for strategic planning
3. **Develop expertise in forecast validation, uncertainty quantification**, and translating predictive analytics into actionable business recommendations

### Software
- Python 3.8+ with packages: pandas, numpy, scikit-learn, matplotlib, seaborn, statsmodels, plotly
- R with packages: forecast, tseries, ggplot2, dplyr, prophet
- Jupyter Notebook or RStudio (free)
- Access to university computing lab

### Hardware
- Laptop capable of running Python/R (minimum 8GB RAM recommended)

# Visual Storytelling with Complex Data: Advanced Techniques for Multi-Dimensional Analysis

**Course Code:** DATA 485  
**Credits:** 3  
**Prerequisites:** DATA 301 (Intermediate Data Analysis), STAT 342 (Statistical Computing), or equivalent  
**Meeting Time:** Tuesdays & Thursdays, 2:00-3:30 PM  
**Semester:** Spring 2024  

## Instructor Information

## Course Description
This advanced course explores the intersection of data science and visual communication, focusing on transforming complex, multi-dimensional datasets into compelling visual narratives. Students will master cutting-edge visualization techniques including interactive dashboards, animated time-series visualizations, network analysis graphics, and immersive data experiences using AR/VR technologies. The curriculum emphasizes advanced statistical visualization methods such as dimensionality reduction plots, uncertainty visualization, and comparative analysis frameworks. Students will work with real-world datasets from fields like genomics, social networks, financial markets, and climate science to create publication-quality visualizations and interactive web applications. The course combines theoretical foundations in human perception and cognitive load theory with hands-on practice using advanced tools like D3.js, Plotly, Tableau Public, and emerging visualization libraries. Projects culminate in developing comprehensive visual analysis portfolios that demonstrate the ability to extract actionable insights from complex data while effectively communicating findings to diverse stakeholders through sophisticated visual storytelling techniques.

## Learning Objectives
Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

1. **Advanced Technical Implementation:** Design and implement advanced interactive visualizations using D3.js, Plotly, and specialized libraries for complex data types including networks, geospatial, and temporal data

2. **Cognitive Design Principles:** Apply cognitive science principles and perceptual theory to create visualizations that optimize human comprehension and minimize cognitive load in multi-dimensional data exploration

3. **Visual Narrative Construction:** Develop expertise in visual narrative construction, creating compelling data stories that guide audiences through complex analytical findings using advanced animation, layering, and interactive techniques

## Weekly Schedule

### Week 1: Foundation - Data Exploration and Quality Assessment
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis and Data Visualization Fundamentals
- **Concepts:**
  - Data profiling - systematic examination of dataset structure, completeness, and quality metrics
  - Univariate analysis - statistical and visual exploration of individual variables including measures of central tendency, dispersion, and distribution shape
- **Activities:** Introduction to visualization tools and data quality assessment
- **Readings:** Chapter 1-2 of textbook

### Week 2: Statistical Foundation for Visualization
**Module:** Statistical Hypothesis Testing for Data-Driven Decision Making
- **Concepts:**
  - Null and Alternative Hypotheses - formal statements that define what the statistical test will evaluate
  - P-values and Statistical Significance - probability of observing results as extreme as those found, assuming null hypothesis is true
- **Activities:** Statistical testing for visualization decisions
- **Due:** Data Quality Assessment Discussion Post

### Week 3: Univariate and Distribution Analysis

# PREDICTIVE ANALYTICS IN BUSINESS: FROM DATA PATTERNS TO MARKET FORECASTS

**Course Code:** DATA 3350  
**Credits:** 3  
**Prerequisites:** Statistics I, Introduction to Data Analysis  
**Meeting Time:** Tuesdays & Thursdays, 2:00-3:30 PM  
**Semester:** Fall 2024  

## COURSE DESCRIPTION

This hands-on course transforms students into business forecasters by combining statistical modeling with real-world market scenarios. Students work exclusively with live datasets from retail, finance, and e-commerce sectors to predict sales trends, customer behavior, and market movements. The curriculum emphasizes practical forecasting techniques including time series analysis, regression modeling, and machine learning algorithms specifically tailored for business prediction challenges. Each week features case studies from companies like Amazon, Netflix, and financial institutions, where students replicate actual forecasting problems and present solutions to simulated executive teams. Students will master industry-standard tools including Python's forecasting libraries, Tableau for visualization, and Excel's advanced analytics functions. The course culminates in a capstone project where teams partner with local businesses to solve genuine forecasting challenges, from inventory management to demand planning. By semester's end, students will have built a professional portfolio of predictive models and gained experience presenting data-driven forecasts to stakeholders. This practical approach ensures graduates are immediately equipped to contribute to business intelligence teams and analytics departments across industries.

## LEARNING OBJECTIVES

Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

1. **Master time series forecasting techniques and seasonal decomposition methods for business applications**
2. **Apply regression analysis, ARIMA models, and machine learning algorithms to predict market trends and consumer behavior**
3. **Develop expertise in communicating forecasting results through executive dashboards and stakeholder presentations**

## REQUIRED MATERIALS

- **Textbook:** *Forecasting: Principles and Practice* by Hyndman & Athanasopoulos (free online)
- **Software:** Python (Anaconda distribution), Tableau Public, Microsoft Excel
- **Hardware:** Laptop capable of running data analysis software
- **Platform:** Course materials available on Learning Management System

## WEEKLY SCHEDULE

### Week 1: Introduction to Business Forecasting
**Topics:** Course overview, forecasting in business context, types of predictions
**Readings:** Chapter 1-2 of textbook

### Week 2: Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) for Pattern Discovery
**Concepts:**
- Data Profiling - Systematic examination of data quality, completeness, and structure to understand dataset characteristics
- Statistical Summaries - Measures of central tendency, dispersion, and distribution shape that describe data numerically

**Activity:** Design and Build a Customer Segmentation Dashboard for E-commerce Strategy (120 minutes)
**Case Study:** Netflix viewing pattern analysis

### Week 3: Data Visualization for Business Intelligence
**Topics:** Advanced visualization techniques, dashboard design principles
**Readings:** Chapter 3 of textbook

### Week 4: Time Series Components and Decomposition
**Topics:** Trend, seasonality, cyclical patterns, irregular components
**Readings:** Chapter 4-5 of textbook
**Case Study:** Amazon sales seasonality analysis

### Week 5: Simple Forecasting Methods
**Topics:** Naive methods, moving averages, exponential smoothing
**Readings:** Chapter 6-7 of textbook
**Activity:** Customer Segmentation Dashboard Creation from E-commerce Transaction Data (110 minutes)

### Week 6: Linear Regression for Forecasting
**Topics:** Simple and multiple regression, model diagnostics
**Readings:** Chapter 8 of textbook
**Case Study:** Financial market trend prediction

### Week 7: Advanced Regression Techniques
**Topics:** Polynomial regression, logistic regression for classification
**Readings:** Chapter 9 of textbook
**Activity:** Design and Build a Customer Churn Prediction Dashboard (210 minutes)

### Week 8: MIDTERM EXAMINATION WEEK
**Assessment:** Customer Churn Analysis and Prediction Project (100 points)

### Week 9: Time Series Regression Models
**Topics:** ARIMA methodology, model identification, estimation
**Readings:** Chapter 10-11 of textbook
**Case Study:** Retail inventory forecasting

### Week 10: Machine Learning for Prediction
**Topics:** Decision trees, random forests, neural networks
**Readings:** Supplemental materials
**Activity:** Design and Build a Predictive Sales Dashboard with Forecasting Model (210 minutes)

### Week 11: Model Evaluation and Selection
**Topics:** Cross-validation, performance metrics, model comparison
**Readings:** Chapter 12 of textbook

### Week 12: Advanced Forecasting Methods
**Topics:** State space models, dynamic regression
**Readings:** Chapter 13-14 of textbook
**Case Study:** Financial institution risk modeling

### Week 13: Capstone Project Work Session
**Topics:** Team consulting projects with local businesses
**Activity:** Design and Build a Customer Segmentation Dashboard for E-commerce Marketing Strategy (4.5 hours - distributed across week)

### Week 14: Communication and Presentation Skills
**Topics:** Executive reporting, data storytelling, visualization best practices
**Readings:** Supplemental materials
**Workshop:** Presentation skills for data analysts

### Week 15: Final Project Presentations
**Assessment:** Customer Behavior Data Analysis Presentation (100 points)
**Format:** 15-minute team presentations to simulated executive panels

### Week 16: FINAL EXAMINATION WEEK
**Assessment:** Comprehensive portfolio review and final examination

## ASSESSMENT PLAN

| Assessment Type | Description | Points | Weight | Due Date |
|----------------|-------------|---------|---------|----------|
| **Portfolio** | Real-World Data Analysis Portfolio: Customer Churn Investigation | 100 | 20% | Week 12 |
| **Discussion** | Data Quality Assessment and Cleaning Strategy Discussion | 100 | 20% | Ongoing |
| **Project** | Customer Churn Analysis and Prediction Project | 100 | 25% | Week 8 |
| **Lab Report** | Customer Churn Analysis Lab Report | 100 | 15% | Week 10 |
| **Presentation** | Customer Behavior Data Analysis Presentation | 100 | 20% | Week 15 |

**Total Points:** 500  
**Final Grade Scale:** A (90-100%), B (80-89%), C (70-79%), D (60-69%), F (<60%)

## DETAILED ASSESSMENT DESCRIPTIONS

### Portfolio (100 points, 20%)
Students will compile a comprehensive portfolio demonstrating mastery of forecasting techniques through the Real-World Data Analysis Portfolio: Customer Churn Investigation. This portfolio will include multiple forecasting models, model comparisons, and business recommendations.

### Discussion Participation (100 points, 20%)
Active engagement in Data Quality Assessment and Cleaning Strategy Discussions throughout the semester. Students will participate in weekly online discussions analyzing real business data quality issues and proposing solutions.

### Midterm Project (100 points, 25%)
The Customer Churn Analysis and Prediction Project requires students to work with actual customer data to build predictive models and provide business recommendations for customer retention strategies.

### Lab Report (100 points, 15%)
The Customer Churn Analysis Lab Report documents the technical methodology, results, and business implications of forecasting analyses conducted during laboratory sessions.

### Final Presentation (100 points, 20%)
The Customer Behavior Data Analysis Presentation showcases students' capstone projects, demonstrating their ability to communicate complex forecasting results to business stakeholders.

## COURSE POLICIES

### Software and Data Policy
All required software is freely available. Students are responsible for software installation and basic troubleshooting. Course datasets are for educational use only and may not be distributed outside the course.

### Professional Development
This course emphasizes professional skills development. Students are expected to:
- Maintain professional communication standards
- Meet project deadlines consistently
- Provide constructive peer feedback
- Present work with confidence and clarity

# Executive Dashboard Design and Narrative Analytics
**Course Code:** DATA 4850

## Course Description

This advanced course transforms students into strategic data storytellers who design compelling executive dashboards and craft data-driven narratives for C-suite decision making. Students master the art of translating complex analytical findings into actionable business intelligence through interactive visualizations, automated reporting systems, and persuasive data presentations. The curriculum emphasizes real-world consulting scenarios where students work with messy, multi-source datasets to create polished executive briefings, KPI monitoring systems, and strategic recommendation reports. Through partnerships with local businesses, students experience the full lifecycle of executive reporting: stakeholder interviews, requirement gathering, dashboard prototyping, user testing, and presentation delivery. Advanced topics include predictive analytics integration, mobile-responsive dashboard design, and cross-functional collaboration with non-technical executives. Students develop expertise in modern BI tools while building critical soft skills in client communication, project management, and business acumen essential for data science consulting roles.

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this course, students will be able to:

1. **Design and implement executive-level dashboards** that effectively communicate complex data insights to senior leadership and drive strategic decision-making
2. **Master advanced narrative techniques** for translating statistical analyses into compelling business stories with clear recommendations and actionable insights
3. **Develop professional consulting skills** including stakeholder management, requirements gathering, and client presentation delivery in real business environments

### Week 2: Data Profiling for Business Intelligence

### Week 3: Advanced Statistical Analysis for Executives

### Week 4: Relationship Analysis and Executive Insights

# COURSE SYLLABUS

## TEMPORAL INTELLIGENCE: PREDICTIVE ANALYTICS AND STRATEGIC FORECASTING SYSTEMS
**Course Code:** DATA 485  
**Credits:** 4  
**Prerequisites:** Statistics (STAT 301), Programming for Data Analysis (DATA 301), Database Systems (CS 320)  
**Meeting Time:** Tuesdays/Thursdays 2:00-3:50 PM  
**Semester:** Spring 2024  

---

## COURSE DESCRIPTION

This advanced course integrates cutting-edge forecasting methodologies with real-world strategic decision-making frameworks. Students explore sophisticated time series analysis, machine learning-based prediction models, and hybrid forecasting systems used by Fortune 500 companies and government agencies. The curriculum emphasizes ensemble forecasting techniques, uncertainty quantification, and the integration of external data streams (economic indicators, social media sentiment, satellite imagery) into predictive models. 

Students work with streaming data architectures, implement dynamic model updating systems, and develop forecasting dashboards using cloud-based platforms. Special focus is placed on forecast accuracy evaluation, bias detection, and the communication of predictive insights to non-technical stakeholders. Case studies span multiple industries including supply chain optimization, financial risk assessment, energy demand planning, and epidemiological modeling. 

The course culminates in a capstone project where student teams partner with local organizations to solve real forecasting challenges, from conceptualization through deployment and monitoring. Graduates emerge with expertise in both the technical aspects of advanced forecasting and the business acumen to translate predictions into actionable strategic recommendations.

---

## LEARNING OBJECTIVES

Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

1. **Design and implement ensemble forecasting systems** that combine multiple prediction algorithms to optimize accuracy across diverse temporal patterns
2. **Integrate heterogeneous data sources** (structured, unstructured, streaming) into unified forecasting frameworks and evaluate their predictive value
3. **Develop automated model selection and hyperparameter tuning pipelines** for time-varying forecasting environments
4. **Construct uncertainty quantification frameworks** that provide confidence intervals and risk assessments alongside point forecasts
5. **Create interactive forecasting dashboards and visualization tools** that effectively communicate predictive insights to business stakeholders

---

## REQUIRED MATERIALS

### Software & Platforms
- Python 3.8+ with libraries: pandas, scikit-learn, statsmodels, plotly, streamlit
- R with forecast, tidyverse, and prophet packages
- Access to cloud platforms (AWS/Google Cloud credits provided)
- Jupyter Notebooks or RStudio

### Hardware
- Laptop capable of running data analysis software
- Minimum 8GB RAM recommended

---

**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) and Data Visualization Fundamentals
- **Tuesday:** Course introduction, temporal data characteristics
- **Thursday:** Time series EDA techniques and pattern recognition
- **Key Concepts:**
  - Univariate analysis for temporal data - examining time-dependent variables through trend, seasonality, and cyclical pattern identification
  - Bivariate analysis - exploring relationships between temporal variables using lag correlation, cross-correlation, and time-aligned visualizations
- 
### Week 2: Time Series Decomposition and Preprocessing

- **Thursday:** Advanced preprocessing: detrending, deseasonalization, differencing
- **Activity:** Build exploratory time series analysis toolkit

### Week 3: Univariate Forecasting Models I
- **Tuesday:** Moving averages and exponential smoothing
- **Thursday:** ARIMA models and parameter selection
- **Assessment:** Customer Segmentation Analysis Quiz (adapted for time series patterns)

### Week 4: Univariate Forecasting Models II
- **Tuesday:** State space models and Holt-Winters
- **Thursday:** Prophet and structural time series models
- **Activity:** Compare forecasting methods on economic data

### Week 5: Machine Learning for Time Series
- **Tuesday:** Feature engineering for temporal data
- **Thursday:** Regression-based forecasting and regularization
- **Discussion:** Data Quality Assessment and Cleaning Strategy Discussion

### Week 6: Advanced ML Approaches
- **Tuesday:** Random forests and gradient boosting for forecasting
- **Thursday:** Neural networks and LSTM introduction
- **Activity:** Design and Build a Customer Churn Prediction Dashboard (4 hours)

### Week 7: Ensemble Forecasting Methods
- **Tuesday:** Simple averaging and weighted combinations
- **Thursday:** Dynamic ensemble selection and stacking
- **Assessment:** E-commerce Customer Behavior Analysis Portfolio

### Week 8: Multivariate Forecasting
- **Tuesday:** Vector Autoregression (VAR) models
- **Thursday:** Cointegration and error correction models
- **Midterm Week**

### Week 9: External Data Integration
- **Tuesday:** Economic indicators and sentiment data
- **Thursday:** Satellite imagery and alternative data sources
- **Activity:** Design and Build a Predictive Dashboard for Local Business Performance (3.5 hours)

### Week 10: Streaming Data and Real-time Forecasting
- **Tuesday:** Streaming architectures and online learning
- **Thursday:** Dynamic model updating and concept drift
- **Case Study:** Financial market prediction systems

### Week 11: Uncertainty Quantification
- **Tuesday:** Prediction intervals and bootstrapping
- **Thursday:** Bayesian forecasting and MCMC methods
- **Assessment:** Customer Churn Analysis and Prediction Project

### Week 12: Forecast Evaluation and Bias Detection
- **Tuesday:** Accuracy metrics and cross-validation strategies
- **Thursday:** Bias identification and model diagnostics
- **Activity:** Design and Build a COVID-19 Impact Dashboard for Local Business Recovery (4 hours)

### Week 13: Industry Applications I
- **Tuesday:** Supply chain and demand forecasting
- **Thursday:** Energy and utilities forecasting
- **Case Study:** Amazon's demand forecasting system

### Week 14: Industry Applications II
- **Tuesday:** Financial risk and epidemiological modeling
- **Thursday:** Communication strategies for stakeholders
- **Assessment:** E-commerce Customer Behavior Analysis Lab Report

### Week 15: Capstone Project Presentations
- **Tuesday:** Team presentations (Groups 1-4)
- **Thursday:** Team presentations (Groups 5-8)

# Pattern Discovery in Complex Data Ecosystems

## Course Description

Students will master cutting-edge algorithms for discovering hidden structures in complex data ecosystems including social networks, temporal sequences, and multi-modal datasets. The curriculum emphasizes practical implementation of advanced mining algorithms such as frequent pattern mining, graph-based clustering, anomaly detection in streaming data, and ensemble methods for pattern recognition. Students will work with real-world datasets from domains like bioinformatics, financial markets, and IoT sensor networks. The course integrates theoretical foundations with hands-on experience using specialized mining frameworks and distributed computing platforms. # Forecasting the Future: Machine Learning Pipelines for Predictive Analytics

## Instructor Information

## Course Description

This comprehensive course transforms students into skilled practitioners of predictive modeling by combining statistical foundations with cutting-edge machine learning techniques. Students will master the complete predictive analytics pipeline—from raw data ingestion and feature engineering to model deployment and performance monitoring. The curriculum emphasizes real-world applications across diverse domains including finance, healthcare, marketing, and operations research. Students will work with time-series forecasting, classification algorithms, regression models, and ensemble methods while learning to handle messy, incomplete datasets. Advanced topics include automated machine learning (AutoML), model interpretability, bias detection, and ethical considerations in predictive systems. Through hands-on projects using Python, R, and cloud platforms, students will build end-to-end predictive solutions that can be deployed in production environments. The course culminates in a capstone project where teams develop a complete predictive analytics solution for a real client or organization, including business case development, technical implementation, and presentation to stakeholders.

## Learning Objectives

By the completion of this course, students will be able to:

1. **Pipeline Development:** Design and implement complete machine learning pipelines from data preprocessing through model deployment and monitoring
2. **Advanced Modeling:** Master advanced predictive modeling techniques including ensemble methods, time-series forecasting, and deep learning approaches for structured data
3. **Model Ethics & Interpretation:** Develop expertise in model evaluation, validation, and interpretation while addressing ethical considerations and bias in predictive systems
4. **Applied Problem Solving:** Apply predictive analytics to solve real-world business problems across multiple industries through hands-on project experience

## Course Description

This hands-on laboratory course transforms students into data storytellers who can craft compelling visual narratives from complex datasets. Students work exclusively in a collaborative lab environment, manipulating real-world datasets from journalism, healthcare, environmental science, and social media to create interactive dashboards, animated visualizations, and multimedia data stories. Students master industry-standard tools including Tableau, D3.js, Python visualization libraries, and emerging AR/VR data presentation platforms. # Bayesian Decision Analytics for Business Intelligence
**Course Code:** DATA 380  
**Credits:** 3  
**Prerequisites:** STAT 201 (Statistics) and DATA 201 (Introduction to Data Analysis)  
**Semester:** Spring 2024  
**Class Time:** MWF 10:00-10:50 AM  

## Instructor Information

## Course Description
This specialized course explores advanced Bayesian statistical methods applied to real-world business decision-making scenarios. Students will master probabilistic reasoning, prior belief updating, and uncertainty quantification in data-driven environments. The curriculum emphasizes practical implementation of Bayesian inference techniques including Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods, hierarchical modeling, and Bayesian A/B testing frameworks. Through industry case studies, students will analyze customer behavior patterns, optimize marketing campaigns, assess financial risks, and evaluate product performance using Bayesian paradigms. The course integrates modern computational tools including R/Stan and Python/PyMC for implementing complex Bayesian models. Students will develop expertise in communicating probabilistic results to stakeholders, constructing informative priors from domain knowledge, and designing robust decision frameworks under uncertainty. Emphasis is placed on comparing Bayesian approaches with frequentist methods, understanding when each paradigm is most appropriate, and interpreting credible intervals versus confidence intervals. By course completion, students will possess specialized skills in Bayesian data analysis that are increasingly valued in data science, consulting, and strategic analytics roles across various industries.

## Learning Objectives
Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

1. **Master Bayesian Inference Fundamentals:** Students will master Bayesian inference techniques including prior specification, likelihood construction, and posterior interpretation for business analytics applications

2. **Apply Advanced Bayesian Modeling:** Students will apply specialized Bayesian modeling approaches including hierarchical models, mixture models, and time-series analysis to solve complex organizational problems

3. **Develop Computational Expertise:** Students will develop practical expertise in MCMC sampling methods, model diagnostics, and computational Bayesian statistics using modern software frameworks

# COURSE SYLLABUS
**Temporal Forecasting and Risk Prediction Analytics**

---

## COURSE INFORMATION

**Course Code:** DATA 485  
**Credits:** 3  
**Prerequisites:** Statistical Analysis (STAT 320), Machine Learning Fundamentals (DATA 350), Programming in Python (CS 210)  
**Class Schedule:** MWF 10:00-10:50 AM  
**Laboratory:** Thursday 2:00-4:50 PM  
**Duration:** 16-week semester  

---

## COURSE DESCRIPTION

This advanced course focuses on building sophisticated predictive models for time-sensitive scenarios and risk assessment applications. Students will master cutting-edge techniques for forecasting temporal patterns, predicting market volatility, credit default risks, and operational failures across various industries. The curriculum emphasizes real-world implementation of ensemble methods, deep learning architectures for sequential data, and survival analysis techniques. Students will work with streaming data, handle concept drift, and develop early warning systems using advanced feature engineering and model validation strategies. Laboratory sessions involve hands-on experience with financial datasets, healthcare outcomes prediction, and supply chain forecasting. The course covers model interpretability, uncertainty quantification, and deployment considerations for high-stakes prediction systems. Students will complete a capstone project involving the development of a complete predictive analytics pipeline for a real client, incorporating model monitoring, automated retraining, and performance tracking. By course completion, students will possess industry-ready skills in temporal modeling, risk quantification, and the ability to architect robust predictive systems that perform reliably under changing conditions.

---

## LEARNING OBJECTIVES

By the end of this course, students will be able to:

• **Master advanced time series forecasting techniques** including LSTM networks, ARIMA-GARCH models, and transformer architectures for temporal prediction
• **Develop expertise in risk modeling methodologies** including survival analysis, credit scoring models, and operational risk prediction systems  
• **Implement end-to-end predictive analytics pipelines** with automated model monitoring, drift detection, and dynamic retraining capabilities

---

## REQUIRED MATERIALS

**Textbooks:**
- Hyndman, R.J. & Athanasopoulos, G. *Forecasting: Principles and Practice* (3rd ed.)
- Hastie, T., Tibshirani, R., & Friedman, J. *The Elements of Statistical Learning* (2nd ed.)

**Software:**
- Python 3.8+ with Jupyter Lab
- Required libraries: pandas, numpy, scikit-learn, tensorflow, pytorch, statsmodels, plotly
- Access to cloud computing platform (AWS/GCP credits provided)

**Hardware:**
- Laptop capable of running Python development environment
- Minimum 8GB RAM recommended

---

## WEEKLY SCHEDULE

### **Week 1: Foundation - Exploratory Data AnalysisModule:** Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) and Data Visualization Techniques  
**Key Concepts:**
- Data profiling: Systematic examination of data structure, completeness, consistency, and validity
- Distribution analysis: Statistical and visual assessment including measures of central tendency, spread, skewness, and outlier identification

### **Week 2: Time Series FundamentalsTopics:** 
- Time series components (trend, seasonality, cyclical, irregular)
- Stationarity testing and transformation techniques
- Autocorrelation and partial autocorrelation analysis

### **Week 3: Classical Forecasting MethodsTopics:**
- Moving averages and exponential smoothing
- Holt-Winters seasonal methods
- Model selection and parameter optimization

### **Week 4: ARIMA ModelsTopics:**
- Autoregressive (AR) and Moving Average (MA) models
- Box-Jenkins methodology for ARIMA modeling
- Model diagnostics and residual analysis

### **Week 5: Advanced Time Series ModelsTopics:**
- GARCH models for volatility forecasting
- Vector Autoregression (VAR) for multivariate series
- State space models and Kalman filtering

### **Week 6: Deep Learning for Sequential DataTopics:**
- Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) fundamentals
- Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks
- Gated Recurrent Units (GRU) and bidirectional architectures

### **Week 7: Transformer ArchitecturesTopics:**
- Attention mechanisms and self-attention
- Transformer models for temporal prediction
- Multi-head attention and positional encoding

### **Week 8: Risk Modeling FundamentalsTopics:**
- Types of risk (credit, market, operational)
- Probability of default models
- Loss given default and exposure at default

### **Week 9: Survival AnalysisTopics:**
- Survival functions and hazard rates
- Kaplan-Meier estimators
- Cox proportional hazards models

### **Week 10: Advanced Risk ModelsTopics:**
- Copula models for dependency modeling
- Value at Risk (VaR) and Expected Shortfall
- Stress testing and scenario analysis

### **Week 11: Ensemble MethodsTopics:**
- Random forests for time series
- Gradient boosting for temporal data
- Model stacking and blending strategies

### **Week 12: Streaming Data and Concept DriftTopics:**
- Online learning algorithms
- Concept drift detection methods
- Adaptive model updating strategies

### **Week 13: Model InterpretabilityTopics:**
- SHAP values for time series models
- Feature importance in temporal contexts
- Model explanation techniques

### **Week 14: Uncertainty QuantificationTopics:**
- Prediction intervals and confidence bounds
- Bayesian approaches to forecasting
- Monte Carlo methods for risk assessment

### **Week 15: Model Deployment and MonitoringTopics:**
- Production deployment considerations
- Model performance monitoring
- Automated retraining pipelines

# Predictive Analytics for Strategic Decision Making: Advanced Forecasting in Dynamic Environments

**Course Code:** DATA 4XX  
**Credits:** 3  
**Prerequisites:** Statistics, Intermediate Data Analysis, Programming (Python or R)  
**Meeting Time:** MWF 10:00-10:50 AM  

## Instructor Information

## Course Description

This advanced course examines sophisticated forecasting methodologies used in high-stakes strategic decision making across volatile industries. Students will master time series decomposition, multivariate forecasting models, and ensemble prediction techniques while working with real-world datasets from finance, supply chain, healthcare, and technology sectors. The curriculum emphasizes handling uncertainty, incorporating external shocks, and building robust predictive models that perform under changing market conditions. Students will learn advanced techniques including ARIMA-X models, Vector Autoregression (VAR), state-space models, and machine learning approaches for forecasting. Special attention is given to forecast evaluation, confidence intervals, scenario planning, and communicating predictive insights to executive stakeholders. The course integrates cutting-edge tools including R, Python, and specialized forecasting software while addressing ethical considerations in predictive modeling. Through case studies involving economic downturns, pandemic disruptions, and technological shifts, students develop the analytical judgment needed to create actionable forecasts that drive strategic planning. Final projects require students to develop comprehensive forecasting frameworks for complex organizational challenges, preparing them for senior analytical roles in consulting, finance, operations research, and strategic planning.

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this course, students will be able to:

1. **Design and implement advanced time series and multivariate forecasting models** for complex strategic decision-making scenarios
2. **Evaluate forecast accuracy** using sophisticated metrics and develop robust models that account for structural breaks and regime changes
3. **Synthesize multiple forecasting approaches** into ensemble models and effectively communicate predictive insights to executive decision-makers

### Software
- Python 3.8+ with pandas, scikit-learn, statsmodels, matplotlib, seaborn
- R with forecast, tseries, vars packages
- Access to course datasets via university portal

### Hardware
- Laptop capable of running statistical software
- Reliable internet connection for cloud computing resources

## Weekly Schedule

### Week 1: Foundations of Strategic Forecasting
**Module:** Exploratory Data Analysis and Data Visualization Fundamentals
- **Topics:** Course overview, strategic forecasting landscape, data exploration for time series
- **Concepts Covered:**
  - Univariate Analysis - Statistical examination of individual variables including measures of central tendency, dispersion, and distribution shape
  - Bivariate and Multivariate Analysis - Exploration of relationships between two or more variables using correlation, cross-tabulation, and scatter plot matrices
- **Activities:** Dataset familiarization, initial EDA on financial time series
- **Readings:** Hyndman Ch. 1-2

### Weeks 2-3: Time Series Decomposition and Pattern Recognition
- **Topics:** Trend analysis, seasonal decomposition, cyclical patterns, structural breaks
- - **Case Study:** Retail sales forecasting with seasonal adjustments

### Weeks 4-5: Univariate Time Series Models
- **Topics:** ARIMA models, model identification, parameter estimation, diagnostic checking
- **Advanced Topics:** ARIMA-X models, seasonal ARIMA, handling non-stationarity
- **Assessment:** Customer Churn Analysis Lab Report (Due Week 5)

### Weeks 6-7: Multivariate Forecasting Techniques
- **Topics:** Vector Autoregression (VAR), cointegration, Granger causality
- **Applications:** Economic indicator forecasting, supply chain demand planning
- **Activity:** Design a Predictive Analytics Dashboard for Local Business Decision-Making (150 minutes)

### Weeks 8-9: State-Space Models and Advanced Methods
- **Topics:** Kalman filtering, dynamic linear models, unobserved components
- **Applications:** Real-time forecasting, handling missing data
- **Assessment:** Data Quality Assessment and Cleaning Strategy Discussion (Due Week 9)

### Week 10: Spring Break - No Classes

### Weeks 11-12: Machine Learning for Forecasting
- **Topics:** Neural networks for time series, ensemble methods, feature engineering
- **Advanced Topics:** LSTM networks, hybrid models, cross-validation for time series
- **Activity:** Design and Build a Customer Churn Prediction Dashboard with Actionable Insights (180 minutes)

### Weeks 13-14: Forecast Evaluation and Uncertainty Quantification
- **Topics:** Accuracy metrics, prediction intervals, scenario analysis, stress testing
- **Applications:** Model comparison, forecast combination, dealing with regime changes
- **Assessment:** Customer Behavior Data Analysis Presentation (Week 14)

### Weeks 15-16: Strategic Communication and Implementation
- **Topics:** Executive dashboards, forecast communication, implementation challenges
- **Capstone:** Final project presentations and peer review
- **Assessment:** Customer Churn Analysis and Prediction Project (Due Week 16)

## Assessment Plan

| Assessment | Type | Points | Due Date | Weight |
|------------|------|--------|----------|---------|
| Customer Churn Analysis Lab Report | Lab Report | 100 | Week 5 | 15% |
| Data Quality Assessment and Cleaning Strategy Discussion | Discussion | 100 | Week 9 | 15% |
| Customer Behavior Data Analysis Presentation | Presentation | 100 | Week 14 | 20% |
| Customer Churn Analysis and Prediction Project | Final Project | 100 | Week 16 | 25% |
| Real-World Data Analysis Portfolio | Portfolio | 100 | Ongoing | 15% |
| Participation and Lab Activities | Participation | 100 | Ongoing | 10% |

**Total Points:** 600

### Assessment Descriptions

**Real-World Data Analysis Portfolio (15%):** Ongoing collection of mini-analyses, code samples, and reflections on forecasting challenges encountered throughout the semester.

**Data Quality Assessment Discussion (15%):** Structured online discussion analyzing data quality issues in provided datasets and proposing cleaning strategies with justification.

**Customer Behavior Presentation (20%):** 15-minute presentation analyzing customer behavior patterns using advanced forecasting techniques, with emphasis on strategic insights.

**Final Project (25%):** Comprehensive forecasting framework addressing a complex organizational challenge, including model development, evaluation, and executive summary.

### Late Assignment Policy
- Late submissions: -10% per day for first 3 days
- After 3 days: -50% penalty
- After 1 week: Assignment may not be accepted
- Extensions granted for documented emergencies

### Collaboration Guidelines
- Study groups encouraged for concept discussion
- Lab activities may involve pair programming when specified
- Final project is individual work only
- Seek clarification when unsure about collaboration boundaries

### Professional Development
This course prepares students for careers in:
- Strategic consulting
- Financial analysis and risk management
- Operations research and supply chain analytics
- Healthcare analytics
- Technology sector forecasting
- Government policy analysis

Students are encouraged to connect course projects with career interests and consider internship opportunities in these fields.

# Project Blueprint Laboratory: Advanced Planning Simulation and Prototyping

## COURSE INFORMATION

**Course Code:** PM 3850  
**Credits:** 4 credit hours  
**Prerequisites:** PM 2100 (Introduction to Project Management), PM 2200 (Project Planning Fundamentals)  
**Meeting Schedule:** Tuesdays and Thursdays, 2:00-4:50 PM  
**Semester:** Fall 2024  

## COURSE DESCRIPTION

This intensive laboratory course immerses students in the critical planning phase of project management through hands-on simulation environments and rapid prototyping methodologies. Students work in teams to develop comprehensive project blueprints for real-world scenarios across multiple industries, utilizing cutting-edge planning software, physical modeling tools, and digital simulation platforms. The laboratory setting emphasizes iterative planning processes, where students construct, test, and refine project plans through controlled experiments and scenario-based challenges. Each week features different planning laboratories focusing on scope definition, resource allocation modeling, risk assessment simulations, and timeline optimization using both traditional and agile planning frameworks. Students engage with industry mentors, utilize professional-grade project planning software suites, and create tangible planning artifacts including 3D project models, interactive Gantt charts, and stakeholder engagement prototypes. The course culminates in a capstone planning portfolio where teams present fully-developed project blueprints complete with contingency plans, resource models, and implementation roadmaps.

## LEARNING OBJECTIVES

Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

1. **Design and Prototype:** Students will design and prototype comprehensive project plans using advanced planning software and physical modeling techniques in laboratory settings
2. **Analyze and Optimize:** Students will analyze and optimize project planning scenarios through controlled experimentation and iterative testing methodologies
3. **Synthesize and Integrate:** Students will synthesize multiple planning frameworks to create integrated project blueprints that address scope, time, cost, and risk management challenges

### Week 2: Project Scope Definition and Requirements Modeling

- **Activity:** Advanced Project Management Framework Component Identification Challenge (50 min)
- **Deliverables:** Team scope definition prototype

### Week 3: Work Breakdown Structure Design Laboratory

- **Lab Focus:** Interactive WBS creation and testing
- **Activity:** Advanced Project Management Methodology Flashcard Marathon (60 min)
- **Deliverables:** 3D WBS model construction

### Week 4: Schedule Development and Critical Path Analysis
- **Topics:** Network diagrams, critical path methodology
- **Lab Focus:** Timeline optimization simulation
- **Activity:** Critical Path Method (CPM) Formula and Calculation Sequence Recall Challenge (70 min)
- **Deliverables:** Interactive Gantt chart prototype

### Week 5: Resource Allocation and Capacity Planning

- **Lab Focus:** Resource optimization laboratory
- **Activity:** Critical Path Method (CPM) Formula Components Flashcard Marathon (45 min)
- **Deliverables:** Resource allocation model

### Week 6: Cost Estimation and Budget Development
- **Topics:** Estimation techniques, budget modeling, cost baselines
- **Lab Focus:** Financial planning simulation environment
- **Activity:** PRINCE2 Process Model Component Identification Challenge (70 min)
- **Deliverables:** Comprehensive budget prototype

### Week 7: Quality Planning and Standards Integration
- **Topics:** Quality metrics, standards compliance, testing protocols
- **Lab Focus:** Quality assurance planning laboratory
- **Activity:** Critical Path Method (CPM) Formula Components Identification Challenge (60 min)
- **Deliverables:** Quality management plan

### Week 8: Risk Management in Project Planning and Execution
- **Topics:** Risk Register, Probability-Impact Matrix
- **Key Concepts:**
  - Risk Register: A comprehensive document that captures identified risks, their characteristics, assessment results, and planned responses throughout the project lifecycle
  - Probability-Impact Matrix: A qualitative risk analysis tool that plots risks based on their likelihood of occurrence and potential impact on project objectives
- **Lab Focus:** Risk simulation and scenario modeling
- **Activity:** Critical Path Method (CPM) Terminology and Calculation Formula Memorization Challenge (80 min)
- **Deliverables:** Risk assessment prototype
- **Assessment Due:** Comprehensive Project Risk Management and Recovery Analysis Lab Report (100 points)

### Week 9: Communication and Stakeholder Engagement Planning

- **Lab Focus:** Stakeholder engagement prototype development
- **Activity:** Critical Path Method (CPM) Formula Components Recall Challenge (60 min)

- **Lab Focus:** Agile planning tool integration
- **Activity:** Critical Path Dependencies Matrix: Memorizing Sequential Task Relationships (75 min)
- **Deliverables:** Hybrid planning framework model

### Week 11: Procurement and Vendor Management Planning
- **Topics:** Make-or-buy analysis, vendor selection, contract planning

- **Assessment Due:** Complex Multi-Phase Project Recovery Case Study Presentation (100 points)

- **Assessment Due:** Complex Project Crisis Management and Recovery Simulation (100 points)

- **Lab Focus:** Final portfolio assembly and refinement

- Primavera P6 Professional

## Course Description

This hands-on course equips students with comprehensive quality assurance frameworks essential for modern project management success. Key focus areas include developing quality management plans, designing inspection protocols, implementing corrective action procedures, and leveraging quality metrics for continuous improvement. The course integrates Lean Six Sigma principles, ISO quality standards, and agile quality practices to provide a comprehensive quality assurance toolkit. Through collaborative projects and peer reviews, students will experience the challenges and solutions of maintaining quality standards under budget and time constraints, preparing them for quality-focused roles in project management across various industries.
